We systematically investigate models that satisfy linear-level constraints, including the "extra power" parameter, galaxy cluster abundances, and high-redshift systems. Our findings indicate that mixed models with a spectral index less than 1 can accommodate up to 20% of non-cold component without violating linear constraints. Furthermore, models with a spectral index close to 1 can still allow for up to 10% of hot component. The implications of these models are discussed in the context of inflationary theories, and we note that they may alleviate the "baryon catastrophe" in galaxy clusters. Our results highlight the potential of mixed models to reconcile CMB and LSS data, and we outline the parameter space that remains viable under stringent linear constraints.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the internal mechanism behind the emergence of ubiquitous 1/f noise, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood. We investigate the distinction between internal system time and physical time as a potential source of 1/f noise. By extending a previously proposed point process model, we derive a stochastic differential equation that describes Brownian-like motion in internal time, paired with an equation relating internal to external time. Our results show that the signal intensity-dependent relationship between internal and physical time can generate 1/f noise across a broad frequency range. This model provides a framework for understanding the appearance of 1/f noise in various systems, offering insights into the underlying mechanisms driving this widespread phenomenon. The findings have implications for the study of stochastic processes, current fluctuations, and driven diffusive systems, shedding new light on the complex interactions between internal and external time scales.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We examine a harmonically confined mirror's response to an optical pulse in cavity optomechanics. A chirped pulse can significantly transfer thermal fluctuations to the cavity field. Frequency modulation enhances cooling by reducing detuning and pulse area dependence. Numerical investigations reveal that pulsed cooling is primarily limited by the cavity-field decay rate, highlighting a key constraint on this optomechanical cooling technique.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the deviation test, a fundamental tool in point process statistics, which assesses hypotheses by comparing empirical summary functions to their expected values under the null hypothesis. The test is crucial for addressing the multiple comparison problem that arises when considering functional differences across various distances. We deconstruct the test into three essential components: selecting a suitable summary function, transforming or scaling the differences, and calculating a global deviation measure. Our analysis focuses on both stationary and finite point processes, with particular emphasis on the random labelling hypothesis. Through toy examples and a simulation study, we demonstrate that the choice of summary function and transformation significantly impact the test's power. Our findings highlight the importance of careful consideration of these factors in deviation test construction, ultimately informing the development of more effective statistical methods for point process analysis. Key applications include marked point processes and Monte Carlo tests.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the near-surface tetragonal phase transition in SrTiO3 using beta-detected nuclear magnetic resonance and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction. The results reveal a distinct depth dependence of the phase transition on micron scales. Measurements support a model of tetragonal domain formation at temperatures above the bulk phase transition temperature, with preferential formation near the crystal's free surface. The research provides insight into tetragonal domain formation and its depth and lateral dependencies, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms governing this phenomenon in SrTiO3, with implications for understanding surface-induced phase transitions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the spectral properties of periodic ordinary differential operators on quantum graphs, focusing on the occurrence of spectral edges. Contrary to claims that spectral edges only occur at the spectra of periodic and antiperiodic boundary value problems in the case of single periodicity, we demonstrate that this property does not hold even in the simplest cases. Our analysis reveals that for a chain of finite graphs connected by single edges, spectral edges indeed coincide with periodic and antiperiodic spectra. However, when connections are formed by at least two edges, spectral edges can occur away from these spectra. This finding contradicts a commonly held assumption and highlights the complexity of spectral properties in multi-dimensional systems. Our results are dedicated to the memory of P. Duclos, and contribute to a deeper understanding of the behavior of periodic differential operators on quantum graphs.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the thermal properties of various knot configurations using Monte Carlo simulations, with a focus on preserving the topology of the knots during thermal fluctuations. A novel method is proposed, enabling rapid calculations for complex knots. The specific energy and heat capacity of the trefoil, figure-eight, and @xmath0 knots are calculated at different temperatures and lengths, assuming short-range repulsive monomer interactions. Knot configurations are generated on a 3D cubic lattice and sampled using the Wang-Landau algorithm and pivot method. The results reveal that topological effects significantly impact short-length polymers. Notably, three distinct temperature regimes are identified, characterized by varying growth rates of the system's internal energy. These findings highlight the importance of considering topological effects in understanding the thermal behavior of knotted polymers, with implications for the design and analysis of complex molecular systems. The results provide new insights into the thermodynamic properties of knotted polymers.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report the discovery of HAT-P-26b, a transiting extrasolar planet orbiting the moderately bright K1 dwarf star GSC 0320-01027. The planet has a period of 4.2345 days, transit epoch 2455205.0213 (BJD), and transit duration 0.1022 days. The host star has a mass of 1.12 ± 0.03 M⊙, radius of 1.32 ± 0.04 R⊙, effective temperature 5860 ± 50 K, and metallicity [Fe/H] = -0.04 ± 0.08. The planetary companion has a mass of 0.059 ± 0.007 MJ, and radius of 0.565 ± 0.072 RJ, yielding a mean density of 0.44 ± 0.09 g/cm³. HAT-P-26b is the fourth Neptune-mass transiting planet discovered to date, with a mass comparable to those of Neptune and Uranus, but a radius 64% larger than those of Neptune and Uranus. Theoretical models suggest that HAT-P-26b is an irradiated Neptune-mass planet with a heavy element core comprising 10% of its mass, surrounded by a significant hydrogen-helium envelope. The planet's unique characteristics make it an attractive target for follow-up observations, which can be easily conducted from both northern and southern ground-based facilities due to the star's equatorial declination. Further study of HAT-P-26b can provide valuable insights into the formation and composition of Neptune-mass planets, and contribute to our understanding of the diversity of exoplanetary systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: The NA48/2 experiment collected large decay samples in 2003-2004. Analysis of form factors and the cusp in ππ distribution yielded scattering lengths. This measurement tests chiral perturbation theory, providing precise branching fractions and form factors for key decays, surpassing previous experiments' data samples and contributing significantly to theoretical understanding.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a timing analysis of RXTE data from the accreting millisecond pulsar XTE J1751-305, observed during its April 2002 outburst. After correcting for Doppler effects caused by the source's orbital motion, a timing analysis of phase delays yielded an estimate of the average spin frequency derivative. This measurement enables the calculation of the torque resulting from the neutron star's spin-up, providing a dynamical estimate of the mass accretion rate. Comparison with the mass accretion rate derived from X-ray flux is also discussed. Additionally, constraints on the distance to the source are explored, resulting in a lower limit of 7 kpc. These findings contribute to our understanding of accreting millisecond pulsars and their properties. The results have implications for the study of neutron star magnetic fields and X-ray binaries.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the electronic transport properties of nanogranular metal composites, which exhibit two distinct regimes depending on the metallic phase concentration. At high metallic loadings, these composites behave as percolating systems, with a critical concentration threshold above which conductive particles form macroscopic clusters spanning the entire sample. Conversely, at lower loadings, the composites enter a dielectric regime, where current flows via hopping or tunneling between isolated nanoparticles. We demonstrate that both regimes can be described within a unified framework, treating percolation and hopping as equally important mechanisms. Using an effective medium approach, we accurately reproduce the concentration-dependent dc conductivity of various nanogranular metal films. By fitting published experimental data, we extract microscopic parameters governing percolation and tunneling, providing insight into the transport properties of these complex materials. Our findings offer a comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms controlling electronic transport in nanogranular metal composites, with implications for the design and optimization of these materials for various applications. The proposed approach enables the prediction of transport properties based on the microstructure and electrical connectedness of the composite, paving the way for further research and development in this field.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article reviews recent theoretical studies on the coalescence of compact binaries, comprising neutron stars or black holes, as promising sources of gravitational radiation detectable by upcoming laser interferometers. Analytic analyses of inspiral waveforms have been conducted using post-Newtonian approximations, while coalescence waveforms from binary neutron stars have been treated using Newtonian hydrodynamics and quadrupole radiation approximations. Numerical simulations of coalescing black hole and neutron star binaries are also being performed in full general relativity. The article summarizes recent results from these approaches, highlighting their strengths and limitations. By comparing and contrasting different methods, this review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of compact binary coalescence and its role in generating gravitational radiation, ultimately informing the development of detection strategies for laser interferometers. Key findings and implications are discussed.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the mechanism of fusion in cells and model membranes, focusing on stalk formation and hemifusion diaphragm expansion. Theoretical predictions are made regarding the initiation of hemifusion via stalk expansion and the dynamics of mesoscopic hemifusion diaphragm expansion. Recent experiments and theory suggest that hemifusion is driven by intra-membrane tension. Key predictions include a square root scaling of hemifusion zone size over time and an estimate of the minimal tension required for initiation. The findings indicate that while pressure is necessary for stalk formation, it is not required for expansion. Notably, tension-induced fusion requires significantly less energy than pressure-driven fusion, providing new insights into the fusion process.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We examine coherent population trapping (CPT) effects in atom interferometer gravimeters utilizing stimulated Raman transitions. CPT induces significant phase shifts, compromising measurement accuracy. However, the K-reversal technique mitigates this issue by averaging measurements with opposing Raman wavevector orientations, provided input internal states remain identical. This method ensures accurate inertial measurements, validating the technique's effectiveness in minimizing CPT-related errors in precision gravimetry applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present the results of a Chandra X-ray Observatory snapshot study of five nearby Herbig Ae/Be (HAeBe) stars kinematically linked to the Oph-Sco-Cen Association (OSCA). Our study, complemented by optical photometric and spectroscopic follow-up of the HD 104237 field, reveals a compact group of pre-main sequence (PMS) stars associated with HD 104237 and its codistant, comoving B9 neighbor. This group, named after its most massive member, comprises five confirmed stellar systems with a high degree of multiplicity, including a quintet system for HD 104237 with four low-mass PMS companions in non-hierarchical orbits. Notably, two low-mass members are actively accreting classical T Tauri stars. Our observations also expand the companion census for HD 141569 and HD 150193, and identify new OSCA members. We discuss our findings in the context of theoretical issues, including the origin of X-rays from HAeBe stars, the dynamical history of the HD 104237 system, and the formation of the observed group within turbulent giant molecular clouds. Our results, combined with those of the similar Cha cluster, provide insight into the structure and evolution of sparse stellar clusters dominated by intermediate-mass stars approximately 3 Myr after their formation, shedding light on the early stages of star cluster development.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a novel approach to typestate-oriented programming (TS-OOP) in a distributed setting, leveraging the actor model to enable concurrent access to objects by multiple processes. By modeling objects not only in terms of their interfaces but also their usage protocols, TS-OOP describes legal sequences of method calls that depend on the object's internal state. We demonstrate the feasibility of TS-OOP in a distributed context using Scala Akka, showcasing how Scala's abstractions support clean and natural typestate-oriented actor programming with asynchronous and non-blocking semantics. Furthermore, we illustrate how the standard type system of Scala, combined with a typed wrapping of Akka's `ActorRef`, provides robust type safety guarantees, ensuring that well-typed actors adhere to their intended communication protocols. Our approach is grounded in a solid theoretical foundation, building on a sound behavioral type system for the join calculus, a foundational calculus of distributed asynchronous processes. By bridging the gap between typestate-oriented programming and the actor model, this work enables the creation of more reliable, efficient, and scalable distributed systems, with a strong focus on type safety and protocol correctness. The examples and case studies presented in this article highlight the potential of this approach to improve the development of concurrent and distributed systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: We Use a Large, Multi-Color Mosaic of HST WFPC2 Images to Measure the Colors and Morphologies of 194 Spectroscopically Confirmed Members of the Rich Galaxy Cluster CL1358+62 at z~0

Abstract:

This study presents an analysis of the color-magnitude (CM) relation of 194 spectroscopically confirmed members of the rich galaxy cluster CL1358+62 at z~0, utilizing a large, multi-color mosaic of Hubble Space Telescope (HST) Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 (WFPC2) images. The dataset allows us to investigate the CM relation as a function of radius within the cluster, extending up to 4.6 arcmin from the center, equivalent to 1.6 Mpc. Our findings indicate that the intrinsic scatter in the rest-frame B-V CM relation of elliptical galaxies is remarkably small, at approximately 0.022 magnitudes. Moreover, the CM relation of ellipticals remains largely invariant with distance from the cluster center. In contrast, the CM relation for S0 galaxies exhibits a significant dependence on radius. While S0s in the core follow a CM relation similar to ellipticals, those at larger radii (>350 kpc) are systematically bluer, with the scatter in the CM relation increasing to approximately 0.043 magnitudes. This blueing of S0s at larger radii is statistically significant at the 4% confidence level. These results suggest that S0 galaxies in the outer regions of the cluster have undergone more recent star formation compared to those in the inner regions. A plausible explanation is that clusters at z~0 continue to accrete galaxies and groups from the field, with infall leading to the cessation of star formation. The homogeneity of the elliptical galaxy population implies that star formation in recently accreted ellipticals was terminated prior to accretion. We have developed models to explore the constraints imposed by these observations on the star formation history of cluster galaxies. Our analysis reveals that the scatter in the luminosity-weighted age is tightly constrained, with an upper limit of 18% for ellipticals and S0s in the cluster core, and 35% for S0s in the outer regions. Furthermore, our models suggest that star formation in ellipticals likely ceased at z~6 or higher. Assuming a constant star formation rate up to a randomly distributed truncation time, we find that S0s in the outer parts of the cluster have experienced star formation until the epoch of observation at z~0. Our study concludes that the population of S0s in clusters is likely to evolve as star-forming galaxies are converted into passively evolving galaxies. Under the assumption of a constant accretion rate after z~0, we estimate that approximately 15% of the present-day early-type galaxy population in rich clusters was accreted between z~0 and z~0.7. The ellipticals, and the brightest S0s, are likely a more stable population, at least since z~6. These findings provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of galaxies in rich clusters, highlighting the complex interplay between galaxy interactions, star formation, and environmental factors.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Here is an abstract of approximately 115 words:

We investigate a radiative neutrino model featuring a SU(2) septet scalar with hypercharge. Active neutrino mass is generated at the one-loop level, and mass matrices are derived from a calculated one-loop diagram. Lepton flavor violations, the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, and flavor-violating Higgs decay are analyzed. Our setup yields sizable muon and related parameters. The collider signature of the septet is discussed, focusing on quadratically charged scalar searches at the LHC (14 TeV). We find that it could be discovered up to 5 TeV mass by searching for multi-charged lepton signal events, offering a promising avenue for experimental detection.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: The Limitations of Constraining Grain Optical Properties through Reflection Nebulae Observations

Abstract:

The optical properties of interstellar grains remain poorly constrained by observations of reflection nebulae, despite their importance in understanding the interstellar medium. To investigate this, we employed radiation transfer models to simulate the interaction between a central star and a hierarchically clumped dust distribution within a spherical shell. Our models incorporate realistic power spectra of projected density distributions and account for the random distribution of dust clumps. The input parameters, including albedo, phase parameter, and radial optical depth, are varied to produce outputs of stellar extinction, optical depth, and scattered flux as viewed from multiple angles.

Our results show that the hierarchical geometry of the dust distribution significantly impacts the scattered flux emerging from the nebula, leading to a large spread in both scattered fluxes and stellar extinctions for any given dust distribution. Consequently, observed extinction and scattered flux can be fitted by a wide range of albedos, making it challenging to determine precise optical constants. While lower limits on albedo can be established, the same observations can be reproduced with varying albedo and phase parameter values. The wavelength-dependent opacity of the clumps introduces an additional complexity, as the effective geometry changes with wavelength.

Our findings have significant implications for the interpretation of multiwavelength observations of reflection nebulae. The determination of relative optical constants from such observations is not entirely reliable, even with a detailed understanding of the dust distribution. Furthermore, our results suggest that previous recipes for estimating scattered flux, such as that proposed by Henry (2002), may overestimate the amount of scattering and lead to underestimates of grain albedos. Our study highlights the need for more sophisticated models and a reevaluation of the assumptions underlying the interpretation of reflection nebulae observations. By acknowledging the limitations of current methods, we can work towards developing more accurate and robust techniques for constraining the optical properties of interstellar grains.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the concept of Symbiotic Cognitive Relaying (SCR) in a dynamic environment, where Secondary User (SU) nodes are mobile and Primary User (PU) nodes remain stationary. In this SCR scenario, mobile SU nodes act as multihop relays to facilitate communication between PU nodes when the direct link is weak. As an incentive, SU nodes are granted access to the licensed PU band for a fixed time period, known as the "time incentive," to conduct SU-SU communication. By introducing mobility to the traditional SCR framework, this paper derives theoretical bounds on throughput and delay for PU-PU transmission. Using a specific mobility pattern and routing strategy, we analytically determine the minimum achievable throughput and maximum delay in our model, shedding light on the performance limits of mobile SCR networks and providing insights for future network design and optimization.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a novel simulation technique to model the growth of a massive supercluster progenitor from redshift 0 to the present day, with its mass increasing from approximately 10^12 solar masses to its current value. Utilizing a nested sequence of high-resolution N-body resimulations, we investigate the structural evolution of both the dark matter object and its surrounding environment. Our simulation achieves optimal resolution at redshifts 4, 2, 1, 0.5, and 0, corresponding to object masses of 10^13, 10^14, 10^15, 10^16, and 10^17 solar masses, respectively. The simulation contains approximately 10^7 particles within the object's virial radius, enabling a detailed analysis of its internal structure. We find that extended Press-Schechter theory accurately predicts the rapid growth and overabundance of massive halos in the object's surroundings at early times. Furthermore, our results suggest that molecular hydrogen cooling could initiate as early as redshift 10, while atomic hydrogen cooling becomes effective at redshift 6. The formation of the first stars in halos with virial temperatures above 10^4 K could occur at redshift 12, with an abundance similar to that of dwarf galaxies today. This research provides new insights into the early universe and the formation of supercluster regions, shedding light on the complex interplay between dark matter, gas, and star formation in the most massive structures of the universe.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study proposes an innovative thermoelectric cooling device based on an atomic-sized junction, leveraging first-principles approaches to examine its working conditions and coefficient of performance (COP). The investigation accounts for phonon thermal current and local heating effects in an atomic-scale electronic refrigerator. Results show that the device's functioning is limited to a narrow range of driving voltages. Notably, the atomic refrigerator exhibits higher efficiency compared to bulk thermoelectric systems, attributed to suppressed local heating via quasi-ballistic electron transport and minimal driving voltages. The quantum nature of the device, enabled by atomic-level control, facilitates enhanced electron cooling beyond conventional thermoelectric device theory expectations, offering a promising approach for efficient cooling at the nanoscale. This breakthrough has significant implications for the development of high-performance thermoelectric devices.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study determines the upper critical temperature for the phase transition between the cholesteric and twist grain boundary C phases in thermotropic liquid crystals using the mean field Chen-Lubensky approach. The results show a split phase transition, with either the @xmath3 or novel @xmath4 phase emerging in a narrow temperature interval. The @xmath4 phase is unique, consisting of two superposed degenerate phases with different layer inclinations, providing new insights into liquid crystal phase behavior and transitions, with implications for understanding complex liquid crystal structures and properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a mean-field formulation of the thermodynamics of ion solvation in immiscible polar binary mixtures. We consider an equilibrium planar interface between two semi-infinite regions of different constant dielectric media, examining the electrostatic phenomenon of differential ion adsorption. Using thermodynamic principles, we construct the mean-field potential and demonstrate the spontaneous formation of an electric double-layer around the interface. Our framework relates bulk ion densities and distribution potential to the Born free energy of ion polarization. We illustrate selective ion adsorption in examples of fully permeable membranes with neutral, negative, or positive charge polarity, providing insights into the underlying mechanisms of ion solvation and adsorption in polar binary mixtures. The results have implications for understanding electrochemical phenomena at interfaces.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article discusses the ongoing research on weakly interacting slim particles (WISPs) as potential candidates for light cold dark matter. QCD axions and axion-like particles with masses between 0.1 eV and 100 MeV, along with hidden photons, are considered strong contenders. The WISP Dark Matter Experiment (WISPDMX) and novel radiometry approaches are introduced. Initial results and future prospects for these experiments are presented, highlighting the potential for groundbreaking discoveries in the field of dark matter research and the ongoing efforts to detect WISPs using innovative methods and large-scale experiments. New initiatives are underway.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a novel proof and extension of the classical divergence theorem, applicable to a wide range of domains in n-space, including smooth manifolds, soap bubbles, and fractals. Replacing traditional requirements with a limit of m-dimensional polyhedral chains, we introduce the concept of "chainlets" as a large class of n-dimensional domains of integration. Utilizing the operator, a geometric dual to the Hodge star operator, we establish the Star Theorem. When combined with the General Stokes Theorem, this result yields concise and optimal forms of the Gauss Divergence Theorem and Green's Curl Theorem. Our approach provides a unified framework for applying these fundamental theorems to diverse domains, enhancing the understanding of vector analysis and its applications. The findings have significant implications for various fields, including mathematics, physics, and engineering.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study introduces a novel first-principles computational approach to investigate the ballistic transport properties of one-dimensional nanostructures exhibiting non-collinear magnetic order. By combining density functional theory with the full-potential linearized augmented plane-wave method and non-collinear Wannier functions, we develop a tight-binding like transport Hamiltonian. The conductance is calculated using the Landauer formula and Green's function method. As a proof of concept, we examine the conductance between two ferromagnetic Co monowires terminated by single Mn apex atoms as a function of Mn-Mn separation, varying from contact to tunneling regimes. The magnetization direction of the Co electrodes is aligned in either parallel or antiparallel configurations, and different spin configurations of the Mn spins are considered. Our results show that the conductance is dominated by specific states in the tunneling and contact regimes. Notably, in the close contact regime, an additional contribution arises for parallel magnetization alignment, leading to an increase in magnetoresistance. Upon allowing the Mn spins to relax, a non-collinear spin state forms near contact due to competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic couplings. This transition leaves a distinct signature in the distance-dependent conductance and magnetoresistance of the junction. We attribute the effect of the non-collinear spin state on conductance to spin-dependent hybridization between Mn states and their coupling to the Co electrodes. Our findings demonstrate the significance of considering non-collinear magnetic order in understanding the transport properties of nanostructures, and provide a foundation for further exploration of complex magnetic phenomena in low-dimensional systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study utilizes the Gran Sasso laboratory to investigate atmospheric neutrino flux, confirming neutrino oscillation with maximal mixing. Measurements across energy samples show agreement, supporting the phenomenon. Additionally, a search for astrophysical neutrino sources is presented, contributing to our understanding of neutrino properties and behaviors.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: We Consider the Effect of Gluon Radiation on the Energy of Top/Antitop Quarks and on the Anticollinearity of Top-Antitop Quark Pairs Produced in e+e- Annihilation

Abstract:
This article investigates the influence of gluon radiation on the energy of top/antitop quarks and the anticollinearity of top-antitop quark pairs produced in e+e- annihilation. Our analysis presents results in terms of the dependence of the differential cross section on the cosine of the opening angle between top and antitop quarks for a center-of-mass energy of 500 GeV. We calculate mean values for the top quark's energy as well as its longitudinal and transverse projections, and for the deviation of the top-antitop quark pair from the anticollinearity limits. At a center-of-mass energy of 500 GeV, we find that gluon radiation causes a total average energy loss of 10.2% of the top quark's energy, with an average energy loss in the longitudinal direction of 12.1% and an average energy gain in the transverse direction of 5.5%. These percentage figures increase to 15.6%, 18.2%, and 8.1%, respectively, at 1 TeV. Furthermore, our results indicate that the mean transverse momentum of the top quark remains close to the mean total momentum of the gluon in the energy range from threshold to 1 TeV, suggesting a large mean transverse component of the gluon momentum. Our findings provide insight into the effects of gluon radiation on top-antitop quark pair production, shedding light on the underlying dynamics of these processes. The study's results have implications for our understanding of the properties of top quarks and the behavior of gluons in high-energy collisions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We investigated underdoped Bi2212 crystals with doping levels @xmath0, @xmath1, and @xmath2 using STM/STS measurements. The nondispersive @xmath3 charge order emerges within the pairing gap, with low doping favoring its formation. Our findings suggest the charge order may be dynamical and pinned by effective pinning centers. This pinned order is linked to the spatially inhomogeneous pairing gap structure, commonly observed in high-@xmath5 cuprates. The results provide insight into the interplay between charge order and superconductivity, shedding light on the complex behavior of underdoped cuprates at @xmath4.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the implications of recently measured large clustering lengths of quasars at a redshift of approximately 0 on the relationship between quasar luminosity and dark matter halo mass. By incorporating the observed quasar luminosity function and accounting for non-linearity, finite scatter, and luminosity-dependent quasar lifetime, our analysis reveals that the observed clustering and luminosity function can only be reconciled if two conditions are met. Firstly, the luminosity to halo mass ratio must increase with halo mass, and secondly, the observed clustering amplitude must exceed that expected solely from halo bias, with the latter result being statistically significant at the 99% level. These findings provide strong evidence for merger-driven quasar activity, where black hole growth is limited by feedback. Notably, our results indicate that there can be significant scatter in the luminosity-halo mass relation, up to 1 dex, and that quasar clustering is not a reliable indicator of quasar lifetime. This research offers new insights into the complex relationship between quasar properties and their host dark matter halos, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms driving quasar activity and galaxy evolution. Our findings have significant implications for cosmology and the study of large-scale structure.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Abstract:

Blazars are known to exhibit flares across the entire electromagnetic spectrum, with many gamma-ray flares being highly correlated with optical wavelength flares. However, a subset of "orphan" gamma-ray flares appears to occur in isolation, with minimal variability detected at longer wavelengths, challenging current models of blazar variability. To explain these events, we present numerical calculations of time-variable emission from a blazar based on a proposed model. In this model, a relativistic plasmoid propagates along the blazar jet, passing through a synchrotron-emitting ring of electrons in the jet sheath, which supplies seed photons for inverse-Compton scattering. Our model incorporates radiative cooling, spatially varying magnetic fields, and bulk velocity acceleration. We compare synthetic light curves to observed light curves from an orphan flare in the blazar PKS 1510-089, which coincided with the passage of a superluminal knot through the inner jet. Additionally, Very Long Baseline Array polarimetric observations support the existence of a jet sheath in PKS 1510-089, lending credibility to our model. We estimate the bolometric luminosity of the sheath, finding it to be a significant source of seed photons. Our results provide new insights into the mechanisms driving blazar variability and highlight the importance of considering the role of the jet sheath in shaping the observed emission. By reproducing the characteristics of orphan gamma-ray flares, our model offers a plausible explanation for these enigmatic events, advancing our understanding of blazar physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores theoretical approaches to nonlinear optical spectroscopy of molecular junctions. We derive optical response functions, facilitating Green function techniques, and express them using pseudoparticle nonequilibrium Green functions. Our formulation accounts for intra-molecular interactions and hybridization, enabling analysis of two-dimensional optical spectroscopy in junctions, providing new insights into molecular dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study derives an expression for the reduced density matrices of ideal Bose and Fermi gases in the canonical ensemble, analogous to the Bloch-De Dominicis theorem in the grand canonical ensemble. By applying this expression, we investigate one- and two-body correlations in homogeneous ideal gases. Notably, the pair distribution function of fermions exhibits antibunching due to the Pauli exclusion principle at all temperatures. In contrast, the pair distribution function of bosons displays bunching, corresponding to the Hanbury Brown-Twiss effect. For bosons below the Bose-Einstein condensation temperature, an off-diagonal long-range order emerges in the one-particle density matrix, and the pair correlation decreases. Our results converge to those obtained in the grand canonical ensemble, justifying the introduction of an "anomalous" average to remove unphysical particle-number fluctuations. This research provides insight into the behavior of ideal quantum gases and sheds light on the relationship between canonical and grand canonical ensembles in the thermodynamic limit. The derived expression and resulting correlations have implications for understanding quantum statistical phenomena and the role of symmetry in many-body systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the correlation between super-massive black hole (SMBH) mass and galaxy velocity dispersion, as well as the similar correlation for nuclear star clusters. Numerical simulations suggest that winds from the central massive object (CMO) drive gas out of classical bulge potential wells, influencing growth timescales. Smaller bulges tend to host nuclear star clusters, while larger ones contain SMBHs. Despite recent progress, feedback processes in bulge formation remain unclear. Our simulations highlight the importance of understanding CMO feeding and feedback mechanisms in shaping host galaxy evolution, providing new insights into galaxy formation dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the dynamics of a qubit encoded in the motional degrees of freedom of an ultra-cold ion in a trap, susceptible to decoherence from a finite-temperature bath. We identify a robust qubit encoding in two motional modes, resilient to zero or one quantum jump. In a zero-temperature bath, we propose a method to transfer quantum jump information to a measuring apparatus without significantly disturbing the ion's state. Furthermore, we describe a unitary restoration of the qubit using Raman processes induced by laser pulses, conditioned on the jump information. This approach enables the mitigation of decoherence effects, paving the way for enhanced coherence times in ion trap quantum computing. Our findings have implications for the development of robust quantum information processing protocols.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a mathematical examination of a massless quartic scalar field theory, characterized by a strong self-coupling, within the framework of classical conformal invariance. By utilizing a recently discovered set of classical solutions, we demonstrate the existence of an infinite array of infrared trivial scalar theories exhibiting a mass gap. Notably, the free particles in these theories possess a harmonic oscillator set of states superimposed upon them. We derive the classical solution via a current expansion and compute the next-to-leading order quantum correction. The implications of this theory for the Standard Model are profound, suggesting the presence of higher excited states of the Higgs particle and reduced decay rates to WW and ZZ, which may be detectable in current experiments, thereby potentially resolving the hierarchy problem and paving the way for Beyond the Standard Model physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines single top production with a Higgs boson in the @xmath0 extension of the Standard Model at the LHC. Production cross sections are calculated for @xmath1 processes. The observability of @xmath2 via @xmath3 is investigated, revealing improved systematic significance, yet detection remains challenging at the 14 TeV LHC with high luminosity.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a comprehensive radio study of the neutral hydrogen (HI) distribution in the direction of Stephan's Quintet, a compact group of galaxies, using the Very Large Array (VLA). Our spectral-line and continuum observations reveal a complex HI structure, comprising high-velocity clouds, a foreground galaxy disk, an extended continuum ridge, and faint dwarf-like galaxies. The observations, conducted with C, CS, and D arrays, confirm four previously detected HI clouds and provide new insights into their spatial distribution and kinematics. Notably, the largest HI features are coincident with tidal tails extending eastward from the group's center. Our findings suggest that the HI clouds are associated with star-forming activity, as indicated by luminous infrared and bright Hα sources. The total HI mass detected at high redshifts is substantial, while no emission is detected from high-redshift galaxies, implying that any remaining HI in their disks must be below our detection threshold. These results contribute to our understanding of the HI content and galaxy interactions within this unique compact group, shedding light on the role of gas in driving star formation and galaxy evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper proposes a novel approach to modeling music rhythm using L-systems, representing the structure as an automata and deriving its complexity. The complexity of the L-system is solved, enabling the measurement of similarity between trees. This complexity serves as a psychological complexity metric for rhythms, providing insights into music perception. The approach is applied to various compositions, including Mozart's K488, to demonstrate its effectiveness. The results have implications for understanding the cognitive processing of music and the notion of the "Mozart effect." This research contributes to the fields of music perception, psychological complexity, and rhythm analysis, offering a new perspective on the temporal associative memory of music.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: Revisiting the Period-Color Relation in W UMa Binaries: The Impact of Evolution and Metallicity

Abstract:
W UMa binaries exhibit a well-established period-color relation, where systems with more massive stars are bluer and have longer orbital periods. However, metal-poor W UMa binaries deviate from this relation, appearing too blue and having shorter orbital periods. While corrections for reduced line blanketing and smaller radii of Population II stars account for part of this discrepancy, the role of evolution remains unexplored. This study investigates the effect of evolution on the period-color plane for equal-mass W UMa binaries in critical contact with their inner Roche lobes. Our calculations yield metallicity-age dependent period-color relations that largely agree with empirical corrections over most periods. Nevertheless, our predictions diverge significantly at older stellar ages, as existing parameterizations neglect evolutionary effects. This research provides new insights into the period-color relation, highlighting the importance of considering evolution and metallicity in understanding W UMa binary properties. By refining our understanding of these systems, this study contributes to the development of more accurate models for binary star evolution and the interpretation of observational data. The findings have implications for the study of binary star populations and the calibration of stellar evolution models.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines decompositions of global constraints, yielding two key theoretical findings. Firstly, we demonstrate that global constraint propagators can be simulated by decompositions with equivalent time complexity but increased space complexity, suggesting space-saving benefits. Secondly, we show that range consistency can be enforced with the same worst-case time complexity as bound consistency. Our research also facilitates the encoding of decompositions as linear inequalities, enabling their integration into integer linear programs. These contributions advance our understanding of global constraints and their applications in optimization problems, with implications for efficient solution methods.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Abstract:

Theoretical models of Universal Extra Dimensions (UED) predict the existence of Kaluza-Klein (KK) excitations of Standard Model particles, potentially observable at TeV-scale colliders. A conserved discrete symmetry, KK-parity, ensures the stability of the Lightest KK Particle (LKP), a viable dark matter candidate if neutral. Recent studies have demonstrated that a certain LKP mass range can yield a relic density consistent with experimental observations, neglecting the impact of early-time KK graviton production. However, the decay of KK gravitons to LKPs can modify the relic density, depending on the reheating temperature. This article investigates the effects of KK graviton production on the relic density, revealing a significant modification of the allowed KK mass range. Furthermore, we derive a stringent upper limit on the reheating temperature as a function of the observed LKP mass, should evidence for UED be experimentally confirmed. Our results provide new insights into the phenomenology of UED models and their implications for dark matter and early universe cosmology, highlighting the importance of considering KK graviton production in relic density calculations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the penetration length of random walkers diffusing through a medium containing perfect or imperfect absorbers. Using a mean-field renormalization group approach, we derive solutions for lattice and continuum systems in various dimensions. For homogeneous systems, we find a power-law relationship between the penetration length and absorber density correlation length. We also investigate cases with long-range correlations and estimate the temporal decay of random walker density. Our results are validated through exactly solvable models and numerical simulations on directed percolation. The implications of our findings for diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) are discussed, and a novel method for measuring penetration length in DLA clusters is proposed. Our work provides new insights into the behavior of random walkers in complex media, with potential applications in understanding DLA and related phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines a non-equilibrium exclusion process where particle creation and annihilation occur in pairs, with asymmetric hopping rates @xmath0 and @xmath1 to the right and left, respectively. We derive exact expressions for the dynamics of a single particle, including entropy, entropy production rate, and entropy flux as functions of time. For a system of many particles, we obtain closed-form solutions for the probability distribution and entropy production rate when the dimer creation and annihilation rates sum to @xmath2. Without this constraint, we employ pair approximation to analyze the time-dependent behavior and determine stationary entropy production. Our results demonstrate that, in the stationary regime, the entropy production rate is a bilinear form in the particle current and force @xmath3, providing insights into the system's non-equilibrium dynamics and thermodynamic properties. This work contributes to the understanding of complex systems far from equilibrium.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present 21 cm observations of Arp 158, a disturbed system comprising optical knots, a linear structure, and a diffuse spray. Our study of neutral hydrogen (HI) reveals three kinematically separate systems. The optical morphology of Arp 158 bears resemblance to NGC 520, a mid-stage merger. Notably, our observations indicate a comparable HI content between Arp 158 and NGC 520. These similarities suggest that Arp 158 is an intermediate-stage merger, providing insights into the formation and evolution of this complex system. Our findings contribute to the understanding of galaxy mergers and their role in shaping galaxy evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We investigate the interface between two media separated by a 2D sheet, modeling the amplitude reflection coefficient by replacing the sheet with a thin film of finite thickness. A relationship between the 3D dielectric function of the film and the 2D dielectric function of the sheet is derived. Graphene and 2D metallic sheets serve as examples, demonstrating the approach's utility in treating non-planar structures, particularly those involving graphene-like sheets.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the implications of the K@xmath0rolyh@xmath0zy uncertainty relation on Minkowski spacetime, revealing a minimal detectable cell size due to energy-time uncertainty. The resulting energy density of metric fluctuations is derived as @xmath5. Inspired by this density, two novel dark energy models are proposed, characterized by the universe's age and conformal age, respectively. Our analysis shows that in both models, dark energy behaves similarly to a cosmological constant at late times. This research contributes to our understanding of dark energy, offering new insights into the universe's evolution. PACS: 95.36.+x, 98.80.cq, 98.80.-k. Keywords: K@xmath0rolyh@xmath0zy uncertainty relation, dark energy, energy-time uncertainty relation.

text: This study explores the novel properties of Dirac electrons in finite graphene samples subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field and an in-plane electric bias. Through numerical analysis of the Hofstadter spectrum and edge-type wave functions, we identify the emergence of "shortcut edge states" under the influence of the electric field. These states exhibit distinct spatial distributions, partially following the sample's perimeter, and display ridges connecting opposite sides of the graphene plaquette. Two types of shortcut edge states are found in different spectral regions, each with unique spatial localization and diamagnetic moments revealing their chirality. By simulating a four-lead Hall device, we investigate the transport properties and observe unconventional plateaus of the integer quantum Hall effect, associated with the presence of these states. The contributions of the novel states to the conductance matrix are examined, revealing their role in determining new transport properties. Notably, the shortcut edge states arising from the splitting of the n=0 Landau level give rise to non-trivial transverse and longitudinal resistance, highlighting the significance of these states in graphene-based systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article introduces ASpid, a comprehensive archive of spectral, photometric, and interferometric data, offering the world's largest collection of raw 3D spectroscopic observations. The ASpid-SR prototype archive provides heterogeneous science-ready data, utilizing the IVOA characterization data model. Multi-level characterization metadata is available for each dataset, enabling efficient querying and access to data model elements. The archive features powerful metadata query mechanisms and multiple access interfaces, including SIAP/SSAP, HTTP-based characterization metadata query, and web services accepting ADQL/X. This facilitates efficient scientific usage and exploration of the complex data repository.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: Identifying the electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave (GW) sources detected by upcoming networks of advanced ground-based interferometers is a daunting task due to the vast number of unrelated astrophysical transients within the large sky localizations. To mitigate this challenge, limiting detailed follow-up to candidates near galaxies within the GW sensitivity range of 200 Mpc for binary neutron star mergers is a potential strategy. However, the incompleteness of galaxy catalogs within this volume hinders the implementation of this approach. This study compares two methods for completing the local galaxy catalog: a narrow-band Hα imaging survey and an emission line radio survey. By utilizing Hα fluxes, stellar masses, and star formation rates from galaxies in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), combined with data from the GALEX Arecibo SDSS Survey and the Herschel Reference Survey, we estimate the completeness of these surveys. The results indicate that a Hα survey with a luminosity sensitivity of 10^40 erg s^-1 at 200 Mpc could achieve a completeness of 70% with respect to total star formation rate, but only 40% with respect to stellar mass. In contrast, an emission line radio survey with sensitivity similar to the proposed WALLABY survey on ASKAP could achieve higher completeness levels of 80% and 60%, respectively. Notably, both surveys are expected to achieve high completeness (>90%) with respect to the host galaxies of short-duration gamma-ray bursts, which may be associated with binary neutron star mergers. These findings have significant implications for the development of strategies to identify electromagnetic counterparts of GW sources and highlight the importance of completing the local galaxy catalog to maximize the scientific return of upcoming GW detections.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the application of semiclassical methods to quantum-field processes, focusing on non-trivial classical solutions and fluctuations. We calculate the one-loop effective action from a semiclassical perspective, aiming to derive an accurate expression for the decay rate of non-static metastable states. This approach provides non-perturbative insights into the theory, enabling the analysis of thermal and quantum fluctuations. The results have implications for finite-temperature field theory and the calculation of decay rates in various physical systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the transport properties of weakly interacting one-dimensional electron systems, considering both thermal equilibration via three-particle collisions and large-scale inhomogeneities. The interplay between interactions and inhomogeneities is shown to significantly impact the resistance of quantum wires. Notably, interactions can substantially increase wire resistance. Furthermore, the effects of interactions on thermoelectric properties are investigated, yielding calculations of thermal conductance, thermopower, and the Peltier coefficient. These findings provide insight into the complex behavior of inhomogeneous quantum wires, highlighting the importance of considering both interactions and inhomogeneities in transport property analyses.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We examine the Gromov width of spaces of polygons with specified edge lengths. For smooth polygon spaces, we derive an expression that yields the Gromov width, and establish it as a lower bound for all such spaces. Additionally, we prove that this expression gives the Gromov width when the space is symplectomorphic to a specific manifold, providing insight into geometric and symplectic properties of polygon spaces.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study derives novel generalized equations of motion for the Weber-Clebsch potentials, encapsulating both Navier-Stokes and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) dynamics. A new parameter is introduced, with dimensions of time for Navier-Stokes and inverse velocity for MHD. Direct numerical simulations (DNS) are conducted to validate the formalism. For Navier-Stokes, the generalized equations accurately capture vortex reconnection in the Boratav-Pelz-Zabusky flow, consistent with previous findings. In the MHD context, the new formalism is applied to detect magnetic reconnection in various flows, including the Arnold-Beltrami-Childress and Orszag-Tang vortex flows. The results reveal a correlation between magnetic enstrophy and reconnection events, characterized by frequent resettings. Furthermore, a positive correlation is observed between the sharpness of resetting frequency increases and the spatial localization of reconnection regions, providing new insights into MHD dynamics and reconnection processes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the chemo-hydrodynamic coupling between autocatalytic reaction fronts and forced hydrodynamic flow, leading to the formation of stationary fronts. We investigate the interaction between self-sustained chemical waves and opposed forced advection, which can result in static stationary fronts, known as frozen fronts. Using the autocatalytic iodate-arsenious acid reaction, experiments, analytical computations, and numerical simulations are performed around a solid disk over a range of flow velocities. The results show two types of frozen fronts: an upstream front that avoids the solid disk and a downstream front with symmetric branches emerging from the disk surface. The range of conditions under which these frozen fronts are observed is delineated. Additionally, the validity of the eikonal, thin front limit in describing the observed front shapes is assessed, providing insight into the selection of frozen front shapes. The findings have implications for understanding complex chemical wave dynamics in flowing systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report a potential detection of a lithium (Li I) line enhancement during an unusual, long-duration optical flare in the chromospherically active binary 2RE J0743+224. The Li I equivalent width variations closely follow the flare's temporal evolution, with a maximum enhancement of 40% occurring shortly after the peak chromospheric emission. A significant increase in the 6Li/7Li isotopic ratio is also observed. Notably, no simultaneous variations are detected in other photospheric lines, suggesting that line blends or starspots are not the primary cause of the Li I variation. Our findings imply that the Li I enhancement is likely produced by spallation reactions during the flare, providing insights into the flare's energetic particle acceleration and nuclear processes. This discovery has significant implications for our understanding of stellar flares and their impact on stellar surfaces.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a significant advancement in matrix multiplication algorithms, building upon the foundational work of Pagh and extending the research into deterministic approaches. We introduce a novel deterministic algorithm for approximating the product of real-valued, nonnegative matrices, which is particularly suited for applications in data mining. The algorithm offers a simple, space-efficient solution that operates in a single pass over the input matrices, providing approximations of individual entry weights and the entrywise 3-norm of the product matrix. With a user-defined parameter, the algorithm achieves a time complexity and space usage, while guaranteeing an additive error factor related to the entrywise 1-norm and the time required for sorting. Notably, our algorithm outperforms existing randomized algorithms for skewed matrix products, a common occurrence in real-world applications. Furthermore, we develop a deterministic group testing algorithm for detecting nonzero entries with large absolute values in matrix products without nonnegativity constraints. Although this algorithm is surpassed by randomized counterparts, it yields the first subquadratic-time deterministic algorithm for matrix products with a limited number of nonzero entries, marking a substantial breakthrough in the field of matrix multiplication. Our research contributes to the ongoing quest for efficient and accurate matrix multiplication methods, with potential implications for various data-intensive applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: Recent observations of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) have unveiled a striking kinematical discrepancy between its HI gas and old stellar populations. While the HI gas exhibits significant rotation, the old stars display little to no rotation. This dichotomy can be attributed to a major merger event that occurred during the SMC's formative stages. Our simulations demonstrate that the merger of two gas-rich dwarf irregulars can give rise to a new dwarf galaxy, comprising a spheroidal stellar component and a rotating extended HI disk. The remnant of this merger exhibits distinct kinematic properties, with a rapidly rotating gas disk and a stellar component characterized by minimal rotation. We propose that the SMC evolved from such a merged dwarf galaxy, with the outer gas stripped away by tidal interactions with the Galaxy and the Large Magellanic Cloud. Further study of the spatial distributions and kinematics of Red Giant Branch (RGB) and Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars of varying ages in the SMC's spheroidal component can provide crucial insights into the occurrence and timing of a past major merger event, shedding light on the SMC's tumultuous history and evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents an automatic Gabor wavelet selection algorithm for face recognition, leveraging parallel AdaBoosting and mutual information. The approach optimizes feature selection for classification accuracy and efficiency. By utilizing properly chosen Gabor wavelets with parallel AdaBoost and mutual information, high recognition rates are achieved with reduced computational cost. Experiments on the FERET face database demonstrate significant reductions in memory and computation costs, while maintaining high classification accuracy, thus enhancing the overall performance of face recognition systems. The proposed framework offers a efficient and effective solution for automatic face recognition.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report the detection of a distant star-forming galaxy, ALMA J010748.3-703028, situated behind the nearby merging galaxies VV114. Utilizing the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) Band 3, we identify a 13CO emission line at 99.75 GHz, with a corresponding flux density of 2 Jy km/s. Additionally, an 880-μm counterpart is observed with ALMA Band 7, exhibiting a flux density of 5 mJy. A detailed analysis of the line and continuum intensities suggests that the line is a redshifted 6CO transition. Photometric redshift analysis, incorporating infrared to radio data, yields a preferred CO redshift of 6.5, although a redshift of 5.5 is also plausible. The presence of a hard X-ray counterpart indicates a luminous active galactic nucleus, obscured by a substantial hydrogen column. Cosmological simulations reveal that the chance detection rate of a CO-emitting galaxy at z=6.5 with 2 Jy km/s is 0.01 per single ALMA field of view, demonstrating ALMA's capability to detect such emission-line galaxies, albeit with low probability. This discovery highlights the potential for serendipitous detections of distant galaxies using ALMA.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents three distinct measurements of the top quark mass in the lepton plus jets channel, utilizing approximately @xmath0 of data from the CDF detector. To minimize dependence on the jet energy scale, we employ quantities such as the mean transverse decay length of @xmath1-tagged jets (L2D) and the transverse momentum of the lepton (lepPT). The top mass is determined to be @xmath2 using L2D, @xmath3 using lepPT, and @xmath4 when combining both variables. These results demonstrate the potential for precise top quark mass measurements using alternative methods. Although some systematic uncertainties are statistically limited, future enhancements to the Tevatron or measurements at the LHC are expected to significantly improve the accuracy of these results, providing valuable insights into the properties of the top quark. The combined measurement yields a top mass of @xmath4, showcasing the effectiveness of this approach.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the violation of the Bell inequality in the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt form for Josephson phase qubits. We analyze the ideal case with maximum violation and then consider the impacts of local measurement errors and decoherence. Optimal configurations in the pseudospin space are identified, particularly those within horizontal or vertical planes. The effects of measurement crosstalk on both classical and quantum results are also discussed. Notably, a crosstalk-insensitive version of the Bell inequality is proposed, providing a robust framework for quantum non-locality tests in the presence of measurement errors and decoherence, with implications for quantum information processing and foundations of quantum mechanics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article introduces a novel dynamical model for simulating the price evolution of financial assets, grounded in a two-level structure. The first level employs an agent-based model to capture the current state of investors' beliefs, perspectives, and strategies, drawing inspiration from predator-prey population dynamics. Agents modify their decisions through self- or mutual interactions on a random basis, independent of the asset's price. This framework yields large oscillations in the number of agents sharing similar perspectives, potentially mirroring bullish and bearish market trends. The second level incorporates a pricing mechanism driven by the relative population of investors in different groups. We develop two pricing models: a basic excess demand model and a more complex liquidity model. The outcomes of both models are thoroughly analyzed and compared, providing insights into the price evolution of financial assets. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of financial market dynamics and the role of investor interactions in shaping asset prices. The proposed model offers a flexible framework for simulating various market scenarios, allowing for the exploration of different investor behaviors and their impact on price fluctuations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a novel approach to abstract unification algorithms for logic programs, addressing the limitations of existing methods. We introduce the @xmath0 domain, a general framework that explicitly captures the interaction between sharing and linearity information. By providing a constructive characterization of the optimal abstract unification operator on @xmath0, we establish a foundation for deriving optimal algorithms for other abstract domains. Specifically, we apply this framework to the @xmath1 and @xmath2 domains, yielding optimal abstract unification algorithms for single binding substitutions. This breakthrough enables more accurate and efficient static analysis of logic programs, enhancing the precision of sharing and linearity information detection. Our work contributes to the advancement of abstract interpretation techniques, with significant implications for the optimization of logic programming languages. The proposed approach paves the way for further research in this area, aiming to improve the effectiveness of static analysis tools.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a novel method for isolating a clean sample of red giant branch stars in the outer regions of the Andromeda spiral galaxy (M31) using a combination of spectroscopic and photometric data. Our study utilizes an ongoing spectroscopic survey conducted with the DEIMOS instrument on the Keck II 10-m telescope, which aims to investigate the kinematics, global structure, substructure, and metallicity of M31's halo. To mitigate contamination from foreground Milky Way dwarf stars, we employ a likelihood-based approach that incorporates five key criteria: radial velocity, photometric measurements of the MgH/MgB absorption features, strength of the 8190 absorption line doublet, location within a color-magnitude diagram, and comparison of photometric and spectroscopic metallicity estimates. By leveraging training sets of confirmed M31 red giants and Galactic dwarf stars, we derive empirical probability distribution functions for each diagnostic and calculate the likelihood of a star being a red giant branch star in M31 versus a Milky Way dwarf star. Application of this method to our spectroscopic dataset yields a sample of 40 M31 red giants beyond a projected distance of 1 kpc from the galaxy's center, including three red giants at distances of up to 2 kpc. This ability to identify individual M31 red giant stars enables an unprecedented level of sensitivity in studying the properties of the galaxy's outer halo, providing valuable insights into the formation and evolution of M31. Our approach demonstrates the potential for future studies to explore the kinematics, metallicity, and structure of the outer halo in unprecedented detail, shedding new light on the complex history of our nearest major galactic neighbor.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the Landau-Lifshitz theory and Israel-Stewart hydrodynamics, revealing a correlation between acausality and instability in relativistic dissipative hydrodynamics. Acausality induces instability, and the scaling solution's stability is also discussed, showing potential instability to inhomogeneous perturbations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study employs first-principles density functional calculations to investigate the interplay between ferroelectricity and polar discontinuities in 1-1 oxide superlattices. The superlattices are composed of ferroelectric and paraelectric components with varied chemical compositions. Our results show that polar discontinuities at the interfaces induce off-centric movements in the ferroelectric layers, resulting in non-switchable polarizations comparable to those in bulk ferroelectrics. In contrast, superlattices without polar discontinuities exhibit suppressed off-centric movements. The behavior and functional properties of these superlattices are found to be sensitive to epitaxial strain, rotational instabilities, and second-order Jahn-Teller activity, which are strongly influenced by the paraelectric layer's chemical composition. These findings provide valuable insights into the complex relationships between ferroelectricity, polar discontinuities, and chemical composition in oxide superlattices, with implications for the design of novel functional materials.
label: llama-3.3-70b

This study presents the results of a balloon-borne experiment designed to measure the absolute temperature of the Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR) at 10.7 GHz. The instrument, comprising a cooled corrugated horn antenna and a total-power radiometer, achieved a temperature measurement with a statistical error of less than 0.1 mK. Systematic errors were minimized through the use of a cryogenic mechanical waveguide switch, a cold front end, and a large outer ground screen and smaller inner screen to shield the instrument from stray radiation. By flying the instrument at 24 km altitude, atmospheric and window emission were also reduced. In-flight tests and observations in narrow frequency bands were conducted to constrain ground radiation contamination and monitor low-level interference. The measured temperature difference between the sky signal and the internal reference load was found to be @xmath1 mK, yielding an absolute temperature measurement of @xmath0 K with a total error representing the quadratic sum of several systematic errors.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study updates our previous research on very short gamma-ray bursts (VSGRBs) with durations ≤10 ms, revealing significant angular asymmetry and uniform distributions using BATSE data. We expand our analysis to include 18 VSGRBs observed by the KONUS satellite, which provides new spectral insights. These events exhibit numerous high-energy photons, with all bursts having photons above 5 MeV, making them among the most energetic observed to date. Our findings offer a fresh understanding of VSGRBs, highlighting their exceptional energy release and potential to probe extreme astrophysical phenomena. Further analysis is warranted to elucidate their origins.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a numerical implementation of a variational approach for reconstructing cracks and cavities in inverse problems. The method utilizes phase-field functions to describe defects and perimeter-like penalizations to regularize the ill-posed problem. A gradient method is employed to solve the corresponding optimality system. Numerical simulations demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results show that the method can accurately reconstruct cracks and cavities, highlighting its potential for solving complex inverse problems. The study contributes to the development of robust numerical methods for inverse problems, with applications in various fields of engineering and physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present accurate BVRI photometry for Uranus' irregular satellites, Sycorax and Caliban. Derived colors indicate Sycorax is bluer than Caliban. Notable variability is detected in Caliban's light-curve, suggesting a 3-hour period. Although brighter, Sycorax exhibits no strong variability, but hints at a 4-hour period, warranting further investigation.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the interplay between star formation activity, stellar mass, and environmental factors in high-redshift galaxies within the 2 deg^2 COSMOS field. By utilizing the [O II] emission line as a proxy for star formation and local galaxy density to characterize environment, we uncover significant trends. Notably, for massive galaxies (M > 10^10 M_sun), the fraction of [O II] emitters in high-density environments is 2.5 times higher than in low-density environments, whereas the [O II] emitter fraction remains environment-independent for low-mass galaxies (M < 10^9 M_sun). To elucidate these findings, we investigate the influence of companion galaxies and discover that the [O II] emitter fraction in galaxies with companions is 3.2 times higher than in those without, particularly at z ~ 1. Furthermore, massive galaxies in high-density environments are more likely to have companions. While the presence of close companions and dense environments increases the number of star-forming galaxies among massive galaxies, the average star formation rate of star-forming galaxies at a given mass remains environment- and companion-independent. These results imply that interactions and mergers in high-density environments may trigger star formation in massive galaxies at z ~ 1, thereby enhancing the fraction of star-forming galaxies with M > 10^10 M_sun. Ultimately, this research provides insights into the complex relationships governing star formation in high-redshift galaxies and highlights the importance of environmental factors in shaping their evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the potential of quantum state engineering utilizing a Kerr-type non-linearity model enhanced by electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT), as proposed by Petrosyan and Kurizki. By transcending the semiclassical approach, we derive a quantum version of the model, incorporating both a full Hamiltonian framework and an analysis of dressed states. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of preparing an entangled coherent state through cross-phase modulation, showcasing robustness against low detection efficiency in terms of locality violation. Furthermore, we investigate the bi-chromatic photon blockade effect in a bi-modal electromagnetic cavity driven by a low-density atomic beam. The effectiveness of this blockade is evident even with multiple atoms present in the cavity. Notably, the ability to control two distinct cavity modes provides valuable insights into generating an entangled state of cavity modes, highlighting the model's potential for quantum state engineering and its applications in quantum information processing.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a comprehensive analysis of the astrometric, spin, and orbital parameters of PSR J1953+1846A, a "black widow" binary millisecond pulsar residing in the globular cluster M71. Leveraging precise radio timing data, we accurately determined the pulsar's position and orbital parameters, facilitating the identification of its optical companion in archival Hubble Space Telescope images. The companion is revealed to be a faint and variable star, situated merely 0.2 arcseconds from the predicted pulsar position. Notably, the optical light curve exhibits a maximum at the pulsar's inferior conjunction and a minimum at its superior conjunction, confirming the association with the system. The observed modulation suggests heating of the companion star by the pulsar wind, while a comparison with the X-ray light curve hints at the presence of an intra-binary shock. This study marks the second identification of an optical companion to a black widow pulsar in a globular cluster, with intriguing similarities to the previously identified companion in M5. Our findings provide valuable insights into the complex interactions within these enigmatic systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a one-dimensional numerical analysis of Alfvén waves propagating along a radial magnetic field, neglecting losses. The results show that any spherical Alfvén wave becomes nonlinear at large radii, regardless of initial amplitude. As expected, the waves steepen and produce current sheets in the nonlinear regime. Notably, even mildly nonlinear waves experience significant damping, with almost complete dissipation occurring before 10 stellar radii. This finding supports models of Alfvén wave-driven winds from old low-mass stars, which require substantial damping within a few stellar radii to accelerate the wind. The research sheds light on the dynamics of Alfvén waves in stellar environments.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study proposes an exactly soluble non-linear interaction Hamiltonian to investigate the fundamental properties of entanglement dynamics in coupled non-linear oscillators. By analytically obtaining the time-evolved state for initial products of coherent and number states, we extract relevant information from the dynamics of subsystem entropies, quadrature mean values, and variances. Our results reveal the re-coherence time scales and identify the interaction term responsible for entanglement in both cases. Notably, we discover two regimes for entanglement dynamics in initially coherent states: a short-time phase spread regime characterized by monotonically increasing entropy, and a self-interference regime marked by oscillating entropy and re-coherence phenomena. Furthermore, we find that the break time between these regimes, as well as re-coherence and reversibility times, increase as Planck's constant becomes smaller than a typical action in phase space. These findings provide valuable insights into the complex dynamics of entanglement in non-linear systems, shedding light on the interplay between quantum mechanics and classical behavior.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines quarkonia production at the LHC, focusing on experimental aspects of @xmath0 and @xmath1(1s) generation. Utilizing LHC data, we investigate high transverse momenta and statistics.
