text: We examine a rotating black string falling into a rotating horizon in 5D spacetime, considering axisymmetric configurations with a smooth intersection. Our analysis extends to rotating and charged flows, exploring the dynamics of Kerr black holes and black string flows in this regime, shedding light on the intricate relationships between these objects in higher-dimensional spacetimes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the statistical properties of the sum of time spent in positive or negative states by a spin in a d-dimensional Ising model under Glauber dynamics. The distribution and first-passage statistics of this quantity are investigated across three temperature regimes: high, critical, and low. Particular attention is given to the temperature dependence of the persistence exponent and the spectrum of exponents in the low-temperature phase. The probability of the temporal mean exceeding the equilibrium magnetization is found to decay according to a specific power law. This discovery enables the numerical determination of the persistence exponent in the low-temperature phase of the two-dimensional Ising model and above the roughening transition in the three-dimensional model. The results provide new insights into the dynamics of the Ising model, shedding light on the behavior of spins in different temperature regimes and dimensions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the development of highly accurate optical clocks, driven by demands from various scientific and technological fields. The current cesium atomic clocks, limited by microwave frequency regime, are being surpassed by next-generation optical clocks aiming for 1 part in 10^18 uncertainty. Focusing on the promising candidate, Yb, we investigate the electric quadrupole and hyperfine shifts in its clock transition. Utilizing relativistic coupled cluster theory, we determine the electric quadrupole moment and magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole hyperfine constants for the relevant states. The crucial role of electron correlation in accurately determining these quantities is discussed. Our research contributes to the understanding of frequency standards in Yb, paving the way for the development of ultra-precise optical clocks. The calculated values are essential for mitigating systematic errors and achieving the desired level of accuracy in optical clock operations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the physical scales of star-forming regions in high-redshift luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxies (LIRGs and ULIRGs) and submillimeter galaxies (SMGs), comparing them to those in local normal star-forming galaxies. Our findings indicate that the star-forming regions in these high-redshift galaxies have similar physical scales to their local counterparts, with their higher infrared (IR) luminosities resulting from higher luminosity surface density. A strong correlation is observed between IR luminosity and IR luminosity surface density in starburst galaxies, spanning over five orders of magnitude of IR luminosity. However, local ULIRGs exhibit smaller star-forming regions, diverging from this correlation and suggesting they belong to a distinct population. We propose that luminosity surface density is a more accurate indicator of the IR emitting environment and observable properties of star-forming galaxies than IR luminosity. This approach is demonstrated by the aromatic features of high-redshift ULIRGs and a lensed galaxy, which agree with those of local LIRGs having similar IR luminosity surface density but lower IR luminosity. The implications of this relationship suggest that the aromatic emission strength in star-forming galaxies will appear to increase at high redshifts for a given IR luminosity compared to local galaxies, highlighting the importance of considering luminosity surface density in the study of star-forming galaxies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study evaluates the mean value and cross-covariance function of chaotic binary sequences generated by chaotic maps with specific properties. The impact of fixed- and floating-point representations on statistical properties is assessed. Statistical tests are applied to identify suitable candidates for pseudo-random binary sequences. The results demonstrate potential for security enhancement in IEEE 802.11 standard, leveraging chaotic binary sequences for improved cryptography and random number generation, with implications for chaos-based security applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the performance limits of ambient backscatter systems in broadband fading environments, where small devices harness power from radio-frequency (RF) signals to compute and communicate. By reflecting existing RF signals from legacy systems, such as digital TV broadcasting, cellular, or Wi-Fi, ambient backscattering devices can convert interference into a usable signal. We develop a detailed signal model to analyze the capacity of both legacy and backscatter systems, considering various amounts of network state information at the receivers. Our results show that, under reasonable conditions, a legacy system using multicarrier modulation can exploit RF interference from backscattering as a form of multipath diversity, significantly enhancing its performance. Furthermore, we demonstrate that simple single-carrier modulation techniques can achieve substantial data rates over short distances, particularly when the backscatter receiver is co-located with the legacy transmitter. This study provides insights into the ultimate performance bounds of ambient backscatter systems, including ergodic and outage capacity, symbol variance, and amplitude constraints, shedding light on the potential of this innovative wireless communication paradigm. Our findings have implications for the design and optimization of ambient backscatter systems, enabling efficient and reliable communication in various applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents an in-depth analysis of the spectrum of an unusually low-mass white dwarf, SDSSJ123410.37-022802.9, identified in our recent catalog of white dwarfs from the SDSS DR1 data release. Utilizing two independent model atmosphere fits, we accurately determine the atmospheric and stellar parameters of this object, yielding a effective temperature of 17,470 ± 1750 K and a surface gravity of 6.38 ± 0.10. Our analysis suggests that this object cannot be classified as a main sequence A star, horizontal branch, or subdwarf B star. Instead, we interpret it as a very low-mass white dwarf with a helium core, possessing a mass of 0.18-0.19 M⊙, similar to the companion of the millisecond pulsar J1012+5307. We propose that this star may be in a binary system, potentially with an undiscovered or dead pulsar companion, or a more ordinary star that underwent Roche lobe mass transfer. A second low-mass white dwarf candidate from the SDSS is also examined, although the poorer quality spectrum hinders definitive classification. Further investigation of this sample is warranted to confirm the presence of additional extremely low-mass white dwarfs, emphasizing the need for precise observation and interpretation.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a novel method for recovering and investigating spiral structures in the nuclear regions of galaxies through a harmonic expansion of the observed line-of-sight velocity field. We apply this technique to the emission-line velocity field within the circumnuclear star-forming ring of NGC 1097, obtained using the GMOS-IFU spectrograph. The results reveal a three-arm spiral pattern in the non-circular motions, which is consistent with a two-arm dust spiral observed in the surface brightness. The nuclear spiral is found to be a weak perturbation in the gravitational potential, characterized by a two-arm logarithmic spiral with a pitch angle of approximately 10 degrees. Using a simple spiral perturbation model, we estimate the fraction of non-circular motions due to radial inflow and combine it with the gas density in the spiral arms to determine the mass inflow rate as a function of radius. Our calculations yield a mass inflow rate of approximately 0.02 solar masses per year at a distance of 100 parsecs from the center, which corresponds to about 0.6% of the Eddington mass accretion rate onto the central black hole in NGC 1097. These findings are consistent with previous mass accretion models and suggest that the presented method provides a valuable tool for quantitatively studying nuclear spirals and their role in fueling the centers of galaxies. The technique offers a cleaner view of nuclear spirals than traditional methods and allows for the estimation of mass inflow rates as a function of radius, making it a promising approach for future studies of galaxy evolution and black hole growth.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the stability of fundamental defects in an unstretchable flat sheet by expanding the bending energy to second order in deformations about the defect. The deformations are found to occur as eigenstates of a fourth-order linear differential operator, with unstretchability imposing a global linear constraint. Conical defects with a surplus angle exhibit an infinite number of states, which possess an n-fold symmetry labeled by an integer, n, if the angle is below a critical value. A nonlinear stability analysis reveals that the 2-fold ground state is stable, while excited states have two unstable modes that come in even and odd pairs. These findings have significant implications for understanding the behavior of defects in unstretchable materials, such as paper, and shed light on the complex interplay between geometry, elasticity, and stability in these systems. The results provide new insights into the mechanical properties of thin sheets.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the Silicon Track Trigger (STT), commissioned in 2004 at the D experiment. The STT enriches the data sample with b-meson events at the second trigger level, providing tracks with impact parameter resolution. Preliminary results and a fast b-identification algorithm for the second trigger level are shown, demonstrating the STT's capability to efficiently select b-meson events.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article investigates Moser's Shadow Problem, which seeks to estimate the minimal value of vertices in a polyhedron's shadow when illuminated from a specific direction. We derive asymptotic bounds for the shadow functions associated with bounded and unbounded convex polyhedra. For bounded polyhedra, we confirm the existing result of Θ(n^2) vertices, building on the 1989 work of Chazelle, Edelsbrunner, and Guibas. In contrast, the unbounded case exhibits a distinct asymptotic growth rate of Θ(n^3) vertices, providing new insights into the problem's complexity. Our findings establish the correct order of magnitude for these functions, shedding light on the intricacies of Moser's Shadow Problem.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the Spitzer Deep, Wide-Field Survey (SDWFS), a four-epoch infrared survey of ten square degrees in the Bootes field of the NOAO Deep Wide-Field Survey, conducted using the IRAC instrument on the Spitzer Space Telescope. As a Spitzer Cycle 4 Legacy project, SDWFS occupies a unique position in the area-depth survey space, enabling the selection of infrared-variable and high proper motion objects over a wide field on timescales of years. The survey's large volume makes it sensitive to galaxies out to high redshifts with minimal impact from cosmic variance, making it an ideal dataset for characterizing galaxy evolution beyond z=1. This paper outlines the SDWFS observing strategy and data processing, and presents the resulting mosaics and source catalogs. The publicly released catalogs contain over 6.78, 5.23, 1.20, and 0.45 million distinct sources detected to the average 3", 4" diameter, aperture-corrected limits of 19.77, 18.83, 16.50, and 15.82 Vega mag at 3.6, 4.5, 5.8, and 8.0 microns, respectively. Preliminary scientific findings include consistent number counts and color-color distributions with other Spitzer surveys, as well as the detection of isolated first radio sources and on-axis XBootes sources. Notably, the multi-epoch imaging has allowed for the identification of four high proper motion IRAC-selected sources, two of which are likely field brown dwarfs of mid-T spectral class. The SDWFS datasets are poised to make significant contributions to our understanding of galaxy evolution, variable and moving objects, and the properties of faint infrared sources.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the critical properties of a self-avoiding loop model with variable bending rigidity, which is equivalent to the strong coupling lattice Schwinger model with Wilson fermions. Two approximate analytical methods are employed to investigate the model's behavior: the independent loop approximation and a method based on the exact solution of the self-avoiding loop model with bending rigidity. The results confirm that the strong coupling lattice Schwinger model undergoes a second-order phase transition, belonging to the Ising model universality class, when the monomer weight reaches a critical value. The critical behavior of the model is analyzed, and the central charge of the strong coupling Schwinger model at criticality is predicted. The findings are compared to known Monte Carlo results, validating the approximate methods used. The study provides insight into the critical properties of the self-avoiding loop model and sheds light on the behavior of the strong coupling lattice Schwinger model, contributing to our understanding of phase transitions in statistical mechanics and field theory. The results have implications for the study of polymers, liquid helium, and cosmic strings, and demonstrate the effectiveness of approximate analytical methods in investigating complex systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article approaches the portfolio selection problem from a signal processing perspective, investigating how and when to diversify capital across assets to achieve optimal expected growth. We first consider two-asset markets with independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) discrete-time returns and proportional transaction costs. By constructing threshold portfolios with recursive updates for expected wealth calculation, we demonstrate that the set of achievable portfolios forms an irreducible Markov chain under mild conditions. We evaluate the stationary distribution of this chain, providing an efficient method for calculating cumulative expected wealth. The parameters are then optimized to yield the growth-optimal portfolio in two-asset markets. We extend our analysis to markets with more than two assets and to discrete-time markets sampled from continuous-time Brownian markets. Furthermore, we address the case of unknown discrete distributions of price relative vectors by incorporating a maximum likelihood estimator into the optimization framework. Our simulations demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in solving the optimal portfolio selection problem in various scenarios, offering a novel and efficient solution to a longstanding problem in finance. The results have significant implications for investment strategies and portfolio management, highlighting the potential of signal processing techniques in optimizing financial performance.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents an analytical investigation of the quasicontinuum method, a multiscale approach used to model the behavior of materials at the atomic scale. We compare the discrete-to-continuum analysis of a one-dimensional atomistic model with a corresponding quasicontinuum model, considering Lennard-Jones type interactions between nearest and next-to-nearest neighbors. Our analysis, utilizing Γ-convergence techniques, reveals that in an elastic setting, the minimizers and minimal energies of the atomistic and quasicontinuum models exhibit the same limiting behavior as the number of atoms increases. However, in the presence of fracture, this equivalence does not hold in general. The choice of representative atoms in the quasicontinuum approximation is shown to influence the fracture energy and crack location. We establish sufficient conditions for selecting representative atoms that ensure the minimal energies of the atomistic and quasicontinuum models coincide in the limit, with the crack forming in the atomistic region as desired. Our findings provide valuable insights into the quasicontinuum method's performance and its application to modeling material behavior at the atomic scale.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We propose a novel method for solving Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov equations in weakly bound nuclei. This approach improves continuum treatment with finite-range interactions by utilizing a mixed eigenfunction expansion and resonance expansion, overcoming continuous spectrum discretization issues and enhancing accuracy in unstable nuclei calculations with finite-range interactions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper presents surface links with link groups that are free abelian groups of rank three or four, contradicting classical link group restrictions. Infinitely many examples of rank three are provided, including one with four triple points, expanding the understanding of link group structures and their potential ranks.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents age measurements for 195 star clusters in the Small Magellanic Cloud, derived from a comparison of integrated colors from the Magellanic Clouds Photometric Survey with simple stellar population models. Our analysis reveals that non-uniform color changes with age can introduce artificial peaks in the cluster age distribution. The observed cluster numbers decrease smoothly with age, and we find that cluster disruption time scales with mass according to a power-law relation. Despite the abundance of young clusters, our results suggest that the dominant epoch of cluster formation occurred initially. Significant spatial variations are also observed in the distribution of clusters of different ages. While limitations in age measurement precision preclude a detailed comparison with field star formation history, this sample provides a foundation for future studies targeting specific age intervals, enabling a more nuanced understanding of star cluster evolution and formation in the Small Magellanic Cloud.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines quintessence models comprising multiple scalar fields coupled to dark matter components. For exponential potentials, scaling solutions are reduced to a single field, yielding simple expressions for effective logarithmic slope and coupling. We also explore solutions with negligible scalar potential, including transient matter-dominated phases. Furthermore, evolution equations for linear perturbations are derived, enabling these models to be tested against observational data. Our findings provide a framework for understanding complex quintessence scenarios and their potential implications for cosmological observations, facilitating future model testing and refinement. Key predictions are thus generated.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a detailed analysis of high-resolution spectra of six core-helium burning 'clump' stars in the open cluster NGC 6134. Building on our previous work, which determined the atmospheric parameters of these stars, we have derived abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and up to 24 other chemical elements. Our analysis reveals significant deviations from solar abundances, including a depletion of carbon by approximately 0.2 dex, an overabundance of nitrogen by around 0.3 dex, and an underabundance of oxygen by about 0.1 dex. These abundance patterns result in a lowered mean C/N ratio and altered 12C/13C ratios. In contrast, the abundance ratios of other elements, including sodium, magnesium, and iron-group elements, are found to be close to solar values. Our findings provide new insights into the chemical evolution of clump stars in open clusters and have implications for our understanding of stellar nucleosynthesis and the enrichment of the interstellar medium. The results of this study contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of the complex processes governing the abundances of chemical elements in stellar populations, and highlight the importance of high-resolution spectroscopy in probing the properties of stars in open clusters.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the Gaussianity of the 4-year COBE-DMR data utilizing spherical Haar wavelets in the HEALPix pixelization. We analyze pixels outside the galactic cut, computing skewness, kurtosis, and scale-scale correlation spectra for wavelet coefficients at each scale. The method's sensitivity to input signal orientation is also considered. Our results indicate a non-Gaussianity detection at a 0% level in one statistic, but after accounting for the total number of statistics computed, the probability of this detection occurring by chance in an underlying Gaussian field is estimated to be 0.69. Consequently, the spherical wavelet technique reveals no strong evidence of non-Gaussianity in the COBE-DMR data, supporting the notion of Gaussianity in the cosmic microwave background. This research contributes to the ongoing analysis of cosmic microwave background data using advanced statistical methods.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the emerging threats to user privacy resulting from the subversion of privacy infrastructures. Despite their intended purpose of safeguarding user privacy, these infrastructures are being exploited by attackers for illicit activities. Focusing on the prominent Tor network, we outline the critical privacy infrastructures developed to protect user anonymity. An assessment of the rising threats to Tor's integrity is presented, highlighting the severity of these risks. Our analysis underscores the need for further research to mitigate the dangers posed by the exploitation of privacy infrastructures. We conclude by recommending avenues for future studies to strengthen the security and integrity of these vital systems, ultimately protecting user privacy in the face of widespread surveillance.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article revisits the concept of strange stars, composed of absolutely stable strange quark matter, first proposed by E. Witten nearly a quarter of a century ago. A notable feature of these objects is the potential presence of ultra-strong electric fields on their surfaces, with ordinary strange matter exhibiting fields of approximately 0 V/cm. However, if strange matter forms a color superconductor, the electric field strength may increase to over 1 V/cm. The associated energy density of such fields is comparable to that of the strange matter itself. Our research demonstrates that this phenomenon alters the masses and radii of strange quark stars by 15% and 5%, respectively. Consequently, this mass increase facilitates the interpretation of massive compact stars, with masses around 2, as strange quark stars, providing new insights into the properties and behavior of these exotic celestial objects. Theoretical implications are discussed.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents low-resolution, ultraviolet-to-visual spectra of two candidate globular clusters in the merger remnant galaxy NGC 3921. Located at projected distances of approximately 5 kpc from the galaxy center, these clusters exhibit halo-type radial velocities and strong Balmer absorption lines, indicating main-sequence turnoffs dominated by A-type stars. Spectral comparisons with model clusters yield age estimates ranging from 200-530 Myr and metallicities near solar levels. The clusters' small half-light radii and ages corresponding to multiple core-crossing times suggest they are gravitationally bound, confirming their status as young globular clusters. Assuming a Chabrier-type initial mass function, their estimated current masses are substantial, roughly half that of omega Centauri. The presence of these young, metal-rich globular clusters in NGC 3921, a galaxy exhibiting characteristics of a 1 Gyr old proto-elliptical, provides evidence that major mergers of gas-rich disks can lead to an increase in the number of metal-rich globular clusters, supporting the notion that such mergers play a key role in the formation of elliptical-like galaxies. These findings contribute to our understanding of globular cluster formation and the evolution of galaxy morphology in the context of major mergers.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study proposes a novel many-variable variational Monte Carlo (MVMC) method integrated with tensor networks to investigate fermionic models. By combining the strengths of both approaches, the variational wave function is constructed from a pair product wave function modified by real-space correlation factors and tensor networks. The method is further enhanced by applying quantum number projections, including spin, momentum, and lattice symmetry projections, to restore the symmetry of the wave function and improve accuracy. Benchmark tests on one- and two-dimensional Hubbard models demonstrate significant improvements over individual MVMC or tensor network results. The method is then applied to the hole-doped Hubbard model on a square lattice, revealing a stripe charge/spin order coexisting with a weak d-wave superconducting order in the ground state for doping concentrations below 0.3. Notably, a charge-homogeneous and highly superconducting state is also found as a metastable excited state for doping concentrations below 0.25, providing new insights into the complex phase diagram of the Hubbard model.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study proposes a generalized Skyrme model to describe nuclei as near-Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) skyrmions, motivated by the relatively small binding energy in nuclei. By incorporating terms up to sixth order in derivatives of the pion fields and treating nonlinear and Skyrme terms as perturbations, we derive well-behaved analytical BPS-type solutions. Our model yields non-shell configurations for baryon density, contrasting with the complex shell-like configurations found in other Skyrme model extensions. We calculate static and rotational energies, and include Coulomb energy and isospin breaking terms to obtain the total mass of nuclei. Fitting the model parameters, we find excellent agreement between the predicted binding energy per nucleon and experimental data. These results support the notion that nuclei can be effectively represented as near-BPS skyrmions, providing a promising approach to understanding nuclear structure and properties. The model's simplicity and accuracy make it an attractive framework for further nuclear physics research.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: In this paper, we examine the reaction recently investigated by the BESIII collaboration, which reported the existence of a resonance, dubbed X, in the invariant mass spectrum with a mass of approximately 4026 MeV and a width of about 26 MeV. Our analysis of the invariant mass distribution reveals that while the BESIII collaboration's explanation is plausible, alternative interpretations, such as a tetraquark resonance or a bound state, are equally possible. Furthermore, we find that the data can be explained without invoking the existence of a resonance or bound state, highlighting the ambiguity of the current results. To resolve this ambiguity, we propose a strategy to distinguish between the possible origins of the observed signal by studying the dependence of the invariant mass spectrum on the total center-of-mass energy. Our findings suggest that increasing the center-of-mass energy from 4.26 GeV to 4.6 GeV could provide valuable insights into the nature of the signal, allowing for a more definitive identification of its origin. These results have important implications for future experiments aiming to clarify the properties of this enigmatic state. Our study underscores the need for further investigation to determine the true nature of the X state.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the scattering of a time-harmonic acoustic incident wave by a bounded, penetrable, and isotropic elastic solid immersed in a homogeneous compressible air or fluid. A numerical solution is developed for this acoustic-elastic interaction problem in three dimensions. An exact transparent boundary condition is established to reduce the problem to a bounded domain, and the perfectly matched layer technique is used to truncate the unbounded physical domain. The well-posedness and exponential convergence of the solution are proven, and an adaptive finite element method is developed to solve the scattering problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showcasing its competitive behavior in solving acoustic-elastic interaction problems. The approach provides a reliable and efficient tool for simulating wave propagation in complex media.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents measurements of the Raman mode in graphene and carbon nanotubes at varying laser excitation energies. The mode, observed between 1050-1150 cm^-1, is attributed to a double-resonant scattering process involving longitudinal acoustic phonons and defects. We examine its dependence on excitation energy, graphene layer thickness, and carbon nanotube diameter. Our findings assign this mode to inner processes with resonant phonons primarily from the high-symmetry direction. The mode's asymmetry is attributed to additional phonon contributions. These results highlight the significance of inner contributions in double-resonance scattering and provide a rapid method for investigating acoustic phonons in graphene and carbon nanotubes using optical spectroscopy, offering new insights into their properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the viability of a CPT-violating neutrino mass spectrum proposed to reconcile discrepancies between various neutrino experiments. A three-generation analysis of global data is performed to assess the compatibility of the LSND results with other experiments. Our findings indicate a significant incompatibility between LSND and other datasets, with no overlap below 3σ CL. Furthermore, the global data, excluding LSND, show no evidence of CPT violation, with the best-fit point occurring near a CPT-conserving scenario. These results suggest that the CPT-violating solution is not supported by the current experimental data, prompting a reevaluation of alternative explanations for the observed neutrino oscillation phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper explores the properties of integral circulant graphs, specifically the clique number, and its relationship to the number of vertices. We investigate a conjecture proposing that the clique number divides the number of vertices, previously proposed in existing literature. Our research provides a complete solution for integral circulant graphs with one and two divisors. However, for graphs with more divisors, we construct counterexamples that disprove the conjecture, shedding new light on the properties of these graphs and contributing to the understanding of their structure. Our findings have implications for graph theory and related fields.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article proposes a novel formalism for classical nonrelativistic mechanics of a mass point, grounded in thermodynamic theory. By treating particle trajectories as geometric dynamical variables on a smooth manifold, a classical statistical mechanics framework is constructed. Thermodynamic variables are introduced via a partition function based on a canonical ensemble of trajectories. This approach reveals classical mechanics as an equilibrium state of statistical mechanics. The relationship between classical and quantum mechanics is examined, with the maximum-entropy principle providing a unified perspective on both. This framework offers new insights into the underlying connections between these fundamental theories.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We re-examine the holographic superconductor in hyperscaling violation geometry, incorporating the coupling between the Maxwell field and background dilaton. Our results show that superconductivity persists, but with altered properties. The critical temperature decreases with increasing hyperscaling violation exponent, while the dynamical exponent's influence is complex, depending on the scalar field's mass and hyperscaling violation. Notably, the frequency gap deviates significantly from the expected universal relation, highlighting the impact of this coupling on superconducting behavior.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We propose an all-dielectric photonic crystal structure supporting 2D confined helical topological edge states. Crystal parameters control topological properties, and an interface between differing band topologies yields edge states in a dielectric slab. These states propagate around sharp corners without backscattering, confined by total internal reflection. 3D finite-difference time-domain calculations confirm out-of-plane confinement. This architecture enables strong interactions between photonic edge states and quantum emitters, paving the way for innovative nanoscale photonic devices with potential applications in quantum optics and information processing, offering new avenues for exploring topological photonics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the exclusive production of vector meson pairs in electron-positron collisions, facilitated by annihilation into two virtual photons. At high energies, the cross section is dominated by independent fragmentation of virtual photons into vector mesons. Utilizing the fragmentation approximation, we calculate cross sections and angular distributions for vector meson pairs producible at B factories. Our predicted cross sections for certain meson productions align with Babar collaboration measurements. Additionally, non-fragmentation corrections for charmonium vector meson production are calculated using the NRQCD factorization formalism, yielding predicted cross sections compatible with Belle collaboration upper limits, providing insight into the production mechanisms of vector meson pairs.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the results of a one-year observational campaign of the Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) 1996X, conducted at the European Southern Observatory (ESO). The campaign included UBVR photometry and optical spectra, supplemented by late-time Hubble Space Telescope (HST) photometry. Spectroscopic analysis reveals that SN 1996X is a 'normal' SN Ia, with an apparent magnitude at maximum and color consistent with this classification. The luminosity decline rate is close to average for a SN Ia, and estimates suggest negligible reddening within the parent galaxy, NGC 5061. A detailed comparison of the light and color curves with other 'normal' SNe Ia highlights the limitations of describing multicolor light curves as a one-parameter family. This, combined with calibration issues, may explain discrepancies in distance modulus estimates derived from different calibrations of absolute magnitude vs. light curve shape relations. Our analysis yields a range of distance modulus values, from 32.02 to 32.48, depending on the method employed. Furthermore, model light curve and synthetic spectra computations confirm that SN 1996X is a normal Type Ia SN, and that a satisfactory fit can be obtained using a W7 progenitor structure only if a short distance is adopted. A larger distance would imply an excessively large nickel mass for this fainter-than-average SN Ia. These findings contribute to our understanding of SNe Ia and the complexities involved in determining their distances and properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: The increasing ability of telescopes like ALMA to resolve Giant Molecular Clouds (GMCs) in external galaxies necessitates a thorough understanding of the observational biases that affect measured GMC properties. This study utilizes a hydrodynamical simulation of a barred spiral galaxy to compare the physical properties of GMCs in 3D position-position-position space (PPP) to those observed in 3D position-position-velocity space (PPV). The effects of disc inclination (face-on and edge-on) and resolution (1.5 pc vs 24 pc) on GMC properties are assessed, including the implications for Larson's scaling relations. Low-resolution PPV data are simulated using ALMA Cycle 3 observations with the CASA package. Results indicate that median properties differ minimally between PPP and face-on PPV at both resolutions, but edge-on PPV clouds exhibit significant deviations. These discrepancies are amplified at lower resolutions, leading to opposing conclusions about the virial parameter and dynamical state of the clouds. The power-law indices of Larson's scaling relations decrease from PPP to edge-on PPV to face-on PPV, and from high to low resolutions, suggesting that these relations are not solely driven by physical origins. Therefore, caution is advised when applying these relations to understand environmental dependencies, dynamical states, and the extragalactic CO-to-H2 conversion factor of GMCs. This study highlights the importance of considering observational biases when interpreting GMC properties in external galaxies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report on a search for solar axions using a helioscope equipped with a 2.3-m long, 4-t superconducting magnet and pin-photodiode X-ray detectors. A new mass region was explored, and no evidence for axions was found. This null result sets a limit on the axion-photon coupling constant, with a 95% confidence level limit of g_aγ < @xmath1 for an axion mass of @xmath2. This study is the first to investigate the @xmath3-@xmath4 parameter region of preferred axion models using a magnetic helioscope, providing new constraints on axion properties and contributing to the ongoing effort to detect these hypothetical particles.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a systematic approach to developing convergent finite element schemes for the Darcy-Stokes flow problem. By combining mixed finite elements that are separately convergent for Darcy and Stokes problems, we establish a methodology that ensures global mass conservation. Unlike existing methods that impose the transmission condition weakly, our approach enforces this condition exactly in the global velocity field space. Theoretical analysis of the Galerkin discretization reveals that stable mixed finite element spaces in the Darcy domain can be paired with stable Stokes mixed finite elements of the same order to achieve a stable global method with quasi-optimal convergence rates. A crucial requirement is that the mixed finite element space in the Darcy domain admits an H(div)-stable discrete lifting of the normal trace. Numerical tests are provided to validate our theoretical convergence estimates, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed method in solving the Darcy-Stokes flow problem.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study delves into the thermodynamic properties of conformal holography in four dimensions, focusing on the computation of the area (or entropy) functional relation for a black hole in both de Sitter (dS) and anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes. The thermodynamic stability is examined through the calculation of the specific heat, revealing a phase transition under specific conditions. The phase structure is analyzed for various values of key parameters, yielding distinct patterns. Notably, in the limiting cases, the results converge to those of Schwarzschild-dS and Schwarzschild-AdS spacetimes, as well as Grumiller spacetime. Furthermore, the thermodynamic volume functional relation is derived in the extended phase space, and a mass-independent entropy functional relation is obtained, which may prove to be a universal quantity. This research contributes to the understanding of conformal gravity and its implications for black hole thermodynamics, highlighting the potential for universal principles underlying these complex systems. The findings have significant implications for the study of gravity and spacetime, particularly in the context of conformal holography.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We synthesized Na@C60OxH2O powder samples by varying water volume in the hydration process and investigated their superconducting properties. The results showed that water volume is crucial for obtaining a single-phase sample with good superconductivity. The transition temperature changed over time in a humid atmosphere, affecting superconducting behavior under high magnetic fields, with high-quality samples exhibiting high sensitivity to temperature.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article revisits the longstanding pursuit of a definitive signal for the manifestation of scale-chiral symmetry in nuclear interactions, inspired by Gerry Brown's unpublished note on the pivotal role of pions and vector mesons. As a tribute to Brown, this work presents a clear example of an unambiguous signal in axial-charge transitions in nuclei. By integrating Brown's ideas with recent developments on hidden symmetries in nuclear physics, a surprising conclusion emerges: the Landau-Migdal fixed point interaction, nuclear tensor forces, and Brown-Rho scaling are all encoded in scale-invariant hidden local symmetry. This symmetry underlies the equivalence of all forces, providing a simple and elegant description of strongly correlated nuclear interactions. The article honors Brown's legacy while shedding new light on the intricate dynamics of nuclear physics, highlighting the significance of hidden symmetries in understanding nuclear interactions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the development of econophysics through scientific communication networks. A weighted, directed network is constructed from 1992-2003 publications, incorporating collaboration, citation, and discussion. Analysis of static properties, including degree distribution and betweenness centrality, provides insight into research dynamics. The introduced method for measuring connection weights offers a general approach to constructing weighted networks, shedding light on the evolution of econophysics research and its complex network structure.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article provides an overview of recent advancements in the statistical mechanics of isolated quantum systems, with a focus on quantum thermalization and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH). We introduce the concept of single-eigenstate statistical mechanics, which arises from the ETH, and then delve into a class of systems that defy quantum thermalization: many-body Anderson localized systems. These systems exhibit eigenstates that violate the ETH, leading to long-time properties that cannot be captured by conventional quantum statistical mechanics ensembles. Notably, many-body localized systems can retain information about their initial conditions indefinitely, making them promising candidates for quantum information storage. We explore the key characteristics of many-body localization (MBL) and review the phenomenology of the MBL phase, highlighting the emergence of dynamically stable ordered phases and phase transitions that are invisible to equilibrium statistical mechanics, even at high energies and low spatial dimensionalities where equilibrium ordering is typically forbidden.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a robust a posteriori error estimator for the Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method applied to convection-diffusion equations with dominant convection. The estimator's reliability and efficiency are established in an energy norm, which remains bounded even as the diffusion coefficient approaches zero. Utilizing a weighted test function technique and Oswald interpolation, the analysis demonstrates uniform bounds on error estimates with respect to the diffusion coefficient. Numerical results confirm the estimator's robustness, providing a reliable tool for error estimation in convection-dominated problems. Theoretical and numerical findings validate the proposed estimator's effectiveness.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article proposes a novel telescope design incorporating Baker-Nunn optics for the observation of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and high-energy neutrinos. The optical system achieves an image resolution of <0.02° within a 50° angular diameter field of view. When paired with a high-quality imaging device, the design enables precise determination of UHECR and neutrino directions with an accuracy of better than 1 arcmin. The telescope's exceptional resolution allows for the separation of charge-separated cosmic rays, facilitating accurate source identification. This significant improvement in angular resolution will facilitate multi-wavelength and multi-particle observations of astronomical objects, enhancing collaborative research with established astronomical observations. The proposed design has the potential to revolutionize the field of UHECR research, offering unparalleled insights into these extreme cosmic phenomena. The Baker-Nunn optics-based telescope is poised to make groundbreaking contributions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates charge exchange spin-dipole excitations in @xmath0Zr and @xmath1Pb using a Skyrme Hartree-Fock + Random Phase Approximation. Calculated spin-dipole strength distributions are compared to experimental data from @xmath0Zr(p, n)@xmath0Nb and @xmath0Zr(n, p)@xmath0Nb reactions. The model-independent sum rule values are analyzed to determine @xmath0Zr's neutron skin thickness. The neutron matter equation of state and nuclear matter symmetry energy are discussed in relation to neutron skin thickness and peak energies of spin-dipole strength distributions, providing insights into nuclear structure and astrophysical applications. Theoretical and experimental results are compared to constrain the neutron skin thickness and its implications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the thermodynamics of complexation between functionalized charged nano-spheres and viral proteins. The interaction is governed by electrostatic forces, screened by salt ions, and configurational degrees of freedom of charged protein tails. A complexation free energy functional is constructed to approach this problem. Through numerical and analytical studies, a phase diagram is developed, revealing assembled structures in thermodynamic equilibrium. The diagram depends on the nano-sphere core's size and surface charge density. Results show that both core charge and radius determine the capsid size forming around the core. This research provides insight into the assembly of viral proteins and nano-spheres, shedding light on the role of electrostatic interactions and configurational entropy in shaping the resulting structures. The findings have implications for understanding viral assembly and designing nano-scale systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article highlights the crucial role of planetary ephemerides in interplanetary spacecraft navigation, solar system dynamics, occultation prediction, and tests of general relativity. To enhance the accuracy of the Saturn ephemeris, we conducted a series of astrometric Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations of the Cassini spacecraft in orbit around Saturn using the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA). Between 2006 and 2009, eight observing epochs yielded positions for the center of mass of Saturn in the International Celestial Reference Frame (ICRF) with accuracies of 0.3 milli-arcseconds (1.5 nrad), equivalent to approximately 2 km at Saturn's average distance. Combining these data with previous VLBA observations and a gravitational deflection measurement, we constrained a new ephemeris (DE 422) with post-fit residuals of 0.2 mas for Saturn. While additional observations are necessary to refine the positions of phase reference sources, our results demonstrate the potential for significant improvements in the Saturn ephemeris, ultimately enhancing the link between inner and outer solar system ephemerides and the inertial ICRF. By continuing these observations, we anticipate improving the accuracy of Saturn's ephemeris by a factor of at least three, contributing substantially to our understanding of solar system dynamics and the refinement of fundamental astronomical reference frames.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We introduce three right-handed Majorana neutrinos, combining type-I seesaw and inert doublet mechanisms. The resultant neutrino mass matrix splits into two parts with distinct energy scales, yielding a hierarchical mass spectrum. Applying this scheme to inverted and normal hierarchy cases reveals a correlation between the smallest mixing angle and lightest neutrino mass, providing insight into neutrino properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We studied @xmath0sn+@xmath1ni and @xmath2sn+@xmath3ni reactions at 35 AMeV using the CHIMERA detector. Central collisions were selected via multidimensional analysis. Source characteristics, such as size and temperature, were examined. Isotope yield ratios of light fragments provided insight into neutron-to-proton density ratios, offering a glimpse into the reaction dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines energy functionals focused on discontinuity lines of divergence-free 2D vector fields valued in the circle. Introduced by Aviles and Giga, these energies are lower semicontinuous with cubic cost functions. However, we present a counter-example demonstrating that line energies with cost functions of a specific form are not lower semicontinuous. Furthermore, we show that the viscosity solution for a convex domain does not minimize the energy, highlighting the limitations of this energy functional for certain cost functions, and contributing to the understanding of its properties and applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the relationship between contact matrices (xmath0-matrices) and contact energy matrices (xmath1-matrices) in native proteins, with a focus on understanding the properties that enable native conformations to achieve the lowest energy states. Assuming that the total conformational energy of a protein can be approximated by the sum of pairwise interaction energies, we investigate the connections between xmath0-matrices and xmath1-matrices. Our analysis reveals that native xmath0-matrices exhibit a relationship with xmath1-matrices akin to a Go-like potential, where the lowest bound of the total energy function corresponds to the total energy of the native conformation interacting in a Go-like pairwise potential. This relationship is characterized by parallel relationships between the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of xmath0-matrices and xmath1-matrices, as well as between contact number vectors and the principal eigenvectors of these matrices. Furthermore, the spectral expansion of xmath1-matrices includes an additional constant term, which is indicative of a threshold of contact energy that separates native from non-native contacts. Our examination of 182 proteins from the SCOP database reveals parallel tendencies between the principal eigenvectors of xmath0-matrices, xmath1-matrices, and contact number vectors. Using a statistical contact potential estimated from protein crystal structures, we evaluate pairwise residue-residue interactions and find that they are insufficient to uniquely determine native structures as the lowest energy conformations. Instead, our results suggest that other interactions, including residue connectivities and steric hindrance, are necessary to achieve this unique energy minimum. The findings of this study provide new insights into the complex interplay between contact matrices, energy matrices, and the conformational energies of native proteins.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report the groundbreaking detection of the first extrasolar planet, ET-1 (HD 102195b), utilizing the Exoplanet Tracker (ET), a state-of-the-art Doppler instrument. This pioneering discovery was made possible by the ET's innovative interferometer-based approach, which enables high-precision radial velocity measurements. The planet orbits HD 102195, a young star with solar metallicity, potentially part of the local association. Our observations reveal that the planet induces radial velocity variability with a semiamplitude of 0 m/s and a period of 4.11 days, resulting in a planetary minimum mass of 0.45  M_Jup. The detection was initially made using the Kitt Peak National Observatory (KPNO) 0.9 m Coudé feed telescope in the spring of 2005 and subsequently confirmed by radial velocity observations with the ET at the KPNO 2.1 m telescope and the 9 m Hobby-Eberly Telescope (HET) with its high-resolution spectrograph. Notably, this discovery was facilitated by the ET's high throughput of 49%, demonstrating the instrument's capability for detecting planets around relatively faint stars. Furthermore, our photometric observations using the Automated Photometric Telescopes (APTs) at Fairborn Observatory reveal that HD 102195 is a spotted variable star, with an amplitude of 0.02 mag and a 4.08 day period. These findings are consistent with spectroscopically observed Ca II H and K emission levels and line broadening measurements, ruling out rotational modulation of surface activity as the cause of the radial velocity variability. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the ET concept and its potential for future multiple-object Doppler observations or high-precision observations with a cross-dispersed echelle spectrograph.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the results of a long-term spectral monitoring of the unique double pulsar binary PSR J0737-3039, conducted through two large programs using XMM-Newton in 2006 and 2011. Over a five-year period, despite significant relativistic spin precession, no evident spectral variability was observed in the soft X-ray emission of the pulsars. Notably, our analysis reveals, for the first time, evidence of hard X-ray emission from the system in the 5-10 keV energy band. By combining standard spectral analysis with energy-dependent spatial analysis, we confirm an excess that is likely attributed to iron line emission. The detection of the Fe Kα emission line at 6.4 keV is unprecedented in non-accreting binary systems and suggests the presence of a relic disk that survived the supernova explosions of the double pulsar's stellar progenitors. This finding supports speculation about the existence of similar structures around other isolated neutron stars, offering new insights into the evolution and properties of these enigmatic systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper investigates cross-layer resource optimization in OFDM systems without explicit channel state information at the base station (CSIT), instead relying on ACK/NACK feedback flows. Conventional cross-layer designs require CSIT, which is challenging to obtain in practice. We model the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and derive a simple, closed-form solution that is asymptotically optimal for sufficiently small target packet error rates (PER). The proposed solution has low complexity, making it suitable for real-time implementation. Our approach achieves significant performance gains compared to systems that do not utilize ACK/NACK feedback for cross-layer designs or those that rely on unreliable CSIT with mismatched error statistics. Asymptotic analysis provides valuable design insights, highlighting the benefits of our method. By adapting power, rate, and user allocation based on feedback, our solution enhances system capacity without requiring explicit CSIT. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of leveraging ACK/NACK feedback for cross-layer optimization in OFDM systems, offering a promising alternative to traditional CSIT-based approaches. Overall, this work contributes to the development of efficient and practical cross-layer scheduling techniques for modern wireless communication systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the representation of a simply connected exponential solvable Lie group induced from a unitary character of a closed connected subgroup. We investigate the spectrum's correspondence to coadjoint orbits and prove that the spectral measure's absolute continuity is equivalent to the subgroup acting freely on a point. A corollary establishes a condition for admissible vectors in nonunimodular groups, providing new insights into the orbital condition's role in representation theory, with implications for the Plancherel measure and spectral variety, shedding light on the intricate relationships between these concepts in Lie group representations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study utilizes the Advanced Camera for Surveys aboard the Hubble Space Telescope to investigate the debris disk surrounding the F2V star HD 15745. The circumstellar disk is observed between 2.0 and 7.5 arcseconds radius, corresponding to 128-1480 AU. Notably, the disk exhibits an asymmetric morphology, resembling a fan, which is consistent with forward scattering grains in an optically thin disk inclined at 26-73 degrees to our line of sight. Modeling the spectral energy distribution and scattered light morphology suggests a disk composed of silicate grains between 60 and 450 AU, with a total dust mass of 4 × 10^-3 M⊕. The star's galactic space motions are similar to those of the Castor moving group, implying an age of approximately 210 ± 70 million years, although further research is necessary to confirm the age of HD 15745 using alternative indicators.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines a remarkable class of high-redshift objects, specifically extended Lyα emission-line blobs, discovered in an over-dense region at redshift 3.1. Observations at submillimeter wavelengths reveal a spectral energy distribution similar to that of Arp 220, a local ultraluminous starburst galaxy. This similarity suggests that the superwind model is applicable to these Lyα blobs, implying a dust-enshrouded, extreme starburst galaxy with a large-scale galactic outflow. Notably, the blob's infrared luminosity exceeds that of Arp 220 by a factor of 30, indicating a new population of hyperwind galaxies at high redshift. Our findings support the superwind scenario proposed by Taniguchi & Shioya, providing insights into the formation and evolution of galaxies in the early universe. The discovery of these hyperwind galaxies sheds new light on the extreme star-forming processes occurring at high redshifts.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the electronics and data acquisition system of the DS-50 experiment, a direct search for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS). The experiment utilizes a 50 kg dual-phase liquid argon Time Projection Chamber (TPC) embedded in water and liquid scintillator veto detectors. The TPC is equipped with 38 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to detect the light emitted from nuclear excitation due to WIMP-nuclear collisions. The veto detectors, instrumented with PMTs, shield the TPC and identify background events caused by cosmogenic and local radioactivity. The system triggers, data flow synchronization, and event building for both the TPC and veto detectors are described in detail. All PMT signals are digitized and transferred to event building computers running the artdaq software, allowing for efficient data acquisition and analysis. The described system enables the DS-50 experiment to effectively search for evidence of WIMP-nuclear collisions, providing valuable insights into the nature of dark matter. The implementation of this system demonstrates the capabilities of modern detection technologies in the pursuit of rare and elusive physics events.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the wave propagation in a two-layered medium comprising a homogeneous compressible air or fluid overlying a homogeneous isotropic elastic solid, with an unbounded rough surface at the interface. We conduct a time-domain analysis of the acoustic-elastic interaction problem in three dimensions, utilizing an exact transparent boundary condition and suitable interface conditions. By coupling the Helmholtz equation and the Navier equation, we establish the well-posedness and stability of the reduced initial-boundary value problem. Our proof employs the method of energy, the Lax-Milgram lemma, and the inversion theorem of the Laplace transform. Furthermore, we derive a priori estimates with explicit time dependence for the acoustic pressure and elastic displacement by selecting special test functions for the time-domain variational problem. These estimates provide valuable insights into the behavior of the acoustic and elastic waves in this complex medium, shedding light on the stability and dynamics of the system.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: Enhanced Sensitivity for Pulsar Detection in Supernova Remnants with the GLAST Large Area Telescope

Abstract:
The detection of at least three pulsars in supernova remnants by the Energetic Gamma Ray Experiment Telescope (EGRET) on the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory at energies above 100 MeV has sparked significant interest in the gamma-ray emission from these objects. However, efforts to identify additional pulsars in the EGRET data have been hindered by limited statistics. The upcoming GLAST Large Area Telescope (LAT) promises to revolutionize the field with its enhanced effective area, narrower point-spread function, and larger field of view. These improvements will increase the photon detection rate and enable better discrimination of diffuse interstellar emission, leading to more sensitive pulsation searches. The LAT's capabilities will also facilitate the resolution of point sources from extended emission in supernova remnants, allowing for a more precise understanding of the associations between gamma-ray sources and supernova remnants. Furthermore, ongoing multiwavelength studies will provide targeted candidate sources for gamma-ray investigation, maximizing the discovery potential of the GLAST LAT. With its unprecedented sensitivity and observational capabilities, the GLAST LAT is poised to make significant contributions to our understanding of pulsars and supernova remnants in the gamma-ray regime.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents an analysis of 55 distant luminous infrared galaxies (LIRGs) selected from the ISOCAM deep survey fields. Utilizing high-quality optical spectra from VLT/FORS2, we derive oxygen abundances and extinction coefficients with sufficient accuracy. The extinction coefficient is estimated through two independent methods: the Balmer-line ratio and the energy balance between infrared and Hα luminosities. The results show a median extinction coefficient of 2.36 and oxygen abundances ranging from 8.36 to 8.93, with a median value of 8.67. This is 0.5 lower than that of local bright disks at the given magnitude. Our findings suggest that a significant fraction of distant large disks are LIRGs, which could have formed a substantial portion of their metals and stellar masses recently. The results provide insights into the chemical evolution and star formation history of these galaxies, highlighting the importance of accurate extinction corrections and moderate-resolution spectroscopy in deriving reliable metal abundances. The study contributes to our understanding of the properties and evolution of LIRGs, shedding light on the role of these galaxies in the cosmic context.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a detailed analysis of observations of the low-mass X-ray binary 2S0921-63, obtained using the gratings and CCDs on Chandra and XMM. This high-inclination system exhibits evidence of an accretion disk corona (ADC), which offers valuable insights into the properties of the heated accretion disk. Our study reveals line emission consistent with previous findings, with the detection of additional lines. Notably, we identify multiple components of the iron K line, a first for this source. By fitting the spectra to photoionization models, we derive constraints on line widths, velocity offsets, and the flux in the medium-ionization region of the ADC. Utilizing density constraints from the O VII line ratio, we estimate the location of the emitting region. Our results suggest that the intrinsic luminosity of the source is comparable to the observed luminosity, under various assumptions about the source's luminosity. These findings, combined with estimates of the emission measure, favor a scenario where the ADC is a significant contributor to the system's overall emission. This study provides new insights into the properties of ADCs in low-mass X-ray binaries, with implications for our understanding of accretion processes in these systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a comprehensive study of exclusive semileptonic decays of heavy mesons to light mesons within the framework of heavy quark effective field theory. Transition matrix elements are characterized by a set of wave functions, independent of heavy quark mass, and form factors are calculated using the light cone sum rule method. Branching ratios are evaluated, and symmetry breaking effects are investigated. Comparisons are made with predictions from other approaches, including large energy effective theory. Our results provide insight into the dynamics of heavy-to-light transitions, shedding light on the interplay between heavy quark and light flavor symmetries. The calculations are performed at leading order of the heavy quark expansion, offering a systematic and consistent treatment of these decays.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present the discovery of an edge-on debris disk surrounding the 17 Myr old A-type member HD 110058 of the Scorpius-Centaurus OB association, using VLT/Sphere near-infrared dual-band imaging and integral field spectroscopy. The disk is traced to a projected separation of approximately 65 AU, with two prominent, bright, and symmetrically placed knots at 32 AU from the star in its northern and southern wings. These knots are interpreted as a ring of planetesimals, whose collisions may produce the observed dust. Notably, the disk exhibits symmetric, hook-like features in both wings, but lacks a bow-shaped structure. We propose that this wing-tilt asymmetry is indicative of an outer planetesimal belt inclined with respect to the disk midplane or radiation-pressure-driven dust blown out from an unseen, inner belt. The misalignment of the inner or outer disk may be a result of interaction with an unseen planet. The disk's geometry bears resemblance to the nearby Beta Pictoris disk, albeit at smaller radial scales. This discovery provides insights into the complex architecture and dynamics of debris disks, highlighting the potential for planet-disk interactions and the importance of high-resolution imaging and spectroscopy in understanding these systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the concept of utilizing a time-dependent dissipative environment to manipulate the quantum state of a two-level atom. By modulating the frequency and coupling strength of microscopic reservoir modes, while maintaining a fixed reservoir structure, we demonstrate the possibility of dynamically decoupling the atom from its environment. Notably, this decoupling can occur even when the atom and environment remain resonant, resulting in Markovian dynamics. The environmental modulation leads to a sideband structure in the reservoir occupation spectrum, with peaks separated by the modulation frequency. A key outcome of this approach is the significant reduction in spontaneous emission rates, surpassing that achievable through oscillatory atom-bath detuning with identical parameters. Our findings highlight the potential of time-dependent dissipative environments as a tool for quantum control, enabling the manipulation of atomic states in a controlled and efficient manner. This has implications for quantum information processing and related applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines boson stars and black holes within the framework of scalar electrodynamics, incorporating a V-shaped scalar potential. Two distinct types of boson stars emerge, characterized by either ball-like or shell-like charge density distributions. An in-depth analysis of these solutions reveals their properties and existence domains. Notably, when mass and charge are equal, a throat-like structure forms in the spacetime. Shell-like solutions may not always be globally regular, potentially possessing a horizon, thereby giving rise to a composite spacetime comprising a Schwarzschild-type black hole surrounded by a shell of charged matter, enclosed within a Reissner-Nordström-type exterior. These findings challenge black hole uniqueness, and a mass formula is derived, relating the mass of black hole solutions to that of regular shell-like solutions, analogous to the isolated horizon framework. The implications of these results on our understanding of black hole physics are discussed.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study extends our previous research on the Parker-Shearing instability by conducting numerical simulations of magnetic flux tube dynamics in the thin flux-tube approximation. Our results indicate that the evolution of flux tubes in numerical simulations closely resembles linear solutions when vertical displacements are less than the vertical scale height of the galactic disc. However, when vertical displacements approach the scale height, nonlinear effects dominate, leading to rapid inflation of the flux tube and eventual singularity in simulations that only account for cosmic rays. We also investigate the impact of a nonuniform external medium, finding that the dominant wavelength of the Parker instability aligns with the wavelength of external medium modulations. This has significant implications for the dynamo α-effect, which is substantially more efficient for short-wavelength modulations than for long-wavelength modes. Furthermore, our simulations demonstrate that differential forces arising from differential rotation and density waves amplify the α-effect in spiral arms while diminishing it in interarm regions, corroborating our previous linear approximation findings. These results provide new insights into the complex interplay between magnetic flux tubes, cosmic rays, and galactic dynamics, shedding light on the nonlinear behavior of the Parker-Shearing instability and its role in shaping the magnetic structure of galaxies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a novel bi-objective minimization model (BOMM) for inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from experimental data. The BOMM simultaneously minimizes the fitting error of derivatives and the number of connections in the network. To efficiently solve the BOMM, a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) is proposed, combined with the separable parameter estimation method (SPEM) to decouple the ordinary differential equation (ODE) system. The Akaike information criterion (AIC) is then used to select the optimal inference result from the obtained Pareto set. Applying this method to the S-system GRN model, our approach accurately identifies network topologies and parameter values without requiring pre-set problem-dependent parameters. This versatility makes our method applicable to inferring various GRN models, addressing a significant challenge in bioinformatics and providing a valuable tool for understanding complex biological systems. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the reionization history of the universe, exploring the impact of various astrophysical and cosmological factors on this pivotal process. We calculate the reionization history for different stellar population models, incorporating the effects of primordial magnetic fields, dark matter decay, and dark matter annihilation. Our results indicate that stellar populations based on a Scalo-type initial mass function for Population II stars are insufficient to drive reionization, unless high star formation efficiencies or photon escape fractions are assumed. The presence of primordial magnetic fields significantly influences the thermal evolution and ionization history of the post-recombination universe, with the magnetic Jeans mass altering the characteristic mass scale of star-forming halos. We derive upper limits to the magnetic field strength and constrain the thermally averaged cross section for dark matter annihilation and the lifetime of dark matter particles. Our findings provide independent confirmation of existing constraints from the recombination era, offering valuable insights into the complex interplay of processes shaping the universe's reionization history. By exploring these factors, our research contributes to a deeper understanding of the universe's evolution, highlighting the importance of considering multiple astrophysical and cosmological components in models of reionization.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a novel modeling approach to understand the complex structure and chemistry of molecular clouds, treating them as ensembles of transient cores. Each core undergoes a lifecycle of growth, densification, and decay, influencing the surrounding gas and dust. The chemical composition within each core responds to its dynamic state and interactions with dust grains, leading to the formation of ices that are subsequently returned to the gas phase as the core expands. Our models, comprising approximately 1000 cores with random positions and evolutionary phases, are used to simulate molecular line emission maps of a dark cloud. The resulting maps exhibit striking similarities to observations of the dark cloud L673, replicating key features such as morphology, emitting region sizes, molecular column densities, and peak emission separations. By comparing our models to observational data, we gain valuable insights into the dynamics and chemical processes governing molecular clouds, providing significant constraints on the interstellar medium. This work offers a powerful tool for understanding the intricate relationships between gas, dust, and chemistry in these complex systems, shedding light on the nature of molecular clouds and their role in the universe.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the parametric estimation of the driving Lévy process in a multivariate continuous-time autoregressive moving average (MCARMA) process observed at discrete time intervals. A novel state space representation is developed to exactly recover the driving Lévy process from continuous observations of the MCARMA process. By leveraging numerical analysis and infinitely divisible distributions, this approach is extended to approximate the recovery of unit increments from discrete-time observations. Theoretical results demonstrate that when the sampling interval is chosen appropriately, a generalized method of moments estimator based on reconstructed unit increments achieves the same asymptotic distribution as one using true increments, yielding asymptotic normality. This finding has significant implications for statistical inference in MCARMA models, enabling accurate estimation and inference from discrete-time data. The methodology developed in this article provides a foundation for further research in this area.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the impact of two-body nucleon-nucleon correlations on heavy-ion collision signatures. We investigate the effects of these correlations on various quantities, including particle production fluctuations, @xmath0 fluctuations, and size fluctuations. Our results indicate that while particle production fluctuations are influenced, other quantities remain unaffected by the presence of nucleon-nucleon correlations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that fluctuations in the transverse size of the initial source lead to fluctuations in the transverse flow velocity at hadronic freeze-out, resulting in event-by-event fluctuations of the transverse momentum of produced particles, @xmath1. Notably, our findings suggest that nearly all observed event-by-event @xmath1 fluctuations can be attributed to this mechanism, providing a comprehensive understanding of the underlying dynamics. These results have significant implications for our understanding of heavy-ion collisions and the role of nucleon-nucleon correlations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study delves into the realm of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) and entropic uncertainty relations, crucial components of quantum cryptographic protocols. Despite their importance, these concepts remain poorly understood. Here, we construct special sets of up to $n$ MUBs in dimension $d$ with notable symmetry properties derived from the Clifford algebra. A unitary transformation is identified, which cyclically permutes these bases, generalizing the Fourier transform to multiple complementary aspects. We establish a lower bound for min-entropic uncertainty relations for any set of MUBs, highlighting the central role of symmetry in achieving tight bounds. Notably, a tight bound is obtained for four MUBs in dimension $d=4$, achieved by an eigenstate of our complementarity transform. The relationship between these symmetries and those obtained through discrete phase space transformations is explored, revealing a connection between the extrema of discrete Wigner functions and min-entropic uncertainty relations for MUBs, shedding new light on the underlying principles.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Here is an abstract of approximately 200 words based on the provided title:

We report the results of an extensive photometric study of V4743 Sgr (Nova Sgr 2002 #3) conducted over 11 nights in 2003 and 2005 using CCD unfiltered photometry. Our analysis reveals two distinct periodicities in the 2005 data: 0.2799 days (approximately 6.7 hours) and 0.01642 days (approximately 24 minutes). While the longer period is also evident in the 2003 data, the shorter period is only weakly detected in that year. Notably, the 24-minute period is slightly longer than the 22-minute period previously identified in X-ray observations. We interpret the 6.7-hour periodicity as the orbital period of the underlying binary system and propose that the 24-minute period represents the beat frequency between the orbital period and the X-ray period, which is likely the spin period of the white dwarf. This classification suggests that V4743 Sgr is an intermediate polar (DQ Her star). Furthermore, our findings support the hypothesis that the transition phase in novae may be related to intermediate polars, as evidenced by the presence of quasi-periodic oscillations in the optical light curve approximately six months after the nova outburst.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a phenomenological model for the 0.7 conductance feature in quantum point contacts. Our model, focusing on finite source-drain bias transconductance, deviates from single-particle expectations. Comparison with experimental data from ultra-low-disorder GaAs systems shows good agreement.
