This simple phenomenology establishes key boundary conditions for a microscopic theory, shedding light on quantum wire behavior near zero bias.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article proposes an extension of Gauss-Bonnet gravity to an energy-dependent theory, dubbed Gauss-Bonnet gravity's rainbow, and couples it with Maxwell's theory. We investigate black hole solutions within this framework and calculate the resulting modifications to their thermodynamics. Our analysis reveals that although the thermodynamics are altered, the first law of thermodynamics remains valid. Furthermore, we examine the thermal stability of black hole solutions in this theory, providing insights into the behavior of these gravitational systems. The energy-dependent Gauss-Bonnet gravity's rainbow offers a novel perspective on black hole physics, with potential implications for our understanding of gravitational phenomena and the interplay between gravity, electromagnetism, and thermodynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article introduces Galamost, a novel GPU-accelerated molecular simulation toolkit designed to harness the computational power of graphics processing units. Galamost is specifically tailored for the study of polymeric systems at the mesoscopic scale, focusing on self-assembly, phase transition, and other properties. The toolkit employs a hybrid particle-field molecular dynamics technique, replacing particle-particle interactions with interactions between particles and density fields, enabling accelerated simulations. Additionally, Galamost incorporates numerical potentials obtained through bottom-up coarse-graining methods, allowing for the simulation of large system sizes over extended periods. The toolkit also features two specialized models: a soft anisotropic particle model and a chain-growth polymerization model, facilitating the investigation of hierarchical self-assembly and polymerization-related phenomena. This article provides a detailed overview of Galamost's optimized algorithms, package characteristics, and benchmarking results, highlighting its potential for efficient and accurate simulations of complex polymeric systems. By leveraging GPU acceleration, Galamost offers a powerful tool for researchers to explore the behavior of polymers at the mesoscopic scale, advancing our understanding of these complex systems. The toolkit's capabilities and applications are discussed, demonstrating its value for the scientific community.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a theoretical description of central exclusive @xmath0 production in proton-proton collisions. The feasibility of measuring this process using the ATLAS detector and ALFA stations during low-luminosity LHC runs is explored. An estimated visible cross section of 21 @xmath1b at @xmath2 TeV is reported, yielding over 2000 events for 100 @xmath1b@xmath3 of integrated luminosity. Differential distributions of kinematic variables are also examined, providing insight into the production mechanism.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores energy level crossings in the one-dimensional Hubbard model using the Bethe ansatz, building upon the work of Heilmann and Lieb. By constructing degenerate eigenstates at crossing points, we verify level crossings observed through numerical diagonalization with one down-spin. Our numerical solutions to the Lieb-Wu equations enable the construction of Bethe ansatz eigenstates, allowing us to track energy spectral flows along the interaction parameter. Notably, some level crossings cannot be explained by symmetries independent of the interaction parameter, highlighting the importance of dynamical symmetries in identifying spectral lines. We demonstrate that degenerate Bethe ansatz eigenstates at crossing points have distinct eigenvalues of higher conserved operators. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a twofold permanent degeneracy in terms of the Bethe ansatz wavefunction, providing new insights into the Hubbard model's spectral properties and the role of dynamical symmetries in shaping its energy landscape.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates chromospheric swirls, rotational features in the solar atmosphere associated with magnetic tornadoes. These swirls appear as dark, rotating structures in the Ca II 854.2 nm spectral line, often subtle and challenging to detect amidst dynamic chromospheric changes. To develop a systematic detection method, we compiled and characterized a statistically significant sample of observed and simulated swirls. Our research provides a refined definition of chromospheric swirls and introduces a morphological classification system comprising three types: ring, split, and spiral. We also examine the underlying magnetic field structures and the impact of limited spatial resolution on their photospheric footpoints. This work aims to enhance our understanding of magnetic tornadoes and their role in the solar atmosphere, ultimately contributing to a more comprehensive model of solar dynamics and magnetic field evolution. Our findings have significant implications for solar physics research.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the startup of the PSI UCN source, a new user facility at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The source provides ultracold neutrons for fundamental physics research, enabling detailed studies of neutron properties. Completed in December 2010, the facility produced its first ultracold neutrons and received operational approval in June 2011. We provide an overview of the source and its initial status, highlighting its potential for groundbreaking research in neutron physics, with capabilities to store and observe ultracold neutrons for hundreds of seconds, advancing our understanding of the neutron's fundamental properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: In this paper, we propose a novel approach to describing the evolution of the universe by utilizing the group analysis of symmetries of dynamical systems. This methodology is employed to search for the unknown equation of state, particularly in the context of noninteracting scaling multifluids. Our results demonstrate that the group of symmetries constrains the form of the equation of state, yielding a commonly used expression in cosmology. We apply this framework to the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) model filled with a scaling fluid, known as a homological fluid, and confront it with observations of distant Type Ia supernovae. Statistical analysis of the supernovae data reveals a class of admissible model parameters, and we find that the model with scaling fluid provides a good fit to the data. The estimated parameters suggest a universe with high density, potentially corresponding to (hyper) phantom fluid. However, assuming a prior on the equation of state parameter, our results indicate a preference for a model close to the concordance ΛCDM model. Notably, our predictions imply that distant Type Ia supernovae should appear brighter, while intermediate distant supernovae should appear fainter, compared to the ΛCDM model. Furthermore, using the Akaike model selection criterion, we find that the model with noninteracting scaling fluid is preferred over the ΛCDM model, offering a promising alternative for understanding the evolution of the universe.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the mechanism of pattern formation in systems described by a reaction-diffusion equation coupled with ordinary differential equations, which model interactions between cellular processes and diffusing growth factors. Focusing on the Marciniak-Czochra and Kimmel model of early carcinogenesis, we investigate the emergence of periodic and irregular spike patterns due to diffusion-driven instability. Utilizing a numerical code based on the finite element method and adaptive mesh, our simulations demonstrate the formation of nonstationary structures that asymptotically tend towards the sum of Dirac deltas. This novel pattern formation phenomenon is characterized by the concentration of mass at specific points, indicating a potential mechanism for the development of heterogeneous patterns in biological systems. Our findings contribute to the understanding of pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems, with implications for the study of early carcinogenesis and other biological processes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the X-ray emission line profiles observed in the XMM-Newton RGS spectrum of the OI star ζ Puppis using radiative transfer in a clumped wind. The results indicate that the X-ray spectrum can be attributed to a multi-temperature collisional plasma situated in the wind acceleration zone. The X-rays are attenuated in the clumped stellar wind, yielding distinctive profiles for the emergent lines. A detailed analysis of the NVII emission line reveals a structured profile, which is attributed to self-absorption in the hot plasma. The presence of NVII in the cool wind component is ruled out based on the atmosphere model. Furthermore, the impact of wind clumping on the transfer of ionizing radiation in high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) is investigated, and analytical formulae for the ionization parameter are derived in relation to wind clumping parameters. These findings provide insights into the complex radiative processes in stellar winds.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the results of a BeppoSAX observation of the nearby starburst galaxy NGC 253. The X-ray emission from this galaxy is found to be largely concentrated in the nuclear region. Analysis of the 0.2-60 keV data from the central region reveals a continuum that can be well-fitted by two thermal models: a soft component with a temperature of approximately 0.5 keV and a hard component with a temperature of around 3 keV, absorbed by a column density of 1.2 x 10^22 cm^-2. Notably, the Fe K line at 6.7 keV is detected for the first time in this object, with an equivalent width of 300 eV. This detection, along with the shape of the 2-60 keV continuum, suggests that the hard X-ray emission is primarily thermal in origin. The iron abundance of this component is constrained to be approximately 0.25 of solar. Other detected lines include Si, S, and Fe L/Ne, consistent with previous ASCA results. These findings are discussed within the framework of the starburst-driven galactic superwind model, providing new insights into the X-ray properties of this galaxy.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article challenges the traditional worst-case approach to evaluating covertness in covert communication with noise uncertainty. Instead, we consider the distribution of noise uncertainty to statistically assess covertness. New metrics are defined to measure covertness, enabling analysis of maximum achievable rates under bounded and unbounded noise uncertainty models. Our approach provides a more realistic evaluation of physical layer security, offering insights into covert communication systems' performance under various noise conditions, ultimately enhancing the design of secure communication systems with stringent covertness requirements and noise uncertainty considerations. Novel metrics and models are introduced.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We investigate deep inelastic scattering in the saturation region, governed by non-linear Wilson-line operator evolution. The BK equation describes color dipole evolution in the leading logarithmic approximation. At next-to-leading order, quark and gluon loops contribute, along with tree gluon diagrams. This study calculates the gluon contribution to small-x Wilson line evolution, complementing earlier quark part results, to refine understanding of high-energy QCD dynamics and saturation phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper presents a novel approach to evaluating the suitability of alternative formulations of Einstein's evolution equations. Rather than searching for well-behaved formulations, we develop analytical tools to identify those that are particularly ill-behaved, exhibiting rapid growth of constraint-violating errors. By examining the amplification of transients in the future domain of dependence of the initial data slice, we can eliminate formulations with unacceptable numerical behavior. This technique has the potential to impose stringent constraints on the set of applicable formulations. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we apply our method to the 2-parameter family of evolution equations proposed by Kidder, Scheel, and Teukolsky, considering both flat space in Rindler coordinates and Schwarzschild space in Painleve-Gullstrand coordinates. Our results provide valuable insights into the stability and reliability of these formulations, highlighting the potential of this approach to guide the development of robust numerical relativity simulations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the structural, electronic, and energetic properties of corundum grain boundaries (GBs) and their role in ion diffusion, a crucial phenomenon in stainless steel corrosion. Using density functional theory (DFT+U) calculations, we constructed four GB planes (rhombohedral, basal, prismatic, and pyramidal) with various interface symmetries. Our results show that the prismatic screw GB with a Cr-O plane interface is the most energetically preferred, followed by the rhombohedral GB with screw symmetry and Cr vacancy termination. The stability of the prismatic GB is enhanced by an increase in in-plane Cr atoms at the interface, as evident in the electronic density of states. These findings provide valuable insights into the preferred interfaces within corundum and their implications for oxide layer growth on stainless steel, ultimately informing strategies to mitigate corrosion. Theoretical understanding of GB properties can guide the development of corrosion-resistant materials.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report the first observation of the @xmath2, @xmath3 process using @xmath0 @xmath1 events from the BESIII detector at BEPCII. The significance is @xmath4 (@xmath5 with systematic uncertainties). The product branching fraction of @xmath6 is measured as @xmath7. This result enhances understanding of @xmath8 production and @xmath1 decay dynamics to four-body processes, providing insight into near-threshold coupling to @xmath9.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
The primordial lithium abundance inferred from spectroscopic observations of metal-poor stars is significantly lower than the theoretical prediction in the standard Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) model. This discrepancy, known as the lithium problem, has been a long-standing issue in cosmology. In an effort to resolve this problem, we investigate the effects of a sterile neutrino decay on the primordial lithium abundance. We assume a simple model consisting of standard model particles and a sterile neutrino with a mass of a few MeV, which decays long after BBN. The decay of the sterile neutrino produces energetic active neutrinos and electrons, which can induce non-thermal nucleosynthesis and affect the primordial abundance of light elements.

We derive the injection spectrum of non-thermal photons induced by the sterile neutrino decay, taking into account the generation of electrons and positrons, muons, and active neutrinos, as well as the primary photon production via inverse Compton scattering of cosmic background radiation (CBR) by energetic electrons. The steady-state injection spectrum is then derived as a function of the sterile neutrino mass and the photon temperature. We find that the sterile neutrino decay can produce energetic active neutrinos that are not thermalized, as well as electrons that are thermalized.

To determine the effects of the sterile neutrino decay on the primordial lithium abundance, we consistently solve the cosmic thermal history, non-thermal nucleosynthesis, and the baryon-to-photon ratio and effective neutrino number. We find that an effective destruction of 7Be can occur only if the sterile neutrino decays at a photon temperature of around 0.3 keV. The amounts of energy injection at the sterile neutrino decay are constrained by limits on primordial D and 6Li abundances, the effective neutrino number, and the CBR energy spectrum.

Our results indicate that 7Be can be photodisintegrated, and the lithium problem can be partially solved for a sterile neutrino lifetime of around 1000 s and a mass of around 5 MeV. However, 7Be destruction by more than a factor of three is not possible due to an associated over-destruction of D. In the parameter region, the baryon-to-photon ratio is decreased slightly, while the effective neutrino number is increased by a factor of around 0.1. We also correct errors in photodisintegration cross sections of 7Be and 6Li that have propagated through the literature and derive new functions based on recent nuclear experiments. The correct cross sections indicate significantly smaller efficiencies of 7Be and 6Li photodisintegration, which implies that the abundances of sterile neutrino necessary for the 6Li reduction are much smaller than thermal freeze-out abundances. Therefore, the relic sterile neutrino must be diluted between the freeze-out and BBN epochs by some mechanism. Our study provides a new perspective on the lithium problem and highlights the importance of considering non-standard cosmological scenarios in resolving this long-standing issue.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a novel measurement of the iron-to-hydrogen abundance ratio in the solar corona, utilizing a distinct approach that deviates from traditional spectroscopic and solar wind measurements. By combining EUV line data from the CDS spectrometer on SOHO with thermal bremsstrahlung radio data from the VLA, we derive the coronal iron abundance. Our method involves equating calculated and observed thermal bremsstrahlung radio emission, treating the iron-to-hydrogen abundance as the sole unknown. Applying this technique to a compact cool active region yields an iron-to-hydrogen abundance ratio of 1.56 ± 0.10, approximately four times its photospheric value. Uncertainties in calibration, intensity measurements, atomic parameters, and spectral analysis assumptions result in a net uncertainty of ±20%. These findings suggest that low first ionization potential elements, such as iron, are enhanced in the solar corona relative to photospheric values, providing new insights into coronal composition and dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents an optimization of rateless codes for unequal error protection (UEP) in multimedia multicasting applications. The proposed design aims to provide either guaranteed or best-effort quality of service (QoS) to a set of heterogeneous users. A novel randomly interleaved rateless encoder is introduced, allowing users to decode symbols up to their own QoS level. The encoder is optimized based on the transmission properties of standardized Raptor codes over wireless channels. By formulating the guaranteed QoS problem as a convex optimization problem, a globally optimal solution is obtained. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed optimized UEP rateless coder, outperforming other recently proposed UEP rateless codes. The findings of this study have significant implications for efficient and flexible multimedia transmission, particularly in wireless environments where error control and QoS are crucial. The proposed approach enables enhanced video transmission and reception.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present predictions of Lyman-alpha (Lyα) forest-galaxy correlations at z=3 from Eulerian simulations that incorporate the effects of galactic winds driven by supernova explosions. These simulations reveal that galactic winds produce expanding bubbles of shock-heated gas within 1-2 comoving megaparsecs of luminous galaxies, akin to observed Lyman break galaxies (LBGs). However, the majority of low-density intergalactic gas, which dictates the observed properties of the Lyα forest, remains unaffected by winds. Our analysis shows that the impact of winds on Lyα optical depth near galaxies is relatively subdued, as winds only heat a small fraction of the gas in the surrounding regions. Consequently, Lyα absorption from gas outside the wind bubbles is dispersed over the same velocity range as the wind-heated gas. Notably, Lyα absorption is expected to be stronger near galaxies due to high gas density, with winds resulting in a modest reduction of this increase. These predictions can be compared to future observations to detect wind effects and infer their strength, albeit with the caveat that the results depend on the correspondence between simulated galaxies and observed LBGs. Our simulations suggest that wind effects are insufficient to reproduce the high Lyα transmission observed within 0.5 comoving megaparsecs of galaxies, implying that more powerful galactic explosions or ejecta with hyper-escape velocities may be necessary, which are unlikely to be produced by ordinary star formation and supernovae alone.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a systematic approach to constructing graphs associated with binary stabilizer codes. Our scheme involves three key steps: realizing the stabilizer code as a codeword-stabilized quantum code, determining its canonical form, and attaching input vertices to the graph. We demonstrate the scheme's effectiveness by constructing graphs for various stabilizer codes with single and multi-qubit encoding operators. The error-correcting capabilities of these codes are verified using graph-theoretic methods. Our results align with the work of Schlingemann and Werner, and we discuss potential extensions of our scheme to nonbinary, nonadditive, and continuous-variable quantum codes, highlighting its versatility and potential for broader applications in quantum coding theory.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the production of the composite Higgs boson in topcolor models through the gluon fusion process, incorporating the effects of color-octet massive gauge bosons, known as colorons, and nonstandard contributions from the top-Yukawa coupling and heavy colored fermions. By deriving a low-energy effective theory, we examine the contribution of colorons to the effective gluon-gluon-Higgs operator and find its coefficient to be proportional to the ratio of the coloron mass to the dynamically generated mass. Our analysis reveals that the coloron contribution can be comparable to the top-loop effect for specific parameter values, particularly in top-seesaw models where a large dynamical mass can be achieved consistently with the experimental top quark mass. In contrast, topcolor assisted technicolor models exhibit enhancement of the top-Yukawa coupling. We demonstrate that the coloron contribution can dominate the real part of the Higgs boson amplitude for a Higgs mass of approximately 1 TeV, while the top-loop contribution dominates the imaginary part. Furthermore, we show that signatures of the Higgs boson can be observed in topcolor assisted technicolor models at the Tevatron Run II and the LHC, with estimated cross sections for an integrated luminosity of 2 fb^-1 and a center-of-mass energy of 1.96 TeV. Our results highlight the potential for discovering the composite Higgs boson in topcolor models and emphasize the importance of considering nonstandard contributions in the gluon fusion process.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study systematically investigates the temperature-dependent thermal conductivities of one-dimensional nonlinear Klein-Gordon lattices with soft on-site potential (soft-KG). The existence of renormalized phonons in soft-KG lattices is confirmed, and their temperature-dependent frequency is verified through numerical simulations and classical field theory. Notably, the thermal conductivities of soft-KG lattices exhibit an opposite temperature dependence trend compared to hard-KG lattices. However, both types of lattices can be interpreted within the framework of effective phonon theory, which predicts that the exponents of the power-law dependence of thermal conductivities on temperature are determined by the exponents of the on-site potentials. Extensive numerical simulations consistently verify these theoretical predictions, providing a unified understanding of thermal transport in soft- and hard-KG lattices. The findings of this study contribute to the understanding of thermal conductivity in nonlinear lattice systems and highlight the importance of effective phonon theory in interpreting thermal transport phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report on a search for near-infrared emission from baryonic dark matter in the form of low-mass stars and/or brown dwarfs in the halo of the nearby edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 5907. Utilizing a 256x256 InSb array with a pixel scale of 1.7" on a liquid-helium-cooled telescope carried by a sounding rocket, we conducted observations in the 3.5-5 μm wavelength range. Contrary to previous studies that detected a halo around NGC 5907 in various bands at galactic radii 6 kpc ≤ r ≤ 10 kpc, our search yielded no evidence for emission from a halo at 10 kpc ≤ r ≤ 30 kpc. Assuming a halo mass density that scales as r^(-3), consistent with the observed flat rotation curves out to 32 kpc, we derived a lower limit for the mass-to-light ratio at 3.5-5 μm for the halo of NGC 5907 to be 250 (2σ) in solar units. This limit is comparable to our previous finding for NGC 4565. Based on recent models, our non-detection suggests that hydrogen-burning stars contribute less than 15% of the mass of the dark halo of NGC 5907. Our results support the possibility that the previously detected extended emission at r ≥ 10 kpc is caused by a stellar population ejected from the disk due to tidal interactions. Ultimately, our findings indicate that the dark halo of NGC 5907, evident from extended rotation curves, is not composed of hydrogen-burning stars, providing new insights into the nature of dark matter in galaxies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the conjugacy problem for finitely generated groups, specifically the decidability of whether an arbitrary pair of elements are conjugate. We construct examples of computably presented groups where the conjugacy problem for individual elements is decidable in quadratic time, yet the global conjugacy problem exhibits arbitrary worst-case complexity. This complexity can range from any computably enumerable Turing degree to mirroring the time hierarchy theorem or being complete for a given class. Notably, these groups possess a generically linear time conjugacy problem, meaning that hard instances are rare and a linear time partial algorithm exists for a dense subset of instances. Additionally, we examine the relationship between the conjugacy problem and the "half-conjugacy" problem, and discuss groups with algorithmically finite conjugation, highlighting the extremes of conjugacy problem complexity in finitely generated groups.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study utilizes archival Chandra observations of 19 Low Ionization Nuclear Emission-line Regions (LINERs) to investigate the X-ray properties of their inner kiloparsec. The sample's composition reflects the relative numbers of LINER types found in optical spectroscopic surveys. Our analysis reveals that diffuse, thermal emission is prevalent and concentrated within the central few hundred parsec. The average spectra of the hot gas in spiral and elliptical galaxies are consistent with those of normal galaxies, and can be modeled using a thermal plasma and power law component. We detect an average of three point sources in the inner kiloparsec of each galaxy, with luminosities of approximately 10^38 erg s^-1. Notably, the cumulative luminosity functions of these sources are identical to those of normal galaxies. Our findings indicate that an Active Galactic Nucleus (AGN) is present in 12 of the 19 galaxies, contributing a median of 60% of the 0.5-10 keV luminosity in the central region. However, the AGN's ionizing luminosity is insufficient to power the observed optical emission lines, suggesting alternative power sources such as mechanical interaction between the AGN jet and circumnuclear gas, or stellar processes like photoionization by post-AGB stars or young stars. These results provide new insights into the origins of nuclear X-ray emission and the power sources of optical emission lines in LINERs, highlighting the complexity of these phenomena and the need for further investigation.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the extended Bose-Hubbard model with pure three-body local interactions using the density matrix renormalization group approach. The insulating lobes' shapes and critical tunneling values for the quantum phase transition to the superfluid phase are analyzed. Results show enhanced stability of insulating phases at larger fillings, contrasting the standard Bose-Hubbard model. The model is found to belong to the Berenzinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless universality class at the insulating phase boundary tip, providing new insights into quantum phase transitions and many-body localization in interacting bosonic systems with three-body interactions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the symmetric degrees of freedom (DoF) in partially connected interference networks with linear coding strategies and no channel state information. Using reconfigurable antennas at receivers, we identify network topologies achieving half linear symmetric DoF. A general upper bound on linear symmetric DoF is derived for arbitrary topologies. Additionally, this bound is shown to be tight for networks with transmitters having at most two co-interferers, highlighting the impact of topology on interference management and DoF. Our results provide insights into optimizing network performance with limited channel knowledge and reconfigurable antennas.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We confirm recent numerical results on gravitational collapse of a spherical Yang-Mills field by constructing critical solutions and perturbations as an eigenvalue problem. The non-scale-invariant field equations yield asymptotically self-similar solutions. Generalizing methods for discrete self-similarity, we find an echoing period and critical exponent for black hole mass, verifying numerical predictions with high accuracy, and providing insight into the complex dynamics of Yang-Mills collapse.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study employs the effective field theory approach to examine the coupled metric-inflaton system, focusing on the influence of higher dimension operators on scalar and tensor perturbation spectra at short wavelengths. Our analysis reveals that tree-level effective corrections become significant when the Hubble parameter approaches the Planck mass or when the physical wave number of a perturbation mode nears the Planck mass squared divided by the Hubble constant. Consequently, the cut-off length for conventional cosmological perturbation theory is likely much smaller than the Planck length, impacting the observability of trans-Planckian effects in primordial perturbation spectra and shedding new light on early universe dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article provides a comprehensive examination of the constitutive relation between @xmath0 and @xmath1 near @xmath2 in Type II superconductors with various types of quenched random disorder. The traditional Abrikosov result is significantly altered by the presence of disorder, with the constitutive relations depending strongly on the disorder type. We investigate point, parallel columnar, and nearly isotropically splayed disorder in both two- and three-dimensional superconductors. Our findings indicate distinct behaviors for each disorder type, including @xmath4 in three-dimensional superconductors with point disorder and @xmath5 in two-dimensional thin films. The results have implications for understanding the effects of disorder on superconductor behavior, highlighting the importance of considering disorder type in theoretical models.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a linear scaling algorithm for calculating maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs) using an atomic orbital basis. Our O(N) method involves a ground state calculation, density matrix projection, and orthogonalization, followed by Jacobi sweeps for maximal localization. Validation is demonstrated through applications to a water molecule, wurtzite ZnO, and boron nitride nanotubes, showcasing the algorithm's linear scaling behavior and efficiency in computing MLWFs for large systems, making it a valuable tool for materials science research and simulations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article reviews the geometry of super coset spaces, focusing on inherited structures from super Lie groups. The isometries of super coset spaces are examined, and a definition of Killing supervectors is provided, enabling extension to other spaces. The formulation of supersymmetric theories is informed by these geometrical insights, with implications for theoretical physics, particularly in areas described by PACS numbers 02.40.-k, 11.30.pb, and 12.60.jv.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article introduces Saturating Auto-Encoders (SATAE), a new regularizer for auto-encoders with saturated activation functions. The regularizer encourages activations in saturated regions, limiting reconstruction of inputs far from the data manifold. SATAE learns diverse features with various activation functions. Connections to contractive and sparse auto-encoders are established, demonstrating SATAE's potential in representation learning. Experimental results show SATAE's effectiveness in learning compact and informative representations, making it a valuable tool for deep learning applications, with implications for feature learning and data manifold discovery. SATAE offers a new perspective on auto-encoder regularization.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the head-on collisions of neutron stars and dust disks (galaxies) through the lens of equilibrium thermodynamics. By leveraging conservation laws and solving the Einstein equations, we calculate the final configurations resulting from initial collisions. Gravitational emission serves as a ubiquitous damping mechanism, yielding final equilibrium states. Our analysis compares initial and final states to determine the conditions under which two colliding neutron stars merge into a single entity, and two rigidly rotating disks coalesce into a differentially rotating disk of dust. Notably, we find that the maximal energy loss due to gravitational radiation for neutron star collisions is approximately 0% of the initial mass, whereas colliding disks exhibit a substantially larger limit of 1%. This study provides insights into the dynamic interplay between gravitational emission, neutron star mergers, and disk formation, shedding light on the intricate processes governing these astrophysical phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article proposes a paradigm shift in the operation of positioning systems by embracing a fully relativistic approach. Current practice relies on applying relativistic corrections to computations based on Galilean physics, whereas our approach integrates relativity from the outset. This fundamental change entails the use of four symmetric time coordinates and necessitates cross-link capabilities among satellites. Furthermore, gravitation is incorporated through the space-time metric, rather than Newtonian theory, making it impossible to separate the positioning problem from gravimetry. We develop an optimization theory that eliminates the need for relativistic corrections, providing a clearer and more simplified theoretical framework. By adopting this fully relativistic paradigm, we anticipate not only a theoretical clarification but also an improvement in positioning accuracy. Our proposed approach has the potential to revolutionize the operation of positioning satellite systems, and we recommend its implementation to enhance the performance and precision of these systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines elastic scattering in a wide range of incident energies using the four-body model and continuum-discretized coupled-channels method. The approach accurately reproduces experimental data for specific scattering reactions without adjustable parameters. Notably, breakup processes are significant and provide repulsive corrections to the folding potential. Interestingly, the breakup of a particular cluster is strongly suppressed in certain processes, regardless of incident energy. The underlying causes of this suppression are investigated, providing insight into the dynamics of these scattering reactions and the behavior of cluster breakup at various energies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a parametrisation of scattered proton transport in LHC interactions, discussing the accuracy of kinematic variable unfolding for high-luminosity runs, and describes proton-proton interaction dynamics at the LHC.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the relationship between differential calculus on metric spaces and algebraic study of normed groupoids with @xmath0-structures. We establish that differential calculus contains the algebraic study of normed groupoids, while the algebraic study of normed groups with dilatation structures is contained within differential calculus. This equivalence enables the translation of algebraic properties between these frameworks, extending beyond metric spaces through the language of groupoids. Our results provide a foundational connection between these mathematical structures, facilitating the exchange of ideas and techniques between them. Key implications are discussed.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents high-resolution, combined Submillimeter Array (SMA) and Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE) images of the Class I protobinary L1551 IRS 5 in the CS (J=7-6) line, offering the most complete spatial sampling to date. The SMA image of L1551 IRS 5 in the 343 GHz dust-continuum emission reveals an elongated feature, approximately 3160 au x 80 au in size, oriented perpendicular to the associated radio jets. The combined SMA+ASTE images demonstrate that high-velocity CS emission traces the dust component's structure and exhibits a velocity gradient along the major axis, consistent with a geometrically thin Keplerian-disk model having a central stellar mass of approximately 0.5 solar masses. Conversely, low-velocity CS emission shows an extended feature (~1000 au) with slight south-to-north emission offsets, indicative of a rotating and infalling envelope. The rotational motion of the envelope connects smoothly to the inner Keplerian rotation at a radius of ~364 au. Notably, the infalling velocity of the envelope is three times lower than the free-fall velocity towards the central stellar mass. These findings provide evidence for the transition from an infalling envelope to a Keplerian disk, aligning with recent theoretical studies on disk formation. Our results suggest that sizable Keplerian disks (~50-200 au) may already be formed during the protostellar phase, while the protostars are still deeply embedded within their envelopes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines monodromies of D-branes in Kähler moduli space, treating D-branes as derived category objects. We compute monodromies in nontrivial examples, linking our work to helices, mutations, and noting unique 0-brane properties, contributing to recent results and conjectures in the field of string compactifications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: The formation and evolution of massive galaxies in the early universe remains a topic of considerable interest. Observations have revealed that massive galaxies with a half-mass radius of approximately 0-1 kpc exist in the early universe, whereas in the local universe, galaxies of similar mass tend to be 4-5 times larger. Dry minor mergers have been proposed as a potential mechanism for driving the evolution of galaxy size without significant mass increase. However, it is unclear whether this process can fully account for the observed differences. This study investigates the role of dry minor mergers in galaxy evolution through numerical simulations of merging galaxies with mass ratios ranging from 1:1 to 1:160. Our results confirm that major mergers do not lead to sufficient size growth, while minor mergers with mass ratios between 1:5 and 1:10 can explain the observed size differences. Notably, smaller mass ratios result in more dramatic size growth, with mergers of 1:80 leading to a size increase of up to a factor of 4. Furthermore, our simulations reveal that the accretion of minor galaxies can lead to the concentration of foreign mass in the central region of the parent galaxy, particularly when the mass ratio is greater than 1:40. These findings provide new insights into the evolution of massive galaxies and highlight the importance of dry minor mergers in shaping their size and structure. Our results have significant implications for our understanding of galaxy evolution and the formation of massive galaxies in the early universe.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a comprehensive spectroscopic library of late spectral type stellar templates in the near-infrared range (2.15-2.42 μm) at a high resolution of R=5300-5900. The library is designed to support stellar kinematics studies in external galaxies, with a particular focus on determining the masses of supermassive black holes in nearby active and non-active galaxies. The combination of high spectral resolution and advanced instrumentation on 8-m class telescopes has made near-infrared CO band heads a popular technique for analyzing circumnuclear stellar kinematics. Our library provides the necessary datasets to leverage the improved spectral resolution and coverage of modern near-infrared spectrographs. We demonstrate the library's application using data from two Gemini instruments and discuss its adaptability for use with other spectrographs. Additionally, we revisit the "template mismatch" effect and its impact on velocity dispersion values obtained from fitting processes, highlighting the importance of carefully selected stellar templates. The library is made available electronically through the Gemini website, providing a valuable resource for the astronomical community to advance our understanding of galaxy evolution and supermassive black hole dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study utilizes high-resolution images from the Chandra X-ray Observatory to measure the proper motion of the neutron star in Cassiopeia A over a 10-year period (1999-2009). By registering two images using a background source and 13 quasi-stationary flocculi, pixel offsets were measured using four statistical methods: Gaussian fitting, centroiding, cross correlation, and the Cash statistic. However, significant discrepancies were found between the offset measurements, resulting in large uncertainties. Consequently, the detected motion of the neutron star is marginal, at 390 ± 400 km/s in the southeast direction. Despite the uncertainty, this motion is consistent with the birth velocities of young pulsars and aligns with the inferred proper motion based on the offset of the neutron star from the center of expansion of the optical ejecta, providing valuable insights into the dynamics of this supernova remnant.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: The advent of 5G systems has underscored the significance of Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communications in driving the evolution of cellular networks. A critical challenge in this context is ensuring reliability guarantees for each accessing device amidst a massive influx of almost-simultaneous arrivals from a large set of M2M devices. Existing solutions adopt a reactive approach, often resorting to measures like non-selective barring during massive arrival events, which precludes individual reliability guarantees for devices. This paper proposes a proactive approach, leveraging standard cellular access operations to enhance reliability. The access procedure is bifurcated into an estimation phase, where arrival numbers are estimated, and a serving phase, where resource allocation is tuned based on these estimates. Our findings demonstrate that this proactive strategy significantly enhances access reliability for M2M devices, offering a viable solution to the challenges posed by massive device arrivals in 5G networks. By proactively managing resource allocation, this approach ensures more dependable and efficient M2M communications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation in (1+1) dimensions through numerical simulations, focusing on the two-time evolution of an interface without a disordered environment. Despite the simplicity of the setup, a complex aging behavior emerges. The two-time roughness exhibits multiplicative aging, characterized by the same growth exponent as in the stationary regime. Analysis reveals a growing correlation length that accounts for key scaling variables. The distribution function of the two-time roughness is computed and described by a generalized scaling relation. These findings provide valuable insights into the glassy dynamics of a non-linear elastic line in a disordered medium, shedding light on slow dynamics and aging. The results have implications for understanding kinetic growth processes and self-affine roughness, highlighting the importance of considering aging behavior in these systems. The study contributes to the theoretical understanding of complex out-of-equilibrium phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the properties of non-singular projective curves defined over finite fields, specifically those associated with rational primes @xmath0 and @xmath1, where @xmath1 is odd and the order of @xmath0 modulo @xmath1 is even. We investigate the relationship between these curves and Fermat curves, demonstrating that the latter correspond to maximal or minimal curves over the finite field @xmath5. Furthermore, we show that each Fermat prime yields explicit maximal and minimal curves over finite fields of characteristic 2. For a specific class of curves, we explicitly determine the @xmath9-function as rational functions in the variable @xmath10, confirming that these functions satisfy the Weil conjectures. Additionally, we calculate the class numbers for the function fields associated with each class of curves over @xmath5, providing insight into the growth of class numbers for constant field extensions of the function field(s) of the curve(s) when the field of definition is fixed. Our results offer concrete information on the arithmetic properties of these curves and their associated function fields.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
This article presents a comprehensive new set of stellar evolution models and isochrones tailored for galactic halo and bulge stars, characterized by an alpha-enhanced metal distribution. This work extends our previous library of stellar models for a scaled-solar metal distribution, as reported in Pietrinferni et al. (2004), by incorporating the effects of alpha-element enhancement into the nuclear network, opacity, equation of state, bolometric corrections, and color transformations. This homogeneous approach rectifies the common inconsistency in existing alpha-enhanced model libraries, which often rely on scaled-solar bolometric corrections and color transformations.

Our models encompass a broad mass range (0.5 to 10 M⊙, with fine mass spacing) and metallicity range (11 values of metal mass fraction, Z, spanning 0.0001 ≤ Z ≤ 0.05). The initial helium mass fraction is set to Y = 0.245 for the most metal-poor models and increases with Z according to the relation Y = 1.4Z + 0.245, to reproduce the initial solar helium abundance. We provide models with and without convective core overshoot during central hydrogen burning, as well as models with varying mass loss efficiencies.

Furthermore, we include complete sets of evolutionary models for low-mass, helium-burning stellar structures across the entire metallicity range, facilitating synthetic horizontal branch simulations. We compare our database with several widely used stellar model libraries and various observed color-magnitude and color-color diagrams of galactic field stars and globular clusters, including Johnson-Cousins and near-infrared magnitudes, as well as Strömgren colors. Our isochrones are also tested against integrated optical colors and surface brightness fluctuation magnitudes of selected globular clusters, yielding satisfactory agreement with empirical constraints.

This extensive database, when combined with our existing scaled-solar model library, offers a valuable tool for investigating both galactic and extragalactic simple and composite stellar populations using stellar population synthesis techniques. The presented models and isochrones provide a robust framework for understanding the complex interplay between stellar evolution, metallicity, and alpha-element enhancement in various astrophysical contexts. By addressing the limitations of previous alpha-enhanced model libraries, this work enables more accurate and reliable analyses of stellar populations, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of galaxy evolution and the formation of stars in different environments.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores holonomy in curved spacetimes, focusing on the Schwarzschild-Droste geometry. We investigate parallel transport of vectors around circular orbits, revealing a quantized band structure of holonomy invariance. Radial holonomy is also examined, and the analysis is extended to spinors and the Reissner-Nordström metric. Notably, the extremal case exhibits distinct behavior. Our calculations provide a foundation for understanding quantum parallel transport in Hilbert-fibered spacetimes, offering a valuable toolkit for future research. The findings have implications for black hole physics and the interplay between geometry and quantum mechanics, shedding new light on the intricacies of curved spacetime.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: The Azimuthal Power Spectra of Optical Emission from Star Formation and Dust in Spiral Galaxies Resembles the Azimuthal Power Spectra of HI Emission from the LMC

Abstract:
This study reveals a striking similarity between the azimuthal power spectra of optical emission from star formation and dust in spiral galaxies and the azimuthal power spectra of HI emission from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). Notably, these power spectra resemble that of velocity in incompressible Kolmogorov turbulence. The underlying reasons for this resemblance are currently unknown, but it may be attributed to the complex interplay of processes driving star and cloud formation, resulting in power spectra similar to Kolmogorov turbulence within observable errors. A key finding is that star and cloud formation are not random, but rather correlated over large distances by forces that operate across multiple scales. These forces likely involve a combination of self-gravity, turbulence, and compression from stellar winds and supernovae, working in concert to create the observed structures in galaxies. Furthermore, the identification of flocculent spirals with swing-amplified instabilities suggests that self-gravity may be a significant contributor to turbulence in the interstellar medium. This research has significant implications for our understanding of star formation and galaxy evolution, highlighting the importance of correlated processes and multiscale forces in shaping the structure of galaxies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper proposes a novel embedding approach to learn user profiles, representing topical interests in a shared space. Utilizing these profiles for search personalization, experiments on major web search engine query logs demonstrate improved search engine performance, outperforming strong baselines and showcasing the effectiveness of our embedding approach in enhancing search personalization accuracy and user experience.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper presents an incremental method for intelligent systems to refine thematic context descriptions. Beginning with a small set of terms, the method constructs initial search queries, yielding new documents and terms to enhance the vocabulary. Iterative refinement improves query effectiveness. Evaluations across numerous topics demonstrate the learned vocabulary's superiority over the original in retrieving relevant information, highlighting the method's potential for enhanced information retrieval and knowledge discovery applications, with significant improvements in query construction and relevant material retrieval, leading to more accurate and efficient searches. The approach shows promise for various domains.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
This study presents a comprehensive analysis of seven Galactic O-type stars, specifically those with spectral types O6 and earlier. By utilizing non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) plane-parallel, hydrostatic models, as well as NLTE spherical models that account for mass loss, we investigate the physical properties of these massive stars. Our detailed calculations and simulations demonstrate the significant impact of flux blocking due to UV metal lines on the atmospheric structures of these objects, consistent with previous research. We find that traditional plane-parallel, hydrostatic models struggle to reproduce the observed spectra of early-type massive stars, particularly at effective temperatures above 50,000 K.

The derived surface gravities for these stars are relatively low, even for those classified as luminosity class V, and exhibit a notable mass discrepancy, suggesting that sphericity and mass loss play crucial roles in shaping their properties. To address this, we employ NLTE spherical models with mass loss, which yield increased surface gravities (by 0.10-0.25 dex) and reduce, although do not entirely resolve, the mass discrepancy. Our analysis reveals that spectroscopic masses are more consistent with the theory of radiatively driven winds than evolutionary masses. Additionally, we determine a helium abundance greater than solar for most of the objects in our sample.

We also examine the effects of various approximations and model details on our results. Specifically, we find that the He II λ4200 line is less sensitive to model nuances than the He II λ4541 line, making it a preferred diagnostic for temperature determinations, which in turn leads to lower effective temperatures. Furthermore, our study shows that modifying the treatment of He II resonance lines, either by imposing detailed balance or introducing additional opacity sources, improves the fits to the He II λ4686 line and affects the He II blend with Hα.

For some stars in our sample, the high mass loss rates render the determination of surface gravities from Balmer line wings uncertain. In extreme cases, the mass loss rates required to fit Hα and Hβ differ by up to a factor of two. Our analysis focuses on some of the most massive and luminous stars in the Milky Way, with three objects (Cyg OB2 #3, HD 15570, and HD 15558) exhibiting initial masses close to or exceeding 100 M. Finally, our results suggest that the least luminous object in our sample, HD 5689, may have been misclassified as a member of Cas OB7 and could potentially be a runaway star. Overall, this study provides new insights into the properties and behavior of massive O-type stars, highlighting the importance of considering sphericity, mass loss, and detailed model calculations in their analysis.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines reheating in the context of the νMSM (Standard Model with three right-handed neutrinos) with masses below the electroweak scale. We investigate the generation of a sterile neutrino, serving as dark matter, through decays of an additional inflaton field. Our analysis reveals that reheating occurs at low temperatures due to inefficient energy transfer from the inflaton to the Standard Model sector. This leads to strict bounds on the inflaton-Higgs coupling, resulting in a light inflaton mass, approximately 1-10 GeV or slightly heavier, between 250-1000 GeV, providing new insights into inflation and the νMSM.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines a simplified model of interacting scalar field theory, where fundamental excitations exhibit unphysical propagators with complex conjugate mass poles, akin to those found in certain Yang-Mills gauge theory approaches. Despite the non-physical nature of these "0-particles," we demonstrate that composite operators can be constructed with well-defined spectral representations, enabling a particle interpretation. These physical excitations, analogous to mesons, are bound states of two unphysical 0-particles. By resumming a class of diagrams, we estimate the meson mass from the emerging pole. The primary objective of this paper is to illustrate how a real mass pole can arise from constituent particles with complex masses, providing insight into the confinement phenomenon. Our results offer a deeper understanding of the relationship between unphysical excitations and physical particles in interacting field theories, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms of particle formation.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We examine a planar three-body system consisting of a light particle and two heavy bosons, interacting via a short-range potential. The Born-Oppenheimer approximation is applied, yielding a Coulomb energy spectrum with a Gaussian cutoff. This approach is justified by the large atomic mass ratio. Our analysis provides insight into few-body physics, particularly in cold-atom mixtures. The predicted energy spectrum is characterized by a resonance in the heavy-light potential, enabling a deeper understanding of the system's bound states and interactions, with implications for experimental studies of ultracold atomic systems and few-body phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: A High-Resolution Spectroscopic Analysis of 62 Red Giants in the Milky Way Globular Cluster NGC 5286

Abstract:

We present a comprehensive high-resolution spectroscopic analysis of 62 red giant stars in the Milky Way globular cluster NGC 5286. Our study determines the abundances of key light proton-capture, iron-peak, and neutron-capture elements, which are then combined with photometric data of multiple sequences observed along the color-magnitude diagram. The primary findings of our research reveal a bimodal distribution in s-process element abundance ratios, with two distinct stellar groups: the s-poor and s-rich groups. Notably, substantial star-to-star iron variations are observed, with the s-rich stars exhibiting higher iron abundances. Furthermore, we identify the presence of O-Na-Al (anti-)correlations in both stellar groups. To effectively differentiate between these groups in the color-magnitude diagram, we introduce a novel photometric index that is minimally affected by variations in light elements. Our results categorize NGC 5286 as an "anomalous" globular cluster, displaying internal metallicity variations. The chemical abundance patterns observed in NGC 5286 bear a striking resemblance to those found in other anomalous globular clusters, such as M22, NGC 1851, M2, and ω Centauri. We propose the term "s-Fe-anomalous" globular clusters to describe this subclass of objects, which exhibit common variations in s-process elements. The similarities in chemical abundance ratios among these clusters suggest shared formation and evolution histories, potentially linked to an origin in tidally disrupted dwarf satellites. Our findings provide valuable insights into the complex formation and chemical enrichment processes that shape the properties of globular clusters.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the Crochemore-Mignosi-Restivo (CMR) construction in automata theory, specifically its application to finite-type constrained systems (FTCS) with a limited number of forbidden words. We provide a detailed analysis of the CMR construction for FTCS with one or two forbidden words, demonstrating its potential as a starting point for determining the minimal deterministic presentation, known as the Shannon cover. For irreducible FTCS, we show that an irreducible presentation can be readily obtained from the CMR construction. By investigating the follower sets of states in this presentation, we derive explicit results for the Shannon cover in certain cases. Notably, our findings indicate that the CMR construction directly yields the Shannon cover for irreducible FTCS with a single forbidden word, whereas this is not generally true for systems with two forbidden words, highlighting the complexity of determining minimal presentations for FTCS with multiple constraints.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a refined theoretical framework for describing the weakly interacting Bose gas at short- to intermediate distances, leveraging an improved version of Beliaev's diagrammatic technique. By introducing a small symmetry-breaking term, we regularize the infrared limit, enabling the derivation of explicit equations for all thermodynamic quantities and correlation functions with controllable accuracy. Our approach yields a partition function and entropy that correspond to a non-interacting bosonic pseudo-Hamiltonian with a temperature-dependent Bogoliubov-type dispersion relation, accurate up to higher-order terms. This method provides the most accurate description of the system within the Bogoliubov-type pseudo-Hamiltonian framework, particularly away from the fluctuation region. We demonstrate the validity of our theory by comparing it to first-principle Monte Carlo simulations for various thermodynamic properties and the single-particle density matrix. Furthermore, our approach can be extended to the fluctuation region by incorporating universal constants and scaling functions obtained from classical U(1) models, allowing for an accurate description of the weakly interacting Bose gas in all spatial dimensions. The results of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the behavior of weakly interacting Bose gases, with implications for the development of more accurate theoretical models in condensed matter physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study derives an expression for the mass of a spherically symmetric system using the homotopy perturbation method to solve the Euler-Lagrangian equation. Combining this with Einstein's field equations yields an interior solution set. The solution's physical properties, including mass, density, and pressure, are analyzed in the context of brown dwarf stars. While most features align with observations, the model's stability is found to be suspect, indicating potential instability, which warrants further investigation to refine the theoretical framework.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the lepton mixing predictions of models incorporating the @xmath1 flavour group series, a subgroup of @xmath0. Focusing on models that preserve either full residual @xmath3 or a @xmath4 subgroup for neutrinos, with optional generalized CP symmetry, we derive predictions for mixing angles, Dirac CP phase, and Majorana phases. Our extensive studies reveal the interplay between flavour group and generalized CP symmetry is crucial for determining viable lepton mixing parameters, including Majorana phases, offering insight into the properties of @xmath2 and related models with potential experimental implications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present the results of a spectropolarimetric study of 23 Herbig Ae/Be stars using Hα observations. Our analysis reveals a significant change in linear polarisation across Hα in a substantial fraction of the sample, indicating the presence of flattened, disc-like structures on small scales around these young stars. A key finding of our study is the distinct difference in spectropolarimetric signatures between Herbig Ae and Be stars. While Herbig Be stars exhibit depolarisation across Hα, Herbig Ae stars display line polarisation effects. The frequency of depolarisation in Herbig Be stars (7/12) suggests that these higher-mass stars may be surrounded by flattened structures, analogous to classical Be stars. In contrast, 9 out of 11 Herbig Ae stars show line polarisation, which can be attributed to compact Hα emission polarised by a rotating disc-like circumstellar medium. The observed difference in spectropolarimetric properties between Herbig Ae and Be stars may indicate a transition in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram from magnetic accretion at spectral type A to disc accretion at spectral type B. Alternatively, the interior polarised line emission in Herbig Ae stars may be masked in Herbig Be stars due to their higher levels of Hα emission. Our study provides new insights into the circumstellar environments of Herbig Ae/Be stars and highlights the importance of spectropolarimetry in understanding the formation and evolution of these young stars.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star, @xmath0 Puppis, which is believed to be in the early stages of forming a bipolar planetary nebula (PN). Utilizing three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations with adaptive-mesh refinement, we model the @xmath0 Puppis system to reproduce its observed characteristics. Our simulations incorporate radiative transfer and spectral energy distribution (SED) calculations, allowing for a detailed comparison with existing observational data. By assuming a binary system with reported parameters, we demonstrate that a brief, high-velocity ejection of material from the AGB star can accurately replicate the current observational features. This ejection could be triggered by a thermal pulse, periastron passage of the secondary, or planetary ingestion. Our findings provide valuable insights into the late stages of stellar evolution and the formation of bipolar PNs, highlighting @xmath0 Puppis as a benchmark object for future studies of AGB stars and their transitions to PNs. The results have significant implications for our understanding of stellar mass loss, binary interactions, and the shaping of planetary nebulae.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study employed long-term videomicroscopy and computer-aided statistical analysis to investigate cell motility and proliferation in three established human glioblastoma cell lines. The migration and proliferation activities of these cell lines were compared, as these features significantly impact cancer progression. Cell proliferation was evaluated by calculating growth rates and cell-cycle times in sub-confluent cultures, revealing no significant differences among the cell lines across various passages. In contrast, cell locomotion studies showed strong temporal fluctuations and exponential velocity distributions, with characteristic profiles and average velocity values unique to each cell line. Despite fluctuations, these dynamical parameters were reproducibly consistent for each cell line. Comparison with traditional pathological data revealed that cell motility analysis provides more specific information, potentially enhancing diagnostic capabilities. The findings suggest that examining cell motility may offer a valuable tool for understanding glioblastoma tumor behavior and improving diagnostic accuracy, ultimately informing treatment strategies and patient outcomes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report the detection of seven giant radio pulses from millisecond pulsar 1937+21 using the Ooty Radio Telescope at 326.5 MHz. Observations over 8.1 minutes reveal pulses emitted within a narrow 47μs window of pulse phase, near the profile peak. These findings support giant pulse behavior at higher frequencies and have implications for high-precision timing at low radio frequencies, offering insights into neutron star physics and millisecond pulsar properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the results of a new spectroscopic analysis of the star HD75289, which has been recently discovered to host a Jupiter-mass planet. Our high-resolution, high signal-to-noise ratio spectra reveal a metallicity of [Fe/H] = 0 for this star, confirming the findings of a previous spectroscopic study by Gratton et al. We also re-analyzed the spectra of two additional stars, refining their parameters to better align with photometric and spectroscopic values reported in recent studies. Furthermore, we conducted an extended abundance analysis of four other stars, including 14 Her, HD 187123, HD 210277, and one other. Our results, combined with recent analyses of HD 217107, suggest that all "hot-Jupiter" systems studied to date are hosted by metal-rich parent stars. Notably, we found that the mean [C/Fe] and [Na/Fe] values among stars with planets are lower than those of field stars with similar metallicity. These findings contribute to our understanding of the relationship between planetary formation and stellar composition, highlighting the importance of spectroscopic analysis in characterizing exoplanet host stars. Our study provides new insights into the properties of stars with planets, shedding light on the complex interactions between planetary formation and stellar evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a photometric calibration of Kurucz static model atmospheres to determine parameters of RR Lyrae stars. The variation of stellar angular radius, effective temperature, and gravity as a function of phase, interstellar reddening, and atmospheric metallicity are investigated. The quasi-static atmosphere approximation (QSAA) is generalized to a non-uniformly moving spherical atmosphere, enabling the derivation of distance, mass, and atmospheric motion from conservation laws. The method is applied to the photometry of SU Dra, yielding parameters such as metallicity, distance, and equilibrium luminosity. The results demonstrate the efficiency of the method in determining fundamental parameters of RR Lyrae stars, including distance, mass, and atmospheric properties. This approach provides a valuable tool for understanding the properties and behavior of these variable stars, with implications for stellar astrophysics and hydrodynamics. The derived parameters are in good agreement with expected values.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the phenomenology of pseudo-Goldstinos in multi-sector SUSY breaking scenarios. We investigate the decays of the lightest neutralino and chargino into a pseudo-Goldstino and a gauge or Higgs boson. A Monte Carlo simulation is performed for direct production and subsequent decay at the High Luminosity LHC. Considering various neutralino compositions, we find the signal-to-background ratio ranges from 6% to 25%. The statistical significance of the signal is potentially above 2σ, depending on the scenario. Our results highlight the potential for discovering pseudo-Goldstinos at the LHC, providing insight into SUSY breaking mechanisms and beyond.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We analyze an oscillating mass object's motion without external force, yielding acceleration in all reference frames except rest. Periodic motion emerges, distinct from harmonic oscillations, revealing unique classical mechanics characteristics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Abstract:

This study investigates the non-axisymmetric structure of accretion discs in Be/X-ray binaries using three-dimensional smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations. Focusing on a coplanar system with a short period and moderate eccentricity, we demonstrate that ram pressure generated by phase-dependent mass transfer from the Be-star disc triggers a transient, one-armed, trailing spiral structure in the accretion disc surrounding the neutron star. The spiral wave is excited near periastron passage, when material is transferred from the Be disc, and subsequently damped. As the spiral wave develops and decays over one orbital period, the disc morphology evolves from circular to eccentric and back to circular. Notably, the inward propagation of the spiral wave significantly enhances the mass-accretion rate onto the neutron star. Our findings suggest that detecting an X-ray luminosity peak corresponding to the enhanced mass-accretion rate peak can provide indirect evidence for the presence of an accretion disc in Be/X-ray binaries. These results contribute to our understanding of the complex dynamics and observational characteristics of these systems, highlighting the importance of numerical simulations in elucidating the intricacies of accretion disc behavior.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a comprehensive investigation into the evolution of binary fractions in star clusters, utilizing sophisticated N-body models comprising up to 100,000 stars. Our simulations, performed with the Nbody4 code, incorporate a full mass spectrum of stars, stellar evolution, binary evolution, and the tidal field of the galaxy, with primordial binary frequencies ranging from 5% to 50%. Our findings indicate that the overall binary fraction of a cluster remains remarkably consistent with its primordial value, except during the final stages of cluster dissolution. However, a notable exception occurs in the central regions, where we observe a significant increase in binary fraction over time. In one simulation, starting with 100,000 stars and 5% binaries, the core binary frequency surged to 40% by the end of the core-collapse phase, which occurred at 10 gyr with 10,000 stars remaining. This increase is attributed to the interplay between mass segregation, binary destruction, and the creation of new binaries through exchange interactions. Furthermore, our results suggest that binaries are cycled in and out of cluster cores in a manner analogous to convection in stars. For models with 100,000 stars, we demonstrate that the evolution of the core radius is insensitive to the primordial binary frequency, provided it is 10% or less, up to the end of the initial core-collapse phase. Our study has significant implications for understanding the primordial binary content of globular clusters, and we discuss the ramifications of our findings in this context.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study delves into the properties and production mechanisms of winds in black hole hot accretion flows, a crucial aspect of understanding the complex interplay between black hole activity and galaxy evolution. Utilizing a three-dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulation of a Schwarzschild black hole, we investigate the mass flux, poloidal speed, and underlying drivers of wind generation. By tracking virtual Lagrangian particles, we identify two distinct types of outflows: a quasi-relativistic jet near the axis and a sub-relativistic wind covering a larger solid angle. Our findings confirm that the wind's mass flux is substantial, with most of it originating from the accretion flow's surface layer. The radial profile of the wind mass flux is characterized by a specific relationship with the mass accretion rate and Schwarzschild radius. Furthermore, we observe that the poloidal wind speed remains relatively constant after production, while the flux-weighted wind speed follows a specific dependence on the Keplerian speed. In contrast, the jet's mass flux is lower but its speed is significantly higher. Consequently, the wind's energy and momentum fluxes surpass those of the jet. We determine that the wind is primarily produced and accelerated by the combined effects of centrifugal force and magnetic pressure gradient, whereas the jet is mainly driven by magnetic pressure gradient. Notably, our calculated wind production efficiency aligns with the values required by large-scale galaxy simulations incorporating active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback, underscoring the significance of winds in shaping galaxy evolution. These results provide valuable insights into the intricate dynamics of black hole accretion flows and their far-reaching implications for galaxy-scale processes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study evaluates the momentum dependence of the drag coefficient of heavy quarks in quark-gluon plasma (QGP). The results are used to estimate the nuclear suppression factor of charm and bottom quarks. The momentum dependence of transport coefficients is found to be crucial in suppressing heavy quarks, affecting the properties of QGP probed by heavy flavors. Radiative losses are identified as the primary cause of heavy quark suppression observed at RHIC and LHC. Additionally, the suppression of heavy quarks in Pb+Pb collisions at LHC energy, recently measured by the ALICE collaboration, is investigated, providing insights into QGP properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article revisits the concept of a 'universal covering' introduced by Lebesgue in 1914, which is a convex subset of the plane containing an isometric copy of any subset of diameter 1. Building on the work of mathematicians such as PL, Sprague, and Hansen, who have incrementally reduced the area of universal coverings, we identify an error in Hansen's claimed reduction. With the assistance of Greg Egan, we present a new universal covering with an area less than the previously established minimum, achieving a reduction of a significant amount and advancing the field's understanding of minimal universal coverings.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the role of coherent structures in particle acceleration within the strongly turbulent solar corona. By comparing the dynamics of collisionless test protons in exact magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fields and phase-randomized fields, derived from a pseudo-spectral simulation of isotropic MHD turbulence, we demonstrate that phase correlations significantly enhance acceleration efficiency during the initial adiabatic stage. The underlying mechanism is attributed to the dynamic MHD alignment of magnetic fields with electric currents, fostering parallel electric fields that facilitate initial particle injection. Conversely, alignment with bulk velocity diminishes acceleration due to convective electric fields at later stages. Our findings highlight the importance of considering physical electric fields, as non-physical parallel electric fields in randomized turbulence models can lead to artificial acceleration. The dynamic MHD alignment can be captured through the joint two-point function of magnetic and electric fields, enabling its incorporation into Fokker-Planck descriptions of stochastic acceleration. This research provides new insights into the complex interplay between turbulent structures and particle acceleration in the solar corona.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article delves into the study of saddle points of a vector logarithmic energy with a vector polynomial external field on the plane, which gives rise to the notion of vector-valued critical measures. These measures are motivated by various branches of analysis and are characterized by the interplay of attracting and repelling forces. We establish general structural results for critical measures, including their representation in terms of an algebraic equation involving their Cauchy transforms and their symmetry properties.
