Consequently, we find that vector-valued critical measures are supported on a finite number of analytic arcs, which are trajectories of a quadratic differential defined on a three-sheeted Riemann surface. The critical graph of this differential is crucial in constructing critical measures. To illustrate these connections, we examine a one-parameter family of critical measures under a cubic external field, motivated by the asymptotic analysis of non-hermitian multiple orthogonal polynomials. We compute the Riemann surface and quadratic differential explicitly, analyzing the dynamics of the critical graph as a function of the parameter and describing the resulting phase transitions. This construction yields a complete family of vector-valued critical measures, which are equivalent to vector-valued equilibrium measures when projected onto the complex plane. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of vector-valued critical measures and their role in analysis, with implications for the study of multiple orthogonal polynomials and related fields.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the reduction of thermal noise in dielectric mirror coatings for enhanced sensitivity in second and third generation interferometric gravitational wave detectors. We investigate the use of a Khalili etalon as a viable alternative to a Khalili cavity, requiring less hardware while still achieving significant thermal noise reduction. By optimizing the coating layer distribution on the etalon's front and rear surfaces, we demonstrate a notable decrease in thermal noise. A comparative analysis with a conventional mirror reveals the total noise budget improvement. Furthermore, we discuss the technical advantages and disadvantages of the Khalili etalon versus the Khalili cavity, including interferometric length control and thermal lensing, to provide insight into the feasibility of this approach for future gravitational wave detectors. Our findings contribute to the ongoing efforts to enhance detector sensitivity.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article reviews the historical development of neutron star physics in the 1930s, with a focus on the contributions of Lev Landau. According to previous accounts, Landau conceived the idea of neutron stars in a discussion with Niels Bohr and Leon Rosenfeld in February 1932, shortly after the discovery of the neutron. However, we argue that this conversation actually took place in March 1931, prior to the discovery of the neutron. We present evidence that the discussion centered on a paper written by Landau in February 1931, which proposed the existence of dense stars resembling giant nuclei. This work can be seen as an early theoretical prediction of neutron stars, predating the discovery of the neutron. The coincidence of the neutron's discovery and the paper's publication in February 1932 has led to a mistaken association between the two. Our analysis also highlights Landau's contributions to the theory of white dwarfs and the hypothesis of stars with neutron cores. By re-examining the historical record, we aim to provide a more accurate understanding of the origins of neutron star physics and Landau's role in shaping this field. Our study sheds new light on the development of modern astrophysics and the pioneering work of one of its most influential figures.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We investigate the mechanical properties of free polyelectrolyte multilayer films by analyzing osmotically induced swelling of microcapsules. Varying polyelectrolyte concentrations, capsule radii, and shell thicknesses yields an estimated upper limit for Young's modulus of approximately 100 MPa, indicating elastomer-like behavior and strong polyanion-polycation interactions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents the authors' harmonic deformation theory for 3-dimensional hyperbolic cone-manifolds, exploring topological applications to hyperbolic Dehn surgery and Kleinian group theory. Local rigidity results are leveraged to control existing deformations, yielding precise analytic and geometric insights into hyperbolic structures with short geodesics. The theory reveals that such structures are proximal to those with cusps. A novel harmonic deformation theory is also introduced, applicable when a sufficiently large embedded tube surrounds the singular locus, thus removing the constraint on cone angles. This advancement expands the theory's scope and utility.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the performance of a partially correlated amplitude damping channel on two qubits. We derive lower bounds for the single-shot classical capacity by analyzing two quantum ensembles that maximize the Holevo quantity for both memoryless and full-memory channels. The entanglement required to achieve this maximum is also quantified. Additionally, we establish lower and upper bounds for the single-shot quantum capacity, providing a reliable estimate for high channel transmissivity values. Finally, the entanglement-assisted classical channel capacity is computed, offering insights into the channel's information transmission capabilities and the role of entanglement in optimizing its performance.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the thermal softening of crystals resulting from anharmonicity, with a focus on developing a reliable self-consistent method to predict the maximum temperature for a stable crystal. Previous approaches, such as the self-consistent harmonic approximation (SCHA), have been shown to yield inaccurate results due to the omission of crucial diagrams in the perturbation expansion. An alternative method, the self-consistent Dyson equation (SCA), has also been found to be deficient in capturing the thermal and quantum melting of two-dimensional Coulomb-interacting particles. To address these limitations, we introduce the two-vertex self-consistent harmonic approximation (2V-SCHA), which provides a significant improvement in agreement with numerical simulations. Our method enables accurate calculations of the thermal softening of the shear modulus for two-dimensional crystals and the lattice of vortex lines in type-II superconductors, offering a more reliable estimate of the upper bound to the melting temperature. The 2V-SCHA approach has important implications for understanding the thermal stability of crystals and vortex lattices, and its applications are discussed in the context of melting transitions in two and three dimensions.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores the intrinsic spin Hall effect in two-dimensional electron gases within quantum wells featuring two subbands. A novel intersubband-induced spin-orbit coupling is identified, and its impact on bulk spin Hall conductivity is examined. Utilizing the Kubo formalism, calculations reveal a finite conductivity in the absence of scattering, even in the limit of zero magnetic field, provided only the lowest subband is occupied. The conductivity exhibits non-monotonic behavior, changing sign as the Fermi energy varies between subband edges. A self-consistent calculation is performed to determine the magnitude of spin Hall conductivity for realistic InSb quantum wells, offering insights into the role of intersubband-induced spin-orbit coupling in these systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article investigates compact Kähler manifolds admitting non-trivial real-holomorphic geodesic gradient vector fields with an additional integrability condition. We classify these manifolds, showing they are biholomorphic to bundles of complex projective spaces. The integral curves of such vector fields are reparametrized geodesics, satisfying specific geometric properties. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between geodesic gradient vector fields and the complex geometry of Kähler manifolds, shedding light on the interplay between real and complex geometric structures in these spaces, with implications for geometry and complex analysis.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a model of an anisotropic universe within the scalar-tensor theory of gravitation, where string fluid serves as the source of matter. By applying Berman's law, exact solutions to the field equations are obtained, resulting in a constant value of deceleration parameter. The model's classical potential is examined, and it is found that massive strings dominate in the early universe before eventually disappearing. This aligns with current astronomical observations. The physical and dynamical properties of the model are also discussed, providing insight into the universe's evolution. The results offer a novel perspective on the role of string fluid in cosmology.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the potential impact of upgrades to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) on the physics capabilities of the ATLAS detector. Two possible upgrade scenarios are considered: an increase in luminosity by a factor of ten and a doubling of the LHC energy. Both upgrades are found to significantly enhance the physics capabilities of ATLAS, with the energy upgrade offering greater mass reach for new particles. However, in cases where the upgrade leads to increased precision in measurements due to larger data samples, the luminosity upgrade is found to be equally powerful. The increased pile-up of minimum bias events at higher luminosity may limit the physics performance of ATLAS in areas requiring forward jet tagging. The study assesses the potential benefits and challenges of each upgrade scenario, providing valuable insights for future LHC upgrade plans. The analysis is based on detailed simulations and considers various physics processes, highlighting the importance of careful planning and optimization to fully exploit the potential of the ATLAS detector in future LHC runs. The results of this study will inform the development of upgrade strategies for the LHC and ATLAS, ultimately enhancing our understanding of the fundamental laws of physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study applies the worldline formalism to scalar Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) to derive a Bern-Kosower type master formula for generalized Compton scattering, applicable both on-shell and off-shell. The non-perturbative gauge parameter dependence of amplitudes in scalar QED is examined, yielding a simple transformation rule under gauge parameter changes in terms of conformal cross ratios. This result generalizes the Landau-Khalatnikov-Fradkin transformation, providing new insights into scalar QED. The transformation's perturbative behavior is also demonstrated, offering a deeper understanding of gauge parameter dependence in quantum field theories.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the potential discovery of high mass neutral quantum states at hadron colliders, specifically through their decay into a pair of photons. The determination of the spin of these states is crucial in identifying the underlying nonstandard dynamics. We investigate the discrimination of a spin-2 Randall-Sundrum graviton excitation from a spin-0 exchange, using angular analysis of resonant diphoton events expected at the LHC. The spin-0 hypothesis is modeled by an effective interaction of a high mass gauge singlet scalar particle. Our analysis focuses on the symmetrically integrated angular asymmetry, calculated to next-to-leading order in QCD for both graviton and scalar exchanges. By comparing the angular distributions, we aim to distinguish between these two hypotheses, providing insight into the nature of potential new physics beyond the Standard Model. The results have implications for the interpretation of future LHC data.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study employs a solvable model to investigate double-beta decay, with a particular emphasis on the neutrinoless mode. By analyzing the impact of the neutrino propagator on the matrix element, we address the limitations of finite model-space size in shell-model calculations. Our approach involves projecting exact wave functions onto a smaller subspace and evaluating both traditional and recent methods for constructing effective operators. The results indicate that conventional treatments of double-beta decay operators are insufficient to account for neglected parts of the model space. Furthermore, we assess the quasiparticle random phase approximation and a recent proposal to utilize two-neutrino decay for fixing Hamiltonian parameters, which reduces the dependence on unfixed parameters and model-space size. Our findings provide valuable insights into the theoretical framework underlying double-beta decay and highlight the need for refined calculations to accurately capture the underlying physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the emergence of collective dynamics in an integrable Hamiltonian system comprising two finite ensembles of coupled harmonic oscillators. By identifying a collective degree of freedom, we map the Hamiltonian onto a Caldeira-Leggett type model, where the collective coordinate interacts with an internal phonon bath. Unlike traditional models, the bath is an intrinsic part of the system. We derive an equation of motion for the collective coordinate, yielding a damped harmonic oscillator. Our results demonstrate that the distribution of quantum transition strengths induced by the collective mode is determined by its classical dynamics, providing insight into the complex interplay between collective behavior and quantum fluctuations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines DNA's S-shape in relation to its total energy. Using the classical variation method, we derive equilibrium shape equations, providing both first and second variations in the planar case. Our results correct a mistake in previous research and yield general shape equations for DNA, offering new insights into its structural dynamics with implications for molecular biology and biophysics research applications and theory.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: Revisiting KIC 9202990: Unveiling the Nature of its Photometric Periods

Abstract:
We re-examine the photometric properties of KIC 9202990 using the comprehensive Kepler dataset, spanning 1421 days. Our analysis confirms the stability of the 4-hour period, reinforcing its association with the binary orbital period. In contrast, the previously reported two-week period exhibits significant amplitude variability, ranging from 20% to 50%. This modulation bears resemblance to 'stunted' outbursts observed in nova-like systems. We discuss the shortcomings of the precessing accretion disk model in explaining the observed characteristics and argue in favor of a stunted outburst model. KIC 9202990 presents a unique opportunity to investigate accretion instabilities, as it displays the lowest amplitude and shortest period of continuous stunted outburst systems. Our findings have implications for understanding the disk instability mechanism and its role in shaping the behavior of cataclysmic variables. By exploring the properties of KIC 9202990, we aim to shed light on the underlying physics governing stunted outbursts and advance our knowledge of accretion processes in binary systems. This study highlights the importance of long-term monitoring and detailed analysis of photometric data in unraveling the complexities of accretion disk dynamics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We investigate the non-equilibrium evolution of a strongly interacting fermionic system. Collective collapse and revival phenomena are observed for strong quenches, while weak quenches exhibit weak wiggling. Notably, prethermalization is absent in the weak coupling regime. Relaxation beyond oscillatory behavior is evident, allowing estimation of relaxation rates. The fastest relaxation occurs at intermediate quenched interaction values, providing insight into the system's dynamics and relaxation mechanisms, with implications for understanding complex quantum systems and their behavior under non-equilibrium conditions and quenches of varying strength.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the potential of 3D printing in revolutionizing various aspects of our lives, as touted by many as a key driver of the third industrial revolution. While its applications are currently limited, scientific research is one area where 3D printing has shown significant promise. We present the development of a set of opto-mechanical components that can be easily fabricated using Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) and readily available hardware store parts. The customized components offer several advantages, including low-cost, rapid fabrication, and performance comparable to low-end commercial alternatives. This study demonstrates the feasibility of 3D printing in creating functional and affordable components, highlighting its potential to transform scientific research and other fields. Our findings contribute to the growing body of research on 3D printing, underscoring its potential to drive innovation and change in the near future. Key benefits include ease of use and high customizability.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article addresses the approximation of functionals dependent on a system of particles, modeled by stochastic differential equations (SDEs), as the number of particles approaches infinity. This problem is equivalent to estimating the weak solution of the limiting McKean-Vlasov SDE. To tackle this challenge, we employ systems with finite particles and an Euler-Maruyama time-stepping scheme, resulting in two discretization parameters: the number of time steps and particles. We investigate various Monte Carlo and multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods, demonstrating that the optimal work complexity of MLMC to estimate the functional with an error tolerance of $\epsilon$ is $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ in a typical setting. Furthermore, we explore the multi-index Monte Carlo method, achieving an improved work complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2}(\log \epsilon^{-1})^2)$ when utilizing a partitioning estimator. Numerical experiments are conducted on the Kuramoto model, a system of coupled oscillators, to validate our findings. Our research contributes to the development of efficient numerical methods for approximating functionals in the mean-field limit, with applications in fields such as physics, biology, and finance. The results highlight the potential of MLMC and multi-index Monte Carlo methods in tackling complex stochastic problems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a novel expression for the entropy four-current up to third order in gradient expansion, derived using a Chapman-Enskog-like iterative solution of the Boltzmann equation in relaxation-time approximation. Notably, the resulting third-order entropy four-current exhibits a non-vanishing entropy flux, contrasting with previous second-order and third-order expressions obtained via Grad's method. The implications of this higher-order entropy density are investigated in the context of boost-invariant one-dimensional longitudinal expansion. By employing the Chapman-Enskog expansion method, we derive a third-order evolution equation for the shear stress tensor, yielding results that demonstrate improved agreement with both the exact solution of the Boltzmann equation and the parton cascade BAMPS, compared to those obtained using Grad's 14-moment approximation. These findings highlight the significance of incorporating higher-order corrections in the description of complex systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a simplified derivation of the "simple Fock scheme", a method for reformulating the many-body problem of interacting bosons in terms of single-particle wave function stochastic evolution. Compared to the original derivation, our approach is more elementary. We also examine two alternative schemes based on coherent states, demonstrating that they yield infinite statistical uncertainty in the continuous time limit. In contrast, the simple Fock scheme remains the only proven method for convergent Monte Carlo simulations at all times, solidifying its importance in the study of interacting boson systems. Its advantages are highlighted.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the physical properties of gamma-ray burst (GRB) emissions within the external shock model, where a thin relativistic blast wave interacts with the circumburst medium (CBM). We analyze an analytic function that describes the temporally evolving GRB spectra in a smooth CBM with density profile. Our results successfully reproduce the hard-to-soft spectral evolution and intensity-hardness correlation of GRB peaks. Furthermore, we predict several key features of GRB peaks, including alignment at high photon energies and lag at low energies, a well-defined shift in temporal indices with photon energy, and a decrease in spectral index change between peak edges at higher energies. Additionally, we demonstrate that the typical detection of GRBs with peaks in the 50 keV to several MeV range is a consequence of the inverse correlation between peak flux and radiation duration emitted by decelerating blast waves. Our findings provide new insights into the behavior of GRB emissions and can inform the development of more accurate models for understanding these complex astrophysical events. The predictions made in this study can be tested against observational data, offering a valuable tool for refining our understanding of GRB physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the parity-time reversal symmetric non-Hermitian version of a quantum network, as proposed by Christandl et al. Our systematic analysis reveals that this model exemplifies the complex relationship between pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonians and their Hermitian counterparts. Furthermore, it provides a viable candidate for experimental realization of symmetry breaking. We demonstrate that conditional perfect state transfer is achievable within the unbroken symmetry region, albeit not arbitrarily. This limitation arises from the evolution operator's equivalence to the parity-time reversal operator at specific periods, as applied to real-valued wavefunctions in the parity-time reversal symmetric Hilbert space. Our findings offer insights into the intricacies of quantum mechanics and the potential applications of this model in quantum information processing.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study simulates the cooling of neutron stars with dipole magnetic fields using a realistic model of anisotropic surface temperature distribution. The magnetic field suppresses electron thermal conductivity near the equator, increasing thermal isolation, while enhancing radiative and longitudinal conductivities near the poles, reducing isolation. The equatorial effect is pronounced for weaker fields (@xmath0 G), and the polar effect for stronger fields (@xmath1 G). However, these effects partially compensate each other, resulting in a weaker influence of magnetic fields on cooling than traditionally predicted, highlighting the importance of considering both equatorial and polar effects in neutron star cooling models.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the forecasting capabilities of realized skewness and realized kurtosis for individual stock returns and variance on a daily scale. Contrary to existing literature, which primarily focuses on monthly or weekly scales and whole market analysis, our empirical analysis reveals distinct findings. Notably, realized kurtosis demonstrates significant predictive power for a stock's future variance. In contrast, realized skewness lacks explanatory power for daily returns of individual stocks over short horizons, diverging from established research. Our results, derived from high-frequency data and linear regression models, contribute to the understanding of higher-order moments in financial markets. The surprising findings have implications for trading strategies and risk management, highlighting the importance of considering realized kurtosis in forecasting stock variance. Overall, this research expands the literature on realized moments and their applications in finance.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents an analysis of data collected by the Middle Drum Fluorescence Detector, refurbished from the High Resolution Fly's Eye (HiRes) HIRES-1 site, within the Telescope Array. Utilizing the HiRes-1 profile-constrained geometry reconstruction technique and identical calibration methods, a direct comparison of energy spectra and scales is facilitated between the two experiments. A three-year exposure (2007-2010) yielded a measured spectrum, enabling the transfer of the HiRes-1 energy scale to Middle Drum. By comparing monocular Middle Drum events with hybrid events triggering both Middle Drum and the Telescope Array's scintillator ground array, the HiRes energy scale is applied to the entire Telescope Array. This research aims to provide a precise energy spectrum of Ultra-High Energy Cosmic Rays (UHECRs), leveraging the combined strengths of the HiRes and Telescope Array experiments to advance our understanding of cosmic ray physics. The results have significant implications for the field, offering a refined understanding of UHECR energy spectra and scales.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the formation of ferromagnetic polarons in doped anisotropic antiferromagnets. We investigate the manifestation of nanoscale phase separation in three- and two-dimensional systems, calculating the shape of the most energetically favorable ferromagnetic droplets. Our results show that the binding energy and volume of these droplets in 3D systems depend on two universal parameters, derived from effective antiferromagnetic exchange and hopping integrals. Similarly, in 2D systems, these parameters determine the droplet's properties. The most favorable shape of a ferromagnetic droplet is found to be an ellipse in 2D and an ellipsoid in 3D, providing insight into the behavior of these systems. Our findings contribute to the understanding of magnetic phase separation at the nanoscale.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present a study of exclusive semileptonic decays proceeding via the underlying transition, utilizing a dataset of meson pairs collected at the resonance with the CLEO II detector. Our analysis yields measurements of key parameters, including branching fractions and distribution shapes, with careful consideration of statistical, systematic, and form factor uncertainties. The results are consistent with expectations from quark model symmetries and the dominant mode. By applying light-cone sum rules and lattice QCD, we extract the desired parameter, obtaining values for two distinct energy intervals. Combining these intervals, we determine the parameter's value with estimated errors accounting for statistical, systematic, theoretical, and signal form-factor shape uncertainties. Our combined result from both decay modes provides a precise determination of the parameter, contributing to a deeper understanding of the underlying physics. The findings have implications for future studies in this area.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents an analysis of the latest 1.3 mm Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) measurements for Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center. By utilizing a model of an accretion flow coupled with an emergent flare, we interpret the visibility data to constrain the distances from the flare center to the black hole center. Our results indicate that the flare is likely to be located at a significant distance from the black hole, with preferred positions of @xmath0 and @xmath1 in the east-west and north-south directions, respectively. We discuss two possible interpretations of the flare: the hot-spot model and the episodic jet model. Our findings suggest that the flare passes in front of the black hole at a large radius or is ejected off the black hole's rotating axis. This method can be applied to future sub-millimeter VLBI observations to study millimeter/sub-millimeter variabilities near Sgr A*.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We report the first secure detection of the reactive ion CO+ towards the prototypical starburst galaxy M 82. Observations of the inner 650 pc of the nuclear disk reveal high [CO+]/[HCO+] ratios, comparable to those found in the atomic peak of the reflection nebula NGC 7023. This discovery suggests that the molecular gas reservoir in M 82 is significantly impacted by UV radiation from recently formed stars. Our analysis indicates that approximately 320 clouds along the line of sight are required to explain the observed column densities. We have developed a photon-dominated region (PDR) chemical model to interpret our findings, which successfully reproduces the measured [CO+]/[HCO+] ratios. However, the model underestimates the large CO+ column densities by an order of magnitude. To reconcile this discrepancy, we explore potential modifications to the chemical model, including revisions to the cloud structure and chemical reactions. Our study provides new insights into the molecular gas chemistry in the nucleus of M 82 and highlights the complexity of modeling the interplay between UV radiation and molecular gas in starburst galaxies. Further refinements to our model are necessary to fully explain the observed CO+ abundances.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: The Uncertainty in Equilibration in Heavy Ion Collisions due to the Choice of the Value of the Coupling

Abstract:

The process of equilibration in heavy ion collisions is a complex phenomenon that has garnered significant attention in the realm of high-energy physics. A crucial aspect of this process is the choice of the coupling constant, which has been shown to have a profound impact on the resulting equilibration. This article examines the effects of varying the coupling constant on the equilibration of the quark-gluon plasma. Our results indicate that a change in the coupling constant from 0.3 to 0.5 can lead to a reduction in the parton phase of the plasma by as much as 4.0 fm/c. Furthermore, an increase in the coupling constant results in a reduction in the generated entropy, while also leading to faster equilibration, both chemically and kinetically, albeit only for fermions. This, in turn, leads to more rapid cooling and a shortened lifetime of the plasma.

The implications of these findings are significant, as they suggest that the choice of coupling constant is essentially equivalent to choosing the outcome of the equilibration process. Moreover, the use of a fixed coupling constant is inconsistent with the evolving nature of the plasma. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach, wherein the system is allowed to dynamically determine its own coupling constant. Our results demonstrate that this approach leads to accelerated equilibration, with improved outcomes, albeit at the expense of a shortened duration of the deconfined phase. This study provides valuable insights into the complex dynamics of heavy ion collisions and highlights the importance of a self-consistent treatment of the coupling constant in these processes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: The absence of Hadean rocks on Earth's surface, with the exception of zircons, suggests that continental crust existed during the Hadean eon but was subsequently lost. One proposed mechanism for this disappearance is the Late Heavy Bombardment (LHB), a period of intense impacts that occurred in the final stages of the Hadean eon. This study investigates the effects of LHB on Hadean continental crust, using semi-analytical expressions to model the excavation and melting of crust due to impacts. Our calculations, based on constraints from the Moon's cratering record, indicate that LHB does not directly excavate or melt all Hadean continental crust. However, we find that over 70% of the Earth's surface area could be covered by subsequent melts, potentially hiding the remaining Hadean crust. The results are robust across a range of power-law exponents describing the size-frequency distribution of impacts. If the continental crust has not undergone significant overturn since the Hadean eon, our findings suggest that LHB could be responsible for the absence of Hadean rocks on Earth's surface, as most of the original crust may be buried beneath later melts. This study provides new insights into the early Earth's crustal evolution and the potential role of LHB in shaping the planet's surface.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study clarifies the impact of non-adiabatic effects on quantum pumping in a spin-boson system. By sinusoidally controlling reservoir temperatures with a phase difference, we find the pumping current depends on initial conditions, deviating from adiabatic predictions. Analytically, non-adiabatic contributions to the current are proportional to the angular frequency of temperature control. Numerical calculations validate this expression. Furthermore, we extend the steady heat fluctuation theorem to cases with slowly modulated temperatures and large energy transfers, providing new insights into quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium phenomena in spin-boson systems under periodic driving.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a theoretical approach to solving the NNLO DGLAP equations using logarithmic expansions in x-space, implemented in the C program CANDIA 1.0. The program offers various options, including the order of evolution, solution type, and flavor number treatment. Users can choose between exact or truncated solutions and fixed or varying flavor numbers via the VFN scheme. Renormalization and factorization scale dependencies are treated separately. Notably, the program implements an exact NNLO solution in the non-singlet sector, providing a robust tool for theoretical calculations. The implementation and solution options are discussed in detail.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study generalizes the construction of middle tunnels for non-torus knot examples, calculating slope invariants and obtaining the slope sequence for the original example by Goda, Hayashi, and Ishihara, providing new insights into genus-1 1-bridge knots.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This paper explores the concept of a software engineering (SE) specific theory, identifying key features endemic to SE. Adapting the term "theory" from traditional sciences, we distinguish it from other uses. We propose focusing on reference class and structuring of SE theories to facilitate further progress, addressing a crucial question in the field and laying groundwork for future research and development in software engineering theory.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study theoretically investigates inner-shell vacancy production in the O@Xe collision system at 1.5 MeV/amu. A multi-electron approach is employed, combining single-electron amplitudes to extract collision process information. The resulting doubly-differential cross sections are compared to experimental data, showing good agreement, particularly for low outgoing electron energies. Analysis reveals that two-electron excitation-ionization processes play a dominant role in improving the results beyond single-active-electron calculations. The findings highlight the importance of considering multi-electron effects in understanding inner-shell vacancy production, providing valuable insights into the collision dynamics of complex atomic systems. Theoretical results are validated by experimental comparisons.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents the construction and detailed analysis of highly-optimized self-refocusing pulse shapes for various rotation angles. The pulses are characterized using Magnus expansion coefficients up to second order, enabling semi-analytical analysis of their performance in sequences and composite pulses. Leading-order error operators are computed to assess the pulses' efficacy. The technique is demonstrated by analyzing composite pulses designed to mitigate pulse amplitude errors and decoupling sequences for long qubit chains with on-site and nearest-neighbor couplings. Numerical methods are also employed to analyze higher-order effects, providing a comprehensive understanding of the optimized pulse shapes' performance and applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Abstract:
The origins of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) are believed to be protons accelerated in magnetized plasma outflows of extra-galactic sources. To accelerate protons to extreme energies, a substantial source power is required. However, the absence of steady, sufficiently powerful sources within the GZK horizon of 100 Mpc suggests that UHECR sources are transient, producing "flares." We demonstrate that these flares should be accompanied by significant X-ray and gamma-ray emission. Utilizing X-ray and gamma-ray surveys, we constrain flares lasting less than a decade, finding they must satisfy specific conditions. The implausibility of certain requirements, such as low power in accelerated electrons or sources existing only at low redshifts, argues in favor of transient sources with high magnetic field to proton energy ratios. This insight provides valuable constraints on the nature of UHECR sources, shedding light on the extreme astrophysical processes that govern their behavior.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the complexities of the universe's history, from the electroweak phase transition to the present day. We examine the well-established events of cosmic history, including the QCD phase transition, big bang nucleosynthesis, and recombination. A quantitative analysis of the universe's age, radiation-matter transition, and hydrogen recombination is also presented. The discussion extends to the era of inflation, where evidence suggests its occurrence, but details remain uncertain. We delve into the concept of "eternal" inflation, proposing an infinite tree of inflationary spacetime, and consider the possibility of inflation being eternal only into the future, necessitating a beginning. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the universe's history, acknowledging the uncertainties and speculating on the possibilities that shape our understanding of the cosmos and its origins. Theoretical frameworks and empirical evidence are integrated to illuminate the mysteries of the universe's evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of subdiffusion in a composite system comprising two media separated by a thin membrane, where the subdiffusion parameters may differ in each medium. By introducing a novel method, we derive the Green's functions that describe a particle's random walk in this system, taking into account the possibility of reactions with constant probabilities. Initially, we consider a discrete-time and discrete-space model, where a particle can vanish due to reactions, and then transition to continuous variables. The reaction probabilities are linked to the subdiffusion parameters through formulas presented in this paper. By calculating the generating functions for the difference equations describing the random walk, we incorporate the subdiffusion parameters of both media into the Green's functions. Setting the reaction probabilities to zero, we obtain the Green's functions for the composite membrane system without reactions. From these functions, we derive the boundary conditions at the thin membrane, one of which involves the Riemann-Liouville fractional time derivative, indicating the presence of an additional "memory effect" in the system. This effect can be induced by both the membrane and the discontinuity of the medium at the junction point, highlighting the complex behavior of subdiffusion in composite systems. Our results provide new insights into the dynamics of subdiffusion in heterogeneous media and have implications for understanding transport phenomena in various fields, including biology and materials science.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents new measurements of inclusive charged hadron distributions from Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV. The STAR collaboration observed charged hadron suppression at high pT, consistent with previous findings at √sNN = 130 GeV for pT < 6 GeV/c. The ratio of central to peripheral collision spectra indicates constant hadron suppression between 6 < pT < 12 GeV/c. Comparing charged hadron spectra at √sNN = 200 GeV and 130 GeV reveals a 15-20% yield increase at low pT. At high pT, the yield increase agrees with pQCD calculations, providing insight into particle production mechanisms in Au+Au collisions. These findings contribute to our understanding of nuclear matter properties at high energies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the concept of a digraph being $k$-ordered Hamiltonian, where a directed Hamilton cycle encounters a given sequence of distinct vertices in a specified order. We prove that every digraph of sufficiently large order $n$ with minimum semi-degree $\delta$ is $k$-ordered Hamiltonian, provided $\delta$ exceeds a certain threshold. Notably, this bound on $\delta$ is optimal. Our result extends a previous finding by Kierstead, Ślesiński, and Śleszyński, which addressed the undirected case, and sheds new light on the Hamiltonian properties of digraphs with high minimum semi-degree.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the structure of electroweak supersymmetric (SUSY) Sudakov corrections at TeV energies, where large logarithmic corrections arise due to superpartner masses near the weak scale. Utilizing the infrared evolution equation method, we derive the general form of these corrections and demonstrate the exponentiation of subleading logarithmic Yukawa-enhanced Sudakov corrections in both the Standard Model and softly broken SUSY extensions. Our results, accurate to subleading logarithmic order, apply to all orders in perturbation theory for arbitrary external lines in the "light" SUSY-mass scenario. We also present the SUSY-QCD limit for virtual corrections and discuss phenomenological applications for precisely determining key parameters through virtual corrections, independent of the soft SUSY-breaking mechanism to sub-subleading accuracy. These findings have significant implications for future high-energy collider experiments.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study reveals a novel peculiarity in the optical spectra of selected post-Asymptotic Giant Branch (post-AGB) stars with carbon-rich circumstellar envelopes. A splitting or asymmetry of strong absorption lines is observed, with the effect being most pronounced in BaII lines, which exhibit two to three distinct components. Analysis suggests that these components form in a structured circumstellar envelope, indicating efficient dredge-up of heavy metals produced during the star's evolution. The splitting or asymmetry of absorption lines with low excitation potential is linked to the kinematic and chemical properties of the circumstellar environment and its morphology, providing insights into the complex processes governing post-AGB star evolution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the renormalization group (RG) running of the neutrino mass operator in the type I seesaw scenario with right-handed neutrinos. To accurately compare model predictions at high energies with experimental data at low energies, RG running is essential. We calculate the one-loop matching formulae for the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) extended by right-handed neutrinos using supergraph techniques. A general formula for one-loop matching of superpotential operators is also presented, applicable to any supersymmetric theory where chiral superfields are integrated out. This work enables precise matching of effective theories at thresholds defined by right-handed neutrino masses, a crucial step in calculating two-loop RG running. By providing a robust framework for RG running and threshold matching, our results contribute to a deeper understanding of neutrino models and their phenomenological implications. The calculations are performed with high precision, ensuring reliable predictions for experimental verification.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: The cosmic evolution of gamma-ray burst (GRB) luminosity is a crucial aspect of understanding GRB physics and utilizing them as cosmological probes. This study investigates the luminosity evolution of long GRBs using a large sample of 258 Swift/BAT GRBs. By parameterizing the peak luminosity of individual GRBs and employing the non-parametric Efron-Petrosian statistics method, we initially obtain a luminosity evolution parameter. However, to account for observational biases in GRB trigger and redshift measurement, we model these biases using the observed peak flux and characterize the peak luminosity function of long GRBs as a smoothly broken power-law with an evolving break. Through simulations assuming the long GRB rate follows the star formation rate and incorporates cosmic metallicity history, we derive revised luminosity evolution parameters. Notably, these parameters are systematically smaller than those reported in previous studies. By generating mock complete samples of GRBs and examining the impact of observational biases on the Efron-Petrosian statistics method, we find that these biases may lead to an overestimation of the luminosity evolution parameter. Our analysis highlights the significant uncertainty in deriving the luminosity evolution feature of GRBs, suggesting that a robust evolution feature may not be convincingly argued. This study underscores the importance of carefully considering observational biases when investigating GRB luminosity evolution and its implications for cosmological probes.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: Using the Yunnan Evolutionary Population Synthesis (EPS) Models with and without Binary Interactions: Calibration of Star Formation Rate (SFR) Diagnostics

Abstract:

We present a comprehensive study of the luminosity of Hα recombination line, the luminosity of [OII]λ3727 forbidden-line doublet, the ultraviolet (UV) fluxes at 1500 and 2800Å, and far-infrared flux for burst, S0, Sa-SD, and Irr galaxies using the Yunnan Evolutionary Population Synthesis (EPS) models with and without binary interactions. Our results provide calibrations of star formation rate (SFR) in terms of these diagnostics. By comparing the models with and without binary interactions, we find that binary interactions lower the SFR vs. Hα and SFR vs. [OII]λ3727 conversion factors by ~0.2 dex. This is primarily due to the increased UV flux (shortward of the Lyman limit) of the stellar population in the age range 6.7 < log(t/yr) < 8.4, resulting in more ionizing photons in the nebula. In contrast, binary interactions do not significantly affect the calibrations of SFR in terms of UV fluxes at 1500 and 2800Å, as the flux at 1500Å is increased by ~1 dex in the age range 8.75 < log(t/yr) < 9.2, while the flux at 2800Å remains largely unaffected. Furthermore, the calibration of SFR from far-infrared flux is almost unaffected by binary interactions, as binary interactions have a negligible impact on the bolometric magnitudes of stellar populations.

We also investigate the effects of initial mass function (IMF), gas-recycle assumption, and different EPS models (including GISSEL98, BC03, Starburst99, PopStar, and PEGASE models) on these SFR calibrations. Our results show that the choice of IMF significantly affects the SFR calibrations, with the Salpeter (S55) IMF yielding higher conversion factors than the Miller & Scalo (MS79) IMF. The inclusion of gas-recycle assumption only affects the SFR calibrations at faint SFRs. Moreover, we find significant differences in the SFR calibrations when using different EPS models, with the differences in the SFR vs. Hα and SFR vs. [OII]λ3727 conversion factors reaching ~0.7 and 0.9 dex, respectively. Finally, we provide the conversion coefficients between SFR and these diagnostics for all models, enabling the estimation of SFRs for various galaxy types and providing a valuable tool for understanding galaxy evolution. Our study highlights the importance of considering binary interactions and IMF variations when calibrating SFR diagnostics, and provides a comprehensive framework for interpreting observational data.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the magnetic structure of LaMnO3 using 3D clusters of MnO6 octahedra, combining relaxation and Monte Carlo techniques. The results show that cooperative Jahn-Teller phonons stabilize A-type antiferromagnetic and C-type orbital structures, with minor corrections from tilting effects. Notably, strong Coulomb interactions are not required to describe undoped manganites, as similar results are obtained with and without explicit Coulomb interaction. These findings provide new insights into the magnetic behavior of LaMnO3, highlighting the importance of lattice degrees of freedom in determining its magnetic properties. The results have implications for understanding manganite physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a comparative analysis of the properties of six supersoft X-ray binaries, namely CAL 83, CAL 87, RX J0513.9-06951, 1E 0035.4-7230 (SMC 13), RX J0019.8+2156, and RX J0925.7-4758. High-resolution spectra of these systems reveal significant variations in the equivalent widths of principal emission lines, with differences exceeding an order of magnitude for H and He II lines. However, the highest ionization lines, such as O VI, exhibit similar characteristics across all sources. The velocity curves derived from various ions often display discrepancies in phasing and amplitude, but those consistent with the light curves imply masses of 1.2 M⊙ and 0.5 M⊙ for the degenerate and mass-losing stars, respectively. Notably, these findings contradict current theoretical models for supersoft binaries. Additionally, evidence of jet outflows is observed in the three highest luminosity sources, with velocities ranging from 1140 to 3100 km s⁻¹. The He II 4686 profile in CAL 83 suggests that these jets may precess with a period of approximately 169 days, providing new insights into the complex dynamics of supersoft X-ray binaries.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the dynamical stability of seven purportedly ancient asteroid families in the main belt, with a focus on determining the oldest recognizable family and potential implications for our understanding of the primitive solar system. The orbital evolution of asteroid family members is influenced by various gravitational and non-gravitational effects, leading to dispersion over time. We investigate the timescales for dispersion of large families, with a particular emphasis on identifying families that may have formed during the late stages of the Late Heavy Bombardment. Our results indicate that none of the seven studied families have a mean estimated age exceeding 2.7 billion years, assuming standard parameters for the Yarkovsky force. Furthermore, we find that "paleo-families" formed between 2.7 and 3.8 billion years ago would likely exhibit a very shallow size-frequency distribution, making them recognizable only in dynamically less active regions. Notably, V-type asteroids in the central main belt could be compatible with a formation from a paleo-Eunomia family. Our findings provide new insights into the evolution and stability of asteroid families, with implications for the history and dynamics of the solar system. By exploring the limits of asteroid family recognition, this study sheds light on the potential for ancient asteroid families to serve as probes of the early solar system.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a computational method for solving extremal Steklov eigenvalue problems, with a focus on maximizing the k-th Steklov eigenvalue under a volume constraint. Contrary to other eigenvalue problems, our results suggest that optimal domains exhibit high structural symmetry. We conjecture that the maximizing domain is unique, up to dilations and rigid transformations, and possesses p-fold symmetry and an axis of symmetry. Furthermore, our findings indicate that the k-th Steklov eigenvalue has multiplicity 2 for even k and multiplicity 3 for odd k, providing new insights into the geometric properties of Steklov eigenvalue problems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: Enhancing Performance and Reliability in Cloud Data Centers through Proactive Load Balancing Strategy

Abstract:

The efficient allocation and management of resources in cloud data centers is crucial for ensuring high performance and reliability. One of the significant challenges in this context is the scheduling of reconfigurable virtual machines (VMs) and the integration of physical machines (PMs) with varying capabilities. Traditional load balancing strategies, such as the Longest Process Time First (LPT) approach, have been widely used but often fall short in achieving optimal load balance, particularly in scenarios involving VM migration. This paper proposes a novel paradigm, termed Prepartition, which proactively sets process-time bounds for each request on PMs and prepares for VM migration in advance to achieve predefined load balance objectives. By doing so, Prepartition reduces process time, instability, and achieves better load balance. Our evaluation, based on both trace-driven and synthetic simulations, demonstrates that Prepartition outperforms existing load balancing algorithms by 10%-20% in terms of average utilization, imbalance degree, makespan, and capacity-makespan for offline scheduling. Furthermore, we extend Prepartition to online load balancing (PrepartitionON) and show that it improves performance by 8%-20% compared to existing online scheduling algorithms, in terms of average CPU utilization, imbalance degree, makespan, and capacity-makespan. Theoretical and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, highlighting its potential to enhance the performance and reliability of cloud data centers. This research contributes to the development of efficient load balancing strategies, crucial for the optimal operation of cloud computing environments.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article introduces a novel family of simplicial complexes associated with arbitrary finite root systems and a nonnegative integer parameter. For a specific value of this parameter, the construction yields the generalized associahedra, equivalent to cluster complexes in finite-type cluster algebras. By computing face numbers and h-vectors of these complexes, we recover enumerative invariants previously defined by C.A. Athanasiadis, hinting at connections to algebraic combinatorics of finite Coxeter groups, root systems, and hyperplane arrangements. Furthermore, recurrences in the face numbers enable the development of combinatorial algorithms for determining Coxeter-theoretic invariants, such as the Coxeter number and exponents, using basic graph-theoretic concepts applied to the input Coxeter diagram. This recursive approach provides a new perspective on classical invariants, highlighting the interplay between geometric and combinatorial aspects of finite Coxeter groups.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines exclusive hadronic decays of ηc and η'b mesons into two-body final states, comprising a light pseudoscalar or vector meson and a D or D*s meson. We analyze these decays using QCD factorization and the heavy-quark expansion, considering unique mechanisms such as gluon coupling and intrinsic charm content. Our theoretical framework accounts for experimental branching fraction data, albeit with significant uncertainties. This research provides insight into flavor-singlet B-decay amplitudes, shedding light on the underlying dynamics of these processes and their phenomenological implications within the context of QCD factorization.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines zero modes of fluctuation around BPS vortices in a gauged nonlinear sigma-model's critical Higgs phase. For two species of BPS vortex solutions with quantized magnetic flux, four linearly independent vortex zero modes are identified. The existence of two species of moduli spaces of dimension four is locally demonstrated, shedding light on the topological defects in this phase.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the color gradients of 22 E/S0 galaxies in Abell 2218, revealing gradients of @xmath0 magnitudes per decade in radius in F450W-F606W and @xmath2 magnitudes per decade in radius in F606W-F814W. These gradients are consistent with a mild metal abundance gradient of @xmath3 dex per decade in radius, aligning with previous work on field and cluster galaxies at various redshifts. Notably, the gradient size is independent of luminosity and morphological type, suggesting a fundamental similarity in stellar population distributions among ellipticals and lenticular galaxy bulges. Our findings contradict simple models of monolithic collapse and hierarchical mergers, implying a more complex formation and evolution process for these galaxies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study revisits the longstanding debate surrounding the physics of unconventional superconductors, particularly cuprates with high transition temperatures. Despite 25 years of research, the origin of superconductivity in strongly correlated metallic systems remains unclear. Various theories have emerged, including Hertz-style critical spin fluctuations and holographic superconductivity. We propose that the dynamical pair susceptibility, measurable through the second-order Josephson effect, holds the key to resolving these discrepancies. By analyzing the frequency and temperature dependence of this quantity, we can distinguish between different pairing mechanisms. Our findings suggest that modern experimental techniques can be employed to construct a "pairing telescope," providing a direct insight into the origin of quantum critical superconductivity. This approach has the potential to settle the controversy and shed new light on the underlying physics of unconventional superconductors, paving the way for a deeper understanding of these complex systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the occurrence of gravitational lensing among high-redshift quasars discovered by the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). Using the Advanced Camera for Surveys on the Hubble Space Telescope, we conducted a snapshot imaging survey of four high-redshift SDSS quasars with redshifts of 4.0 and 6.30. Our observations aimed to detect gravitationally split lenses, which are expected to be present due to magnification bias. However, we found no evidence of lensed companions within 5 magnitudes and a separation larger than 1 arcsecond, or within 2.5 magnitudes and a separation larger than 0.1 arcseconds. The non-detection of strong lensing in these systems allows us to constrain the quasar luminosity function, yielding a slope of -3.5, assuming a break at M1450 = -26. This constraint has significant implications for our understanding of the ionizing background in the early universe, which is thought to be dominated by quasars. Furthermore, the lack of strong lensing in these quasars suggests that estimates of their central engine masses, derived using the Eddington argument, may be reliable, potentially challenging current models of black hole formation. Our results provide valuable insights into the properties of high-redshift quasars and their role in shaping the early universe.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the gamma-ray emission from the Vela pulsar using 62 months of Fermi-LAT data. We confirm significant pulsation in the 30-50 GeV energy range and extract the pulse profile using the Bayesian block algorithm. A likelihood ratio test comparing the pulse profile to the distribution of photons above 50 GeV reveals significant pulsation detection with a p-value of @xmath2 (@xmath3). Notably, pulsation is significantly detected above @xmath4 at @xmath5 GeV and above @xmath6 at @xmath7 GeV energy bands, marking the highest energy pulsation significantly detected by the LAT. Our findings are explored in the context of a non-stationary outer gap scenario for very high-energy emissions from the Vela pulsar. This research contributes to our understanding of pulsar emissions at extreme energies, shedding light on the underlying physical mechanisms driving these phenomena. The detection of pulsed emission above 50 GeV provides new insights into the Vela pulsar's behavior and has implications for future studies of high-energy astrophysical sources.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study explores double parton scatterings (DPS) in high-energy proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions to gain insight into multi-parton correlations. DPS probes the multi-parton structure differently in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions. However, interpreting experimental results from proton-nucleus collisions is complicated by interference terms, which are absent in proton-proton collisions. To mitigate this, we investigate φ-meson production, a reaction channel devoid of interference terms. Our analysis of φ-meson production in proton-nucleus collisions suggests that DPS events may be 3-4 times more frequent than in proton-proton collisions. The increased fraction of DPS events can provide valuable information on the significance of various correlation terms, offering a unique perspective on multi-parton correlations and the underlying structure of protons and nuclei.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the primary properties of dark matter haloes, as inferred from observations of rotation curves surrounding spiral and dwarf galaxies. With detailed rotation curves available for over a thousand galaxies, it has been revealed that these curves are not uniformly flat in the outer regions, instead exhibiting a rise for late-type galaxies and a decline for early-type galaxies. A key finding is that most luminous galaxies are not dominated by dark matter within their optical disks, whereas dark matter plays a predominant role in the visible regions of dwarf and low surface brightness (LSB) galaxies. The three-dimensional shape of haloes is investigated through various methods, including polar rings, flaring of HI planes, and X-ray isophotes. While the extent of haloes remains uncertain, tentative estimates have been made. Notably, the dark matter appears to be coupled to the gas in spirals and dwarfs, suggesting that dark baryons may be the primary contributor to rotation curves. Theoretical frameworks, such as Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND), which aim to replace non-baryonic dark matter with alternative dynamical or gravitational laws, must account for the presence of dark baryons and their distinct spatial distribution.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We analyze pseudointegrable EBA billiards, observing a transition from semi-Poissonian to Poissonian statistics as resonances increase. This agrees with the notion that a classical particle is unaffected by point perturbations, contradicting earlier results (P.EBA, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64, 1855 (1990)). Our findings shed new light on singular statistics, utilizing Ewald's method and renormalized Green functions to inform the Weyl formula.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article proposes a novel nonparametric approach for estimating univariate regression functions of bounded variation. By leveraging the Jordan decomposition, which represents a function of bounded variation as the sum of a non-decreasing and a non-increasing function, we develop an iterative algorithm called Iterative Isotonic Regression (IIR). The IIR algorithm combines the backfitting algorithm for estimating additive functions with isotonic regression for estimating monotone functions. Our primary technical contribution is establishing the consistency of the proposed estimator as the number of iterations increases appropriately with the sample size. The proof relies on two auxiliary results of independent interest: a generalized consistency property of isotonic regression for non-monotone regression functions and a connection between the backfitting algorithm and von Neumann's algorithm in convex analysis. Theoretical guarantees are provided, and the algorithm's performance is demonstrated through mathematical analysis. This work contributes to the field of nonparametric statistics, isotonic regression, and additive models, with applications in metric projection onto convex cones. The proposed method offers a new tool for estimating complex regression functions, and its consistency properties make it a reliable choice for practitioners.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Abstract:

The study of ultra-relativistic nuclear collisions has led to the development of a paradigm wherein the high energy nuclear wavefunctions and initial stages of the collision are dominated by classical fields. However, the inclusion of quantum fluctuations around these classical background fields is crucial for a more accurate description. We focus on two classes of quantum fluctuations: those contributing to the energy evolution of multi-parton correlators in the nuclear wavefunctions, and unstable secular terms that grow rapidly with proper time after the collision. By resumming the leading contributions of these secular terms to all loop orders, we obtain expressions for final state observables in terms of the spectrum of fluctuations on the initial proper time surface.

In the context of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), we compute the essential elements of this fluctuation spectrum, specifically the small quantum fluctuation modes in the classical background field. Our derivation provides the necessary ingredients to compute inclusive quantities in heavy ion collisions at early times, including all-order leading logs, strong multiple scattering contributions, and leading secular terms. Furthermore, our results have important implications for the study of early hydrodynamic flow, sphaleron transitions off-equilibrium, and "jet quenching" in strong color fields at early times. A numerical analysis of the energy-momentum tensor in a scalar theory analogous to QCD suggests the possibility of early hydrodynamic flow, and we anticipate similar behavior in QCD. Our work provides a foundation for a more comprehensive understanding of ultra-relativistic nuclear collisions and the underlying dynamics of quantum fields in these extreme environments.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents simulation results on the two-dimensional Ising ferromagnet under the influence of a special type of noise. The noise spectrum follows a power law, where the probability of flipping randomly selected spins at each time step is a variable parameter. This setup aims to mimic the self-organized criticality that can arise from the complex interactions within an environment. Our simulations successfully reproduce a phase transition similar to that observed when the noise amplitude is constant. Notably, above a certain threshold of noise amplitude, the magnetization tends to zero, whereas below this threshold, it remains constant after an initial relaxation period. Furthermore, short-range spin-spin correlations preserve information about the initial spin orientation to some extent. The distribution of times between spin flips is found to be exponential. These findings contribute to the understanding of complex systems and are discussed in the context of modeling social systems, where the introduction of power-law noise can simulate the disturbance of majority rule. The results provide insight into the behavior of systems under the influence of random fluctuations and have implications for the study of phase transitions in various domains.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines a one-dimensional continuum gas consisting of point-like positive and negative unit charges interacting through a logarithmic potential. By mapping this system onto a two-dimensional boundary sine-Gordon field theory with zero bulk mass, we obtain a comprehensive understanding of the thermodynamics of the log-gas across its entire stability range of inverse temperatures. Notably, an exact formula is derived for the excess chemical potential of a foreign particle with arbitrary charge introduced into the log-gas. The validity of our results is verified through a small-fugacity expansion and at the collapse point. Furthermore, the possibility of extending our analysis beyond the collapse temperature is discussed, highlighting the potential for further exploration. This research contributes to the understanding of two-component plasmas, logarithmic interactions, and the application of the boundary sine-Gordon model, with implications for the study of integrable systems and their thermodynamic properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the stability of cold fronts in galaxy clusters, recently observed by Chandra, with respect to Kelvin-Helmholtz instability. The cold fronts are thought to form when hot gas flows over a colder, gravitationally bound gas cloud. Our analysis reveals that an intrinsic interface width of a few percent of the curvature radius significantly suppresses perturbation growth. Focusing on the well-studied Abell 3667 cluster, we find that current observational data on the front's width and extent can be explained without invoking dynamically important magnetic fields. This research provides new insights into the dynamics of cold fronts in galaxy clusters, shedding light on their formation and evolution. The results have implications for our understanding of cluster physics and the role of magnetic fields in these systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We extend the applicability of Density Functional Theory for Superconductors (SCDFT) to systems with significant particle-hole asymmetry by introducing a new exchange-correlation kernel. This kernel is numerically stable and finite in the low-temperature limit. Analytical and numerical solutions of the gap equation for model systems reveal a systematic decrease in transition temperature due to the asymmetric component of electronic density of states, previously unaccounted for. Notably, this decrease can be substantial, reaching several tens of percent in certain cases, highlighting the importance of considering particle-hole asymmetry in SCDFT calculations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the translational invariance of the relative-locality framework, extending previous findings to processes involving multiple interactions. We provide an explicit example of boundary conditions that ensure translational invariance, even in cases where interactions are causally connected. Using a momentum-space geometry inspired by the Poincaré group, with a de Sitter metric and non-metric connection, we illustrate the relativistic description of distant observers. Our results show that simultaneously emitted massless particles do not reach a distant detector simultaneously, consistent with previous findings on non-metric connections. We also demonstrate that the theory admits a free-particle limit, reproducing previous relative-locality results. Notably, the torsion of the Poincaré connection introduces a dependence of detection time on interaction properties at the source, which, although small, may be observable. This work provides new insights into the relative-locality framework, highlighting the importance of considering multiple interactions and non-metric connections in the description of particle physics phenomena. Our findings have implications for the understanding of spacetime and gravity, and may lead to new experimental tests of the relative-locality framework.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the viscosity and self-diffusion constant of mesoscale hydrodynamic methods, including MPC and DPD, with and without angular-momentum conservation. Analytical results are derived for ideal-gas fluids and compared to simulation data, yielding a general viscosity form for MPC variants. Theoretical and simulation results show excellent agreement, validating the derived expressions for these key transport properties in particle-based methods.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a novel collective model formalism that effectively describes the strong parity shift observed in the low-lying spectra of nuclei exhibiting octupole deformations, along with the fine rotational band structure that emerges at higher angular momenta. By solving the Schrödinger equation for oscillations of the reflection asymmetric (octupole) shape between two opposite orientations in an angular momentum-dependent double-well potential, the parity effect is successfully reproduced. Additionally, a collective quadrupole-octupole rotation Hamiltonian is employed to generate the rotational structure. The proposed model scheme demonstrates excellent agreement with the complex beat staggering patterns observed in the octupole bands of light actinide nuclei. It provides a comprehensive understanding of the angular momentum evolution of octupole spectra, attributing it to the interplay between the octupole shape oscillation (parity shift) mode and the stable quadrupole-octupole rotation mode. The findings of this study offer valuable insights into the nuclear structure of quadrupole-octupole deformed nuclei, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms that govern their behavior. The model's ability to reproduce the intricate patterns observed in experimental data underscores its potential as a powerful tool for understanding the complex phenomena associated with octupole deformations in nuclei.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the emergence of singularities in Kohn variational calculations for low-energy elastic scattering. Our analysis reveals that the implementation of the Kohn variational principle, when paired with a sufficiently accurate trial wavefunction, inherently produces non-spurious singularities. To mitigate anomalous behavior in scattering phase shift calculations, we propose two optimization approaches for a free parameter in the trial wavefunction. The first approach leverages the existence of these singularities, while the second involves a conventional optimization of the generalized Kohn method. Our results show close agreement between the two optimization schemes, with both yielding outcomes equivalent to those obtained using the complex Kohn method. Notably, the first optimization scheme offers the advantage of not requiring an explicit solution to the Kohn equations. However, we also identify anomalies that cannot be avoided using either scheme, highlighting the importance of considering variations in nonlinear parameters of the trial function to circumvent such issues.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study investigates the impact of localized contact adhesion between grains on the maximum static critical angle of a dry sand pile. By introducing dimer grains, composed of two rigidly bonded spheres, into a mixture with spherical monomer grains, we create a system with strong, localized adhesion between particles. Our results show that increasing the proportion of dimer particles from 0 to 1 raises the critical angle from 0.45 to 1.1, while decreasing the grain packing fraction from 0.58 to 0.52. The enhanced stability of dimers on the surface is attributed to the increased critical angle, allowing for a more efficient accommodation of monomers in stable surface traps. A comprehensive characterization and geometrical stability analysis of surface traps yields a strong quantitative agreement between experimental and theoretical findings across a wide range of dimer concentrations, without requiring fitting parameters.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the interaction between an expanding pair-electromagnetic pulse (PEM pulse) and a shell of baryonic matter surrounding a black hole with an electromagnetic structure (EMBH). The analysis focuses on selected values of baryonic mass at distances well outside the dyadosphere of an EMBH, where the dyadosphere is considered in the context of a Reissner-Nordstrom geometry. The interaction is modeled using both a simplified constant-thickness approximation and a full general relativistic hydrodynamical approach. The constant-thickness approximation is validated for the presence of baryonic matter, demonstrating excellent agreement with general relativistic computations for baryonic shell mass-energies less than 1% of the dyadosphere's total energy. However, the approximation breaks down for larger baryonic shell masses, which are less relevant to observed gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Numerical computations using the slab model for PEM pulses reveal the relativistic evolution of the pulse colliding with a baryonic shell, as well as the expected emission energy and observed temperature of associated GRBs for a given EMBH mass. The results are presented for baryonic mass-energies ranging from $10^{18}$ to $10^{22}$ erg, which is a fraction of the total energy of the dyadosphere. These findings provide insights into the complex dynamics of PEM pulses interacting with baryonic matter in the vicinity of EMBHs, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms of GRBs. The study's results have implications for our understanding of these cosmic events and the role of EMBHs in their production.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents an analysis of intrinsic ellipticities in a sample of 28 face-on spiral disks. By combining velocity fields and multi-band images, we estimate kinematic and photometric inclination and position angles. Our results indicate a log-normal distribution of ellipticities, ranging from circular to highly elliptical. A tight Tully-Fisher relation is constructed for the face-on sample, allowing us to assess the impact of disk ellipticity on the observed scatter. Our findings provide insights into the structural properties of spiral galaxies and the factors influencing the Tully-Fisher relation, with implications for galaxy evolution and cosmology.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the spin transport properties of acene series molecules using density functional theory and non-equilibrium Green's function approach. Our findings indicate that short acenes exhibit non-magnetic behavior, whereas molecules with more than nine acene rings display a spin-polarized ground state. In the gas phase, these molecules have a singlet total spin configuration due to antiferromagnetic coupling of unpaired electrons. However, asymmetric attachment to Au electrodes via thiol linkers lifts orbital degeneracy, resulting in a fractional magnetic moment. The Au/acene/Au system can function as an efficient spin-filter, offering promising applications in organic spintronics. Our research provides valuable insights into the spin transport properties of acene molecules, highlighting their potential for innovative spin-based devices. Theoretical modeling of these systems can inform the design of future organic spintronics technologies.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines ISO phot data from intermediate-redshift steep-spectrum 3CR radio galaxies and quasars to test consistency with the radio-loud AGN unification scheme. Supplemental submillimeter and centimeter radio data are also analyzed to assess beamed nonthermal radiation.
