The generalized fast mode exhibits distinct acoustic effects in parallel and perpendicular directions to the ambient magnetic field, and the magneto-sonic wave suppresses the firehose instability in the fast-mode instability. Our findings are supported by graphic illustrations, and threshold conditions for various instabilities are obtained, providing a deeper understanding of the complex behavior of homogeneous collisionless magnetized plasmas. This work contributes to the advancement of plasma physics, with implications for the study of space and astrophysical plasmas.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the implications of current precision electroweak data, Z' searches, and dark matter constraints on an extended Standard Model featuring an additional massive gauge boson and a "hidden valley" sector with a confining gauge group. We derive a lower mass limit of 3 GeV for the Z' boson from direct searches and precision tests. The model includes a pseudoscalar dark matter candidate, and we find that dark matter constraints impose an upper bound on the Z' mass of approximately 5 TeV. A TeV-scale mass is required for the hidden valley states, and the Sommerfeld factor significantly suppresses the allowed parameter space for p-wave dark matter annihilation. Our analysis provides new insights into the interplay between electroweak precision data, Z' searches, and dark matter constraints, shedding light on the viable parameter space of this extended Standard Model. The results have important implications for model-building and experimental searches.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the spectral and temporal properties of X-ray flares emitted by several Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs). A sample of GRBs with large amplitude variations and multiple rebrightenings in their X-ray light curves is analyzed. The origin of these fluctuations is investigated to distinguish between refreshed shocks and late internal shocks. Time-resolved spectral analysis of select bursts supports the presence of a long-lived central engine, where rebrightenings are consistent with energy injection in refreshed shocks. This occurs when slower shells, generated during the prompt phase, catch up with the afterglow shock at later times, providing diagnostic insights into the underlying mechanisms driving these complex phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the applicability of a novel X-ray scaling method for estimating the mass of supermassive black holes in low-accreting active galactic nuclei (AGN). Our previous work demonstrated the reliability of this method for moderately to highly accreting black holes. However, for low-accreting AGN, the underlying assumption that the photon index correlates with accretion rate breaks down. Using a control sample with high-quality X-ray data and dynamically measured masses, we find that the X-ray scaling method is not applicable in these cases. Nevertheless, an inverse correlation observed in low-accreting black holes can be utilized to constrain masses within a factor of 3 of dynamically determined values. We propose a simple recipe using X-ray spectral data to estimate black hole masses, providing a sanity check for indirect optical methods. This work contributes to the understanding of black hole mass estimation in low-accreting AGN, with implications for active galaxy research.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study proposes a novel approach to observe ultra-high energy astrophysical neutrinos and identify their flavors in future neutrino telescopes. The flavor ratio of astrophysical neutrinos detected on Earth is influenced by both the initial flavor ratio at the source and flavor transitions during propagation. A model-independent parametrization is used to classify flavor transition mechanisms. A new parameter, @xmath0, is introduced to directly probe flavor transitions without assuming @xmath1 symmetry. Several flavor transition models are tested using this parametrization, and observational constraints on flavor transition mechanisms are discussed. This research aims to advance our understanding of astrophysical neutrino flavor transitions, with implications for neutrino telescopes and cosmology, categorized under PACS numbers 95.85.ry, 14.60.pq, and 95.55.vj.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a general variational framework for modeling finite temperature effects in superfluid systems, with a focus on complex scenarios such as the mixed neutron superfluid/proton superconductor expected in neutron star cores. By treating excitations as a massless "entropy" fluid, we demonstrate the formal equivalence of our approach to the traditional two-fluid model for superfluid helium, highlighting the role of entropy entrainment in encoding the normal fluid density. The superfluid constraint of irrotationality is shown to reduce the number of dissipation coefficients, providing insight into the more general problem of vortex presence and the incorporation of mutual friction forces. Our hydrodynamic formalism, applicable to single superfluid condensates, can be readily extended to more complex situations, including colour-flavour locked quark superconductors potentially present in deep neutron star cores. The developed framework offers a foundation for understanding finite temperature effects in superfluid systems, with implications for the study of neutron star physics and other extreme environments. By exploring dissipative mechanisms and finite temperature effects, this work aims to contribute to a deeper understanding of the complex dynamics governing superfluid systems, ultimately informing the development of more accurate models for these phenomena.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
The internal structure of neutrons remains poorly understood compared to protons, primarily due to the lack of free neutron targets. Typically, neutron information is extracted from data on nuclear targets like deuterium, which requires corrections for nuclear binding and nucleon off-shell effects. These corrections are model-dependent and plagued by significant uncertainties, particularly for large values of the Bjorken scaling variable x. As a result, the same data can yield different conclusions, such as the behavior of the d-quark distribution in the proton at large x.

The Barely Off-shell Nucleon Structure (BONUS) experiment at Jefferson Lab aimed to address this limitation by measuring the inelastic electron-deuteron scattering cross section, tagging spectator protons in coincidence with scattered electrons. This novel approach substantially reduces nuclear binding uncertainties, enabling the first nearly model-independent extraction of the neutron structure function F2n in the resonance and deep-inelastic regions.

The experiment employed a custom-built compact radial time projection chamber to detect protons with momenta between 70 and 150 MeV/c and over a nearly 4π angular range. To extract the free-neutron structure function F2n, spectator protons at backward angles and with momenta below 100 MeV/c were selected, ensuring that the scattering occurred on a nearly free neutron. Scattered electrons were detected using Jefferson Lab's CLAS spectrometer, with data collected at beam energies near 2, 4, and 5 GeV.

The extracted neutron structure function F2n and its ratio to the inclusive deuteron structure function F2d are presented in both the resonance and deep-inelastic regions, covering a range of kinematic variables. The dependence of the semi-inclusive cross section on spectator proton momentum and angle is investigated, and tests of the spectator mechanism are performed for different kinematics. The results provide new insights into neutron resonance excitations, quark-hadron duality in the neutron, and binding effects, including the nuclear EMC effect. This study offers a unique opportunity to develop more precise parametrizations of structure functions and investigate the asymptotic behavior of the d-quark distribution at large x, ultimately enhancing our understanding of neutron structure and its role in nuclear physics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the nonlinear theory of dust-acoustic waves (DAWs) in an unmagnetized dusty negative-ion plasma, considering the extreme scenario where free electrons are absent. The dynamics of cold, massive charged dusts are modeled using fluid equations, while the two species of ions (positive and negative) are described by kinetic Vlasov equations. A Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation with Landau damping is derived to govern the behavior of weakly nonlinear and weakly dispersive DAWs. The results indicate that, for typical laboratory and space plasmas, Landau damping and nonlinear effects dominate over finite Debye length effects, rendering the KdV soliton theory inapplicable to DAWs in dusty pair-ion plasmas. The study examines the properties of linear phase velocity, solitary wave amplitudes, and Landau damping rate, taking into account the effects of the positive ion to dust density ratio, as well as the ratios of positive to negative ion temperatures and masses. The findings provide insight into the behavior of DAWs in extreme plasma conditions, highlighting the significance of Landau damping and nonlinear effects in shaping the dynamics of these waves.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text:
Title: Evaluating the Preservation of Information in Dimensionality Reduction Techniques for Complex Networks

Abstract:
The increasing complexity of large networks has led to the development of various dimensionality reduction techniques, including network motif analysis, graph spectra, and spectral sparsification methods. However, the extent to which these techniques preserve or lose information remains unclear. This study introduces a framework based on algorithmic information theory to quantify the preservation of information in over 20 biological and artificial networks. Our results show that spectral sparsification is highly sensitive to edge deletion, leading to significant inconsistencies, while graph spectral methods capture algebraic information but lose most of the original network's information content. In contrast, network motif analysis excels at preserving the relative algorithmic information content of a network, enabling the recovery of essential properties across different networks. This methodology provides a rigorous framework for assessing and comparing dimensionality reduction methods, facilitating the evaluation of their capabilities. By applying algorithmic information theory, we validate the effectiveness of network motif analysis in preserving information and demonstrate the potential of this approach in identifying and characterizing complex networks. Our findings have implications for the development and application of dimensionality reduction techniques in various fields, including biology, social science, and computer science. Keywords: dimensionality reduction techniques, Kolmogorov complexity, network, graph spectra, graph motifs, graph sparsification.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the problem of quickest detection in a distributed sensor system, where multiple sensors receive sequential observations from the environment and employ cumulative sum (CUSUM) strategies. The sensors communicate with a central fusion center using one-shot schemes, where each sensor transmits a single message after which a detection decision is made. We consider an asynchronous communication scenario, where the fusion center declares an alarm upon receiving the first communication. Assuming independent observations at each sensor and random signal appearance times, we analyze the performance of one-shot schemes in comparison to centralized detection. Our results show that one-shot schemes do not incur a performance loss in an extended Lorden min-max sense, as the minimum of multiple CUSUMs is asymptotically optimal when the mean time between false alarms increases without bound. This finding has significant implications for distributed inference and decision-making in multisensor systems, highlighting the effectiveness of one-shot schemes in quickest detection applications.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study proposes a time-dependent phenomenological model to investigate @xmath0-CDM cosmology. A time-dependent equation of state parameter is derived, enabling a sign flip in the deceleration parameter. Calculated universe age matches observational data for specific parameter values, validating the model's effectiveness in describing cosmic evolution accurately.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study demonstrates the feasibility of realizing a Photonic Floquet Topological Insulator (PFTI) in an atomic ensemble. By interfering three coupling fields, a periodic refractive index structure with a honeycomb profile is formed, which can be modulated by adjusting the frequency detunings and intensities of the coupling fields. This structure gives rise to Dirac cones in momentum space, whose appearance is influenced by the honeycomb lattice's helical ordering. When the lattice sites are ordered, gaps open at the Dirac points, yielding a PFTI in the atomic vapor. The edge states of the PFTI can confine an obliquely incident beam, allowing it to propagate along the lattice's zigzag edge without scattering. Notably, the third-order nonlinear susceptibility can shut down the Dirac cones and PFTI formation, while the fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility can reopen them, offering a unique means of controlling topological phenomena in photonic systems.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article addresses estimating the effective dimension-reduction subspace in multi-index regression models. A new procedure for recovering subspace directions is proposed, proven to be consistent under mild assumptions. Numerical simulations demonstrate the algorithm's empirical behavior, offering insights into its effectiveness in dimension reduction with additive noise and deterministic design, particularly when structural dimension is limited.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the asymptotic behavior of entropy in flexible chains comprising multiple monomers placed on stripes, utilizing the transfer matrix approach. Focusing on high-density regimes, we analyze the entropy's dependence on monomer density and stripe width, building upon recent analytical work on dimers. Our calculations yield the asymptotic entropy for chains with numerous monomers, as well as the special case of polymers with a large number of monomers. The results exhibit regular behavior, consistent with analytical findings for dimers. Furthermore, our transfer matrix calculations validate the mean-field expression for entropy in the low-density limit, demonstrating the accuracy of our approach. These findings provide valuable insights into the thermodynamic properties of flexible chains in confined geometries, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms governing their behavior.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article examines the nonstationary circuit QED setup, where multiple qubits interact with a single electromagnetic field mode in a resonator. We apply harmonic time modulation to the atomic transition frequency or atom-field coupling strength and derive unitary dynamics up to the second order. Our analysis reveals that resonant phenomena occurring at modulation frequencies equal to the cavity frequency also occur at halved frequencies, albeit with significantly reduced transition rates. The effectiveness of modulating the coupling strength is also diminished at these lower frequencies. We explicitly calculate transition rates and discuss the potential applications of second-order resonances in dynamical Casimir effect-related phenomena, providing new insights into the behavior of nonstationary circuit QED systems. The results have implications for quantum information processing and quantum optics.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents pioneering worldline analytical and numerical results on the intricate relationship between geometric and thermal dependencies of the Casimir effect. Notably, our findings indicate that the temperature dependence of the Casimir force is substantially more pronounced in open geometries, such as perpendicular plates, compared to closed geometries like parallel plates. For surface separations relevant to experimental settings, thermal corrections in the perpendicular plates configuration exhibit a stronger parameter dependence, surpassing those in parallel plates by an order of magnitude at room temperature. This disparity stems from the gapless spectrum of open geometries, facilitating thermal excitation of low-lying modes at low temperatures, whereas closed geometries have a gapped spectrum, inhibiting such excitations.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study examines the impact of longitudinal structuring on fast kink modes in coronal loops. By deriving analytical dispersion relations and mode profiles for the magnetic field perturbation, we investigate deviations from homogeneous loop frequencies and mode profiles as a function of density scale height. The effects of fixed and variable column masses, negative scale heights, and density contrasts are analyzed. Our results provide tools to estimate solar photospheric parameters, including frequency ratios, mode profiles, and antinode shifts from homogeneous loop sine profiles. We expand relevant factors up to the second order in the stratification parameter, verifying that first overtone antinode shifts are within the millimeter range, accessible to current observational resolutions. This research offers new insights into coronal loop dynamics and the potential to infer solar photospheric properties through the analysis of fast kink modes. The findings have implications for our understanding of the solar corona and its underlying structures.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the possibility that dark matter halos can be described by the Fermi-Dirac distribution at finite temperature, a scenario that arises if dark matter is composed of massive neutrinos in statistical equilibrium or if it can be treated as a collisionless gas undergoing violent relaxation. To rigorously analyze the stability of such systems, we employ the fermionic King model, focusing on the non-degenerate limit that yields the classical King model. Originally developed to describe globular clusters, we propose extending this model to large dark matter halos where quantum effects are negligible. Our analysis reveals that equilibrium states exist only above specific critical energy and temperature thresholds in the microcanonical and canonical ensembles, respectively. Below these thresholds, the system undergoes either a gravothermal catastrophe or an isothermal collapse. We compute density, circular velocity, and velocity dispersion profiles, comparing the classical King model's predictions with observations of large dark matter halos. The model accurately describes these halos near the point of marginal microcanonical stability, where it generates a density profile akin to the modified Hubble profile, featuring a flat core and a large-distance decay similar to the observed Burkert profile. Our findings suggest that statistical mechanics provides a viable framework for understanding dark matter halos, with discrepancies attributable to incomplete relaxation, analogous to stellar systems. This work supports the notion that dark matter halos can be described by the Fermi-Dirac distribution at finite temperature, offering new insights into the nature and behavior of dark matter. By applying the principles of statistical mechanics to dark matter, we may uncover a more comprehensive understanding of the universe's large-scale structure and the role of dark matter within it.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article explores the properties of @xmath0-optimal fields, a subclass of @xmath0-minimal fields that encompasses all known examples. By utilizing methods rooted in Denef's work, we establish a cell decomposition theorem, which in turn yields the existence of definable Skolem functions and strong @xmath0-minimality. We then focus on strongly @xmath0-minimal fields that satisfy the extreme value property, a characteristic present in fields elementarily equivalent to a @xmath0-adic one. For such fields, we demonstrate that definable subsets with fibers over the field that are inverse images of subsets of the value group are semi-algebraic. Combining these results, we derive a preparation theorem for definable functions, leading to the conclusion that infinite definable sets over these fields are in definable bijection if and only if they have the same dimension, shedding light on the structural properties of these fields.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of simultaneous radio and X-ray observations of the atoll-type X-ray binary 4U 1728-34, conducted in 2000 and 2001. Our findings reveal a significant correlation between radio emission and X-ray states, with the strongest and most variable radio emission occurring during transitions between hard and softer X-ray states. A positive correlation is observed between the radio flux density at 8.46 GHz and the 2-10 keV X-ray flux, as well as between radio flux density and X-ray timing features. These correlations provide evidence for a disc-jet coupling in atoll-type X-ray binaries, a phenomenon previously observed in black hole binaries. Furthermore, our results confirm that accreting neutron stars are less radio-loud than black holes, with a significant difference in radio emission factors. This research contributes to our understanding of the complex relationships between accretion, jet formation, and radiation mechanisms in neutron star X-ray binaries, and has implications for the study of compact objects and their environs. The observations and analysis presented here offer new insights into the physics of atoll-type X-ray binaries and their role in the broader context of astrophysical research.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: This article presents a comprehensive study of double parton distributions (DPDFs), including both conventional and parton splitting contributions, for various two-parton combinations. Our calculations reveal that the conventional and splitting DPDFs exhibit similar shapes in the momentum fractions $x_0$ and $x_1$. We provide the first quantitative evaluation of the single-ladder-splitting contribution to double parton scattering (DPS) production of two S- or P-wave quarkonia, two Higgs bosons, and $W^+W^-$. The ratio of single-ladder-splitting to conventional contributions is investigated as a function of center-of-mass energy, mass of the produced system, and other kinematical variables. Using a simple model for the conventional two-parton distribution, we find that the single-ladder-splitting contribution is comparable to the conventional contribution. This implies that phenomenological analyses of DPS processes must be revised to include the single-ladder-splitting contributions. While the differential distributions in rapidity and transverse momenta are similar for conventional and single-ladder-splitting DPS processes, making experimental separation challenging, the existence of both components leads to an energy and process dependence of the empirical parameter $\sigma_{\text{eff}}$. Our results have significant implications for the understanding of DPS processes and highlight the need for a more comprehensive treatment of DPDFs in phenomenological analyses.
label: llama-3.3-70b

text: We present sensitive dual-frequency (1.7 and 5 GHz) European VLBI Network (EVN) observations of the central regions of nine Seyfert galaxies, which are among the faintest and least luminous members of a complete sample of nearby (≈ 20 Mpc) low-luminosity Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN). Our high-resolution observations reveal radio emission on milliarcsecond scales in the nuclei of four galaxies, while upper limits of ≈ 1 mJy are set for the remaining five sources. Notably, three sources (NGC 3227, NGC 3982, and NGC 4138) exhibit radio emission at both frequencies, resolved into two or more components. We characterize the structural and spectral properties of these features, finding high brightness temperatures (≈ 10^4-10^5 K) and flat/intermediate spectral indices (α ≈ -0.5 to 0.5) in the primary components, accompanied by secondary steep-spectrum extended components. These findings suggest non-thermal emission from jets or outflows as the most plausible explanation. Additionally, a faint feature detected in NGC 4477 at 5 GHz may originate from the hot corona, given the unrealistic magnetic field values required by synchrotron self-absorption. Our results provide new insights into the nature of these low-luminosity AGN, while the non-detections highlight the need for further observations on intermediate scales to elucidate their properties.
label: llama-3.3-70b
